meta.title: Stormlight Recall Atlas
meta.subtitle: Spoiler-safe through the final epilogue of Rhythm of War
meta.scope: The Way of Kings → Words of Radiance → Edgedancer → Oathbringer → Dawnshard → Rhythm of War, plus Cosmere connections published/revealed by the Rhythm of War era.
meta.completeness: Comprehensive named-reference edition focused on recurring, plot-relevant, factional, magical, historical, and cross-Cosmere entities. It is not a page-level concordance and excludes unnamed background figures. The original Oathbringer build indexed numbered chapters but not every interlude; the extension explicitly indexes all Rhythm of War interludes and corrects the scope wording.
meta.chapterMethod: Every numbered chapter in all six included works is navigable. Dawnshard prologue/epilogue and all Rhythm of War interludes are indexed; earlier-book interludes remain represented through timeline/entity anchors rather than as separate chapter-grid records. Expanded entries are curated major anchors and arc context rather than scene-by-scene retellings.
meta.mapMethod: Original schematic map, intentionally not to scale and not copied from official artwork.
meta.spoilerRule: No fact whose first textual reveal occurs after the Rhythm of War epilogue (“Dirty Tricks”) is used as an answer. Later-book terminology and retcons are intentionally excluded.
meta.copyright: Fan-made study aid. Names and setting belong to Brandon Sanderson / Dragonsteel and their publishing partners. No book text or official map artwork is reproduced.

books.title: The Way of Kings
books.chronology: Primary story: late 1173; several flashback layers
books.summary: Kaladin is reduced from soldier to slave and then rebuilds Bridge Four; Dalinar follows visions while Alethi politics fracture; Shallan seeks Jasnah as both ward and would-be thief; Szeth’s assassination campaign expands.
books.why: Start here. Establishes Roshar, the Shattered Plains, Surgebinding’s return, and the major viewpoint lines.
books.chapters: Prelude, Prologue, 75 numbered chapters, interludes, epilogue

books.title: Words of Radiance
books.chronology: Immediately after TWoK; roughly 71 primary-story days
books.summary: The viewpoint lines converge on the Shattered Plains; Shallan develops as a Lightweaver and enters Ghostblood politics; Kaladin’s oaths are tested; the listeners summon the Everstorm; Urithiru is rediscovered.
books.why: Continues directly from TWoK and changes the political and magical status quo.

books.title: Edgedancer
books.summary: Lift leaves Azimir for Yeddaw, follows Nale’s pursuit of budding Radiants, encounters the Stump and the Sleepless, and reaches a new understanding of what it means to remember people others overlook.
books.why: Read before Oathbringer. It explains Lift, Nale, Szeth’s new circumstances, and the changing Skybreaker mission.
books.chapters: WoR interlude reused as prologue, then 20 chapters

books.title: Oathbringer
books.chronology: Roshar year 1174, approximately day 4 through day 100
books.summary: Dalinar builds a coalition while recovering the truth of his past; Urithiru, Kholinar, Shadesmar, and Thaylen Field become linked fronts; old identities and loyalties fracture; the Desolation becomes an open world war.
books.why: Core novel 3. Its ending is no longer the atlas ceiling; continue with Dawnshard before Rhythm of War.

books.title: Dawnshard
books.chronology: About three months after Oathbringer; before Rhythm of War
books.summary: Rysn leads the Wandersail expedition to Akinah while Lopen and Huio accompany the mission as Windrunners. The expedition discovers the Sleepless defenses, ancient caches, and a Dawnshard whose Command bonds to Rysn.
books.why: Read after Oathbringer and before Rhythm of War. It explains Rysn’s changed status, Aimia, Cord’s equipment, Chiri-Chiri’s development, and Lopen/Huio’s oaths.

books.title: Rhythm of War
books.chronology: Roughly one year after the Battle of Thaylen Field; Roshar year 1175
books.summary: The war shifts toward technology, spren politics, and control of Urithiru. Navani and Raboniel transform the science of Light; Kaladin resists the occupation of the tower; Adolin and Shallan enter Lasting Integrity; Venli confronts responsibility for her people; the conflict with Odium changes at its source.
books.why: Current hard spoiler ceiling. This is Stormlight book 4 and the endpoint of this atlas.

cosmereBooks.title: Elantris
cosmereBooks.connection: Introduces Sel and one traveler later seen on Roshar. The Roshar cameo is intentionally subtle.

cosmereBooks.title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
cosmereBooks.connection: Introduces Scadrial and metal-based Investiture; one later Roshar visitor originated here.

cosmereBooks.title: The Well of Ascension
cosmereBooks.connection: Part of the Scadrian background relevant to broader Cosmere mechanics, not required for Oathbringer.

cosmereBooks.title: The Hero of Ages
cosmereBooks.connection: Completes Era 1 and makes Shards and planetary Investiture easier to recognize.

cosmereBooks.title: Warbreaker
cosmereBooks.connection: The most useful non-Stormlight companion before Oathbringer: explains the origins of Zahel, Azure, Nightblood, Breath, and Awakening.

cosmereBooks.title: The Alloy of Law
cosmereBooks.connection: Later Scadrial; useful only for broad Cosmere context at this spoiler boundary.

cosmereBooks.title: The Emperor’s Soul
cosmereBooks.connection: Compact explanation of Identity, Connection, and a different expression of Investiture.

cosmereBooks.title: The Eleventh Metal
cosmereBooks.connection: Prequel story; no direct Oathbringer requirement.

cosmereBooks.title: The Hope of Elantris
cosmereBooks.connection: Side story on Sel; no direct Oathbringer requirement.

cosmereBooks.title: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell
cosmereBooks.connection: Shows another world’s Cognitive Shadows and Investiture rules.

cosmereBooks.title: Allomancer Jak and the Pits of Eltania
cosmereBooks.connection: Scadrian side story; no direct Stormlight dependency.

cosmereBooks.title: Sixth of the Dusk
cosmereBooks.connection: Shows a distant Cosmere culture and invested ecology; not needed for Oathbringer.

cosmereBooks.title: Shadows of Self
cosmereBooks.connection: Broader Shard and magic context; not directly tied to Oathbringer’s plot.

cosmereBooks.title: The Bands of Mourning
cosmereBooks.connection: Expands Scadrian Identity and Connection mechanics, useful for theory but not required.

cosmereBooks.title: Mistborn: Secret History
cosmereBooks.connection: Makes the Cognitive Realm and Shardic conflict more explicit. Contains major Mistborn spoilers.

cosmereBooks.title: White Sand, Volume 1
cosmereBooks.connection: Introduces Taldain; white sand later acts as a practical Investiture indicator in Oathbringer.

cosmereBooks.title: Arcanum Unbounded
cosmereBooks.connection: Contains Edgedancer, planetary-system essays, and several earlier short works. The essays supply cross-Cosmere framing available before Oathbringer.

cosmereBooks.title: White Sand, Volume 2
cosmereBooks.connection: Continues Taldain background. White sand remains a useful Investiture detector in Rhythm of War-era research.

cosmereBooks.title: White Sand, Volume 3
cosmereBooks.connection: Completes the original graphic-novel run available before Rhythm of War; relevant mainly to Taldain and white-sand Investiture detection.

cosmereBooks.title: Dawnshard
cosmereBooks.connection: Stormlight 3.5. Read between Oathbringer and Rhythm of War; introduces the Dawnshard revelation on Akinah and materially updates Rysn, Lopen, Huio, Cord, and the Sleepless.

cosmereBooks.title: Rhythm of War
cosmereBooks.connection: Stormlight book 4 and this atlas’s spoiler ceiling.

characters.name: Kaladin Stormblessed
characters.summary: A surgeon’s son turned soldier, slave, and leader. His bond with Syl restores Windrunner powers, while his central conflict is how to protect people when opposing sides both contain people worth saving.

status.label: Soldier, then enslaved after Amaram’s betrayal
Bridge Four member; begins rebuilding the crew
Captain of Dalinar’s guard; two Windrunner Ideals spoken
Bond damaged by conflicting promises, then restored; Third Ideal spoken
Windrunner commander returning to occupied Hearthstone
Kholinar mission member; unable to reconcile competing groups during the palace battle
Returns from Shadesmar and fights at Thaylen Field
Relieved from frontline command after cumulative battle trauma
Builds a clinic and peer-support model in Urithiru
Primary mobile resistance fighter during the occupation
Accepts he cannot save everyone, swears the Fourth Ideal, and gains living Shardplate
Chooses to continue mental-health work and prepares for a mission to Shinovar

characters.name: Sylphrena
characters.summary: Kaladin’s honorspren. Curious and empathetic, she gradually recovers identity and memory as their bond strengthens. She represents the moral rather than merely technical side of Windrunner oaths.

status.label: Half-aware windspren-like companion
Recognized as an honorspren and source of Surgebinding
Nearly lost when Kaladin violates the spirit of his oaths
Bond restored; can become a living Shardblade
Active Windrunner spren at Thaylen Field
Fourth-Ideal Windrunner bond; Kaladin’s windspren form living Shardplate

characters.name: Dalinar Kholin
characters.summary: Gavilar’s brother and former conqueror. Visions, the Codes, and his bond with the Stormfather push him from Alethi warlord toward coalition builder; Oathbringer restores the memories he surrendered to survive his guilt.

status.label: Highprince troubled by highstorm visions
Trades his Shardblade for Bridge Four and commits to unification
Bonds the Stormfather and rediscovers Urithiru
Coalition architect; recovered memories reveal the Rift
Rejects Odium’s attempt to claim his pain and opens Honor’s Perpendicularity
Bondsmith and public author of Oathbringer
Leads coalition war effort in Emul while seeking deeper Bondsmith mastery
Confronts Ishar and witnesses dangerous unbound Bondsmith powers
Negotiates a ten-day contest-of-champions agreement with Odium

characters.name: Navani Kholin
characters.summary: Engineer, political organizer, and widow of Gavilar. She coordinates fabrial research and the Oathgate network, marries Dalinar, and supplies much of the coalition’s practical infrastructure.

status.label: Queen mother and patron of artifabrians
Leads Urithiru research and communications
Marries Dalinar; central coalition organizer
Coordinates defense and Oathgate operations at Thaylen Field
Captured during Urithiru occupation and forced into research under Raboniel
Co-discovers Warlight and develops tone-based Light science
Discovers anti-Voidlight and the path to anti-Light
Bonds the Sibling and becomes a Bondsmith; restores Towerlight

characters.name: Adolin Kholin
characters.summary: Dalinar’s elder son, an elite duelist and unusually socially perceptive soldier. His killing of Sadeas remains concealed through Oathbringer; in Shadesmar, his respectful relationship with his deadeye Blade becomes visibly unusual.

status.label: Kholin heir and Shardbearer
Wins pivotal duels; supports Kaladin and Shallan
Kills Sadeas in an isolated confrontation
Kholinar strike-team member
Travels through Shadesmar with Mayalaran
Marries Shallan after Thaylen Field
Human diplomatic envoy seeking renewed honorspren bonds
Accepts trial by witness in Lasting Integrity
Maya’s testimony establishes that ancient spren participated willingly in the Recreance

characters.name: Renarin Kholin
characters.summary: Dalinar’s younger son. Quiet, medically stigmatized, and eager to contribute, he secretly bonds Glys. By Oathbringer, his visions differ from ordinary Truthwatcher expectations because Glys has been altered by Sja-anat.

status.label: Unarmored prince seeking a useful place
Joins Bridge Four training and reveals a healing bond
Recognized Truthwatcher with troubling future visions
Confronts Jasnah and survives; helps resist the Thrill

characters.name: Jasnah Kholin
characters.summary: Historian, philosopher, and accomplished Elsecaller. She researches the returning Desolation, survives the attack on the Wind’s Pleasure by entering Shadesmar, and becomes queen of Alethkar after Elhokar’s death.

status.label: Renowned scholar in Kharbranth; Shallan’s target and future mentor
Apparently killed aboard the Wind’s Pleasure, actually escaped to Shadesmar
Returns near Urithiru after a long Cognitive Realm journey
Coalition strategist and senior Radiant
Crowned queen of Alethkar
Rules Alethkar-in-exile and fights personally on the Emuli front while planning structural reforms

characters.name: Shallan Davar
characters.summary: A Veden artist who seeks Jasnah to steal a Soulcaster and save her family. Her Cryptic bond, repressed trauma, Ghostblood infiltration, and personas—especially Veil and Radiant—become inseparable from her growing Lightweaver skill.

status.label: Would-be thief seeking Jasnah’s wardship
Confesses her theft and glimpses Shadesmar; accepted as ward
Survives ship attack; travels independently with Pattern
Lightweaver and Ghostblood contact; opens the Oathgate to Urithiru
Investigates murders and Re-Shephir while persona boundaries weaken
Kholinar mission; creates an unstable network of disguises
Uses mass illusions at Thaylen Field
Marries Adolin; still divided but choosing an anchored life
Leads espionage/diplomatic mission into Shadesmar while searching for Restares
Rejects the Ghostblood assassination mission against Kalak
Integrates Veil after acknowledging that Radiant killed Ialai
Admits Testament was her first Cryptic and that she broke that earlier bond

characters.name: Pattern
characters.summary: Shallan’s Cryptic partner. Fascinated by lies, truth, and human contradiction, he helps her Soulcast and Lightweave while pushing her to acknowledge memories she has buried.

status.label: Seen first in drawings and symbol-headed figures
Fully present as Shallan’s bonded Cryptic
Can become a living Shardblade
Active Lightweaver spren; bond remains tied to difficult truths

characters.name: Szeth-son-son-Vallano
characters.summary: A Shin man declared Truthless and compelled to obey whoever holds his Oathstone. He assassinates rulers with Jezrien’s Honorblade, is defeated at Narak, restored by Nale, takes up Nightblood, and ultimately chooses Dalinar as the authority he will follow.

status.label: Truthless assassin wielding Jezrien’s Honorblade
Controlled through a succession of masters, ultimately the Diagram
Defeated at Narak; separated from the Honorblade and restored by Nale
Skybreaker trainee carrying Nightblood
Completes a Skybreaker Ideal by choosing Dalinar as his moral law
Fights for the coalition at Thaylen Field
Uses Nightblood during Ishar confrontation and prepares for a Shinovar crusade
Kills Taravangian’s mortal body, unintentionally placing Nightblood within reach of Rayse

characters.name: Nightblood
characters.summary: A sentient Awakened sword from Nalthis, created under a dangerously vague command to destroy evil. It consumes enormous Investiture and can kill far beyond ordinary physical damage. Nale gives it to Szeth.

status.label: Offered by Nale after Szeth’s restoration
Carried by Szeth during Skybreaker training
Used against the Thunderclast at Thaylen Field
Cuts Ishar’s Connection and chips an Honorblade during the Tukar confrontation
Consumes Rayse, killing Odium’s Vessel but leaving the Shard available for Taravangian

characters.name: Wit
characters.summary: A worldhopping storyteller who appears across the Cosmere. On Roshar he serves as Alethi Wit, advises or provokes major characters, uses several non-Rosharan arts, and at Oathbringer’s end rescues a Cryptic from occupied Kholinar.

status.label: Court Wit operating around the Kholins
Meets Jasnah as she exits Shadesmar
Performs stories in occupied Kholinar and supports Shallan
Bonds a Cryptic in the palace ruins
Confronts the new Odium unknowingly; some Breath-stored memories are removed and the encounter is replayed

characters.name: Taravangian
characters.summary: A ruler whose visit to the Nightwatcher/Cultivation produces alternating intelligence and compassion. On his most intelligent day he dictates the Diagram, a plan to save a remnant of humanity through controlled atrocities and political domination.

status.label: Apparently gentle king and hospital patron
Revealed as Szeth’s secret master and Diagram leader
Diagram expands through Jah Keved’s collapse
Joins Dalinar’s coalition while hiding his agenda
Betrays coalition intelligence to Odium, then accepts a deal intended to preserve Kharbranth
Betrays the coalition in Emul; Diagram collapses and he is imprisoned
Uses Renarin/Sja-anat uncertainty and Szeth’s hatred to create an opening against Odium
Kills Rayse with Nightblood and Ascends as the new Vessel of Odium
Begins planning as the new Odium while hiding the Vessel change

characters.name: Lift
characters.summary: A young Edgedancer who metabolizes food into usable Investiture rather than relying on Stormlight in the normal way. Her irreverence masks a fierce commitment to people institutions overlook.

status.label: Intruder in Azir; saves Gawx and helps make him Prime
Travels to Yeddaw and speaks her Third Ideal while protecting the Stump
Joins the Radiant coalition at Urithiru
Enters Dalinar’s vision and helps at Thaylen Field
Captured during the occupation because her Lifelight use bypasses parts of the tower suppression

characters.name: Wyndle
characters.summary: Lift’s cultivated, anxious spren companion. He forms plantlike trails in the Physical Realm and can become her living Shardfork/Blade despite preferring civilized restraint.

status.label: Bonded to Lift under Cultivation’s influence
Supports Lift through Yeddaw and Nale’s pursuit
Active Edgedancer spren at Thaylen Field

characters.name: Odium
characters.summary: The Shard of divine hatred and passion. Rayse holds it through nearly all of Rhythm of War, still bound to the Rosharan system and increasingly strained by setbacks. Near the end, Taravangian kills Rayse with Nightblood and takes up the Shard; the power remains Odium but its Vessel and strategy change.

status.label: Distant enemy inferred through visions and history
Everstorm restores a direct route for the Fused
Appears personally to Dalinar and negotiates through visions
Fails to claim Dalinar at Thaylen Field; remains bound and dangerous
Rayse continues directing the Fused war and pressure on Dalinar/Kaladin
Rayse agrees with Dalinar to a contest of champions in ten days
Rayse is killed; Taravangian Ascends as Odium
Taravangian secretly tests his new freedom and manipulates Wit’s encounter

characters.name: Stormfather
characters.summary: Vast spren of the highstorm and a repository of Honor’s power and impressions. Reluctantly bonds Dalinar, gives visions, and becomes the core of Dalinar’s Bondsmith abilities.

status.label: Voice in highstorms; source of visions is initially misunderstood
Accepts a Bondsmith bond with Dalinar
Shows coalition rulers Honor’s visions
Participates in opening Honor’s Perpendicularity

characters.name: Cultivation
characters.summary: One of Roshar’s resident Shards. Often conflated with the Nightwatcher, but personally intervened in Dalinar’s and Taravangian’s boons and curses as part of long-term plans.

status.label: Known mainly through religion and the Nightwatcher tradition
Revealed to have personally pruned Dalinar’s memories and prepared their return
Her intervention in Taravangian is also strongly implied
Reveals that preparing Taravangian was one of her long-term gambles and offers to teach the new Odium

characters.name: Honor
characters.summary: The dead Shard once held by Tanavast. His power remains in the Stormfather, honorspren, Honorblades, oaths, and Rosharan systems; his recorded visions warn of Odium and urge unity.

status.label: Dead before the main story; visions are mistaken for direct speech
Nature of his recordings and death becomes clearer
Dalinar briefly unites Spiritual, Cognitive, and Physical power associated with Honor

characters.name: Gavilar Kholin
characters.summary: Dalinar’s brother, Navani’s first husband, and the king whose assassination begins the war on the Shattered Plains. Oathbringer reveals his secret dealings with listeners, Heraldic knowledge, unusual gemstones, and plans to force a Desolation.

status.label: Unifier of Alethkar and secret sponsor of the Sons of Honor
Assassinated by Szeth during the treaty feast; leaves Dalinar the command to unite

characters.name: Elhokar Kholin
characters.summary: Gavilar’s son, an insecure king who slowly recognizes his failures. He joins the mission to retake Kholinar and begins speaking a Lightweaver oath while protecting his child, but Moash kills him before he completes it.

status.label: King directing the Vengeance Pact from the Shattered Plains
Asks Kaladin to teach him how to become better
Insists on joining the Kholinar infiltration
Killed by Moash while beginning a Radiant oath

characters.name: Aesudan Kholin
characters.summary: Elhokar’s wife and Gavinor’s mother. Left as regent in Kholinar, she embraces excess and attempts to bond the Unmade Yelig-nar; the bond consumes her.

status.label: Regent of Alethkar in Kholinar
Rules amid the Heart of the Revel’s influence
Consumed after taking Yelig-nar into herself

characters.name: Gavinor Kholin
characters.summary: Young son of Elhokar and Aesudan. Rescued from the palace during Kholinar’s fall and taken toward safety with the surviving mission.

characters.name: Evi Kholin
characters.summary: Dalinar’s first wife and mother of Adolin and Renarin. Gentle and culturally isolated at the Alethi court; she dies in the burning of Rathalas after trying to negotiate peace, a truth Dalinar had asked Cultivation to remove from his memory.

status.label: Political bride who tries to moderate Dalinar
Killed at the Rift; memory and even her name later excised from Dalinar
Recovered memory becomes the center of Dalinar’s reckoning

characters.name: Tien
characters.summary: Kaladin’s younger brother, whose optimism and death in battle define Kaladin’s protective drive. Oathbringer’s Spiritual vision lets Kaladin speak with an impression of him during the Battle of Thaylen Field.

status.label: Conscripted through Roshone’s retaliation
Killed as an inexperienced messenger placed in a sacrificial squad

characters.name: Lirin
characters.summary: Hearthstone’s surgeon and Kaladin’s father. His strict medical pacifism shaped Kaladin, while his conflict with Roshone helped trigger the family’s losses.

characters.name: Hesina
characters.summary: Kaladin’s perceptive mother, skilled at balancing Lirin’s principles with emotional practicality. Reunited with Kaladin when he returns to occupied Hearthstone.

characters.name: Oroden
characters.summary: The baby born to Lirin and Hesina after Kaladin left Hearthstone; his existence surprises Kaladin on his return.

characters.name: Brightlord Roshone
characters.summary: Exiled lighteyes made citylord of Hearthstone. His feud with Lirin and manipulation of conscription contribute to Tien’s death; by Oathbringer he is a diminished figure under singer occupation.

characters.name: Laral
characters.summary: Kaladin’s childhood friend, later Roshone’s wife and de facto local authority. She challenges Kaladin’s simplified memory of Hearthstone and helps manage civilians during occupation.

characters.name: Meridas Amaram
characters.summary: An admired Alethi general who murders Kaladin’s surviving squad and steals their Shards. Exposed but politically protected, he later inherits Sadeas’s army, accepts Yelig-nar, and dies fighting Kaladin at Thaylen Field.

status.label: Kaladin’s commander and public model of honor
Steals Helaran’s Shards and enslaves Kaladin
Privately exposed before Dalinar but avoids public justice
Highprince over Sadeas’s forces and secret Sons of Honor leader
Bonds Yelig-nar; killed in battle

characters.name: Torol Sadeas
characters.summary: Dalinar’s old war companion and chief political rival. He abandons Dalinar at the Tower, weaponizes public perception, and refuses reconciliation; Adolin kills him after Narak.

status.label: Highprince and nominal ally
Betrays Dalinar at the Tower
Open political enemy
Killed by Adolin in Urithiru

characters.name: Ialai Sadeas
characters.summary: Sadeas’s politically formidable wife. After his death she retains control of his faction and tries to obstruct Dalinar’s coalition while investigating who killed him.

characters.name: Teleb
characters.summary: Veteran archer and officer who served Dalinar from the unification wars through the Shattered Plains; killed before the main Oathbringer campaign, with flashbacks expanding his history.

characters.name: Kadash
characters.summary: A former soldier who became an ardent after witnessing the Rift. He debates Dalinar’s rejection of Vorin orthodoxy and embodies the cost of Dalinar’s old campaigns.

characters.name: Sebarial
characters.summary: A deliberately eccentric highprince whose practical commerce and logistics repeatedly prove more useful than his reputation suggests. Patron and partner of Palona.

characters.name: Palona
characters.summary: A Herdazian darkeyes who manages Sebarial’s household and commercial affairs with blunt competence.

characters.name: Aladar
characters.summary: One of the first highprinces to support Dalinar’s reforms after seeing Sadeas’s destructive politics; commands coalition forces.

characters.name: Roion
characters.summary: Cautious highprince who joins the Narak expedition and is killed by Szeth during the battle.

characters.name: Ruthar
characters.summary: Aggressive, obstructionist highprince who resists Dalinar’s coalition and exploits Alethi custom.

characters.name: Hatham
characters.summary: Diplomatic highprince whose wife’s social network and his relative moderation make him a useful coalition participant.

characters.name: Bethab
characters.summary: One of Alethkar’s highprinces, generally a secondary political actor in the Plains and Urithiru councils.

characters.name: Thanadal
characters.summary: One of the ten Alethi highprinces; mostly present through council and campaign politics.

characters.name: Vamah
characters.summary: An Alethi highprince who participates in the political realignment around Dalinar and the coalition.

characters.name: Dukar
characters.summary: An ardent associated with Kharbranth’s Soulcasters and the examination of Jasnah’s supposed fabrial.

characters.name: Baxil
characters.summary: Interlude thief who works for the woman later identifiable as the Herald Shalash, destroying depictions of herself.

characters.name: Av
characters.summary: Baxil’s cousin and partner during the interlude involving the destruction of Heraldic art.

characters.name: Teft
characters.summary: One of Kaladin’s earliest supporters and the source of old Radiant lore through the Envisagers. Addiction and shame isolate him in Oathbringer, but he returns to protect Bridge Four and speaks a Windrunner Ideal.

status.label: Bridge Four veteran who recognizes Surgebinding
Core lieutenant and trainer
Struggling with firemoss addiction and self-loathing
Speaks a Windrunner Ideal and arrives at Thaylen Field
Steps down from active duty to stay with Kaladin and pursue recovery
Awakens to defend others during the final occupation crisis
Killed by Moash after Phendorana is permanently destroyed

characters.name: Lunamor
characters.summary: Horneater member of Bridge Four, usually called Rock. Serves as cook, storyteller, emotional center, and reluctant fighter; at Thaylen Field he breaks a personal taboo to save Kaladin by killing Amaram.

status.label: Bridge Four cook and morale builder
Windrunner squire able to use Stormlight near Kaladin
Kills Amaram with a Shardbow to protect Kaladin; troubled by the act

characters.name: Sigzil
characters.summary: Azish former apprentice of Wit who becomes Bridge Four’s record keeper, experimenter, and organizational officer. His precision helps turn a survivor group into a functioning military unit.

characters.name: The Lopen
characters.summary: One-armed Herdazian bridgeman whose relentless humor and enormous cousin network conceal sharp resilience. Stormlight regrows his arm, and he develops Windrunner powers as a squire.

status.label: Swears the Third Ideal after the Akinah expedition

characters.name: Moash
characters.summary: A capable bridgeman whose grandparents died through Roshone and Elhokar’s failures. His revenge plot breaks his bond with Kaladin; among the singers he kills Elhokar, later kills Jezrien with a special dagger, and accepts the name Vyre.

status.label: Bridge Four member and Kaladin’s close friend
Shardbearer in the guard; secretly joins Graves’s assassination plot
Attacks Kaladin and flees after the plot collapses
Captured by singers, then voluntarily works within their army
Kills Elhokar in Kholinar
Kills Jezrien and is named Vyre
Works directly for Odium and argues Kaladin must be spiritually broken, not simply killed
Permanently kills Phendorana and murders Teft
Flees restored Urithiru; loss of Odium’s numbing Connection briefly exposes his guilt and he becomes blind

characters.name: Skar
characters.summary: Bridge Four veteran who becomes a squire and instructor. He initially struggles to draw Stormlight, then succeeds while helping others rather than focusing on himself.

characters.name: Drehy
characters.summary: Bridge Four member and Windrunner squire. He and Skar survive Kholinar’s fall and carry Gavinor away from the palace.

characters.name: Hobber
characters.summary: Bridge Four member whose legs are severed by Szeth. Windrunner squiring and Stormlight eventually restore his ability to stand and walk.

characters.name: Leyten
characters.summary: Bridge Four member who takes responsibility for equipment and uniforms as the group professionalizes.

characters.name: Dabbid
characters.summary: Quiet Bridge Four member, long assumed unable or unwilling to speak. He remains observant and loyal, often handling practical work others miss.

status.label: Secretly active while most Radiants are unconscious; becomes a key resistance courier

characters.name: Peet
characters.summary: Bridge Four member and Windrunner squire who serves as a dependable guard and field operative as the unit expands beyond its original crew.

characters.name: Torfin
characters.summary: Named Bridge Four member who survives the bridge crews and joins the expanding Windrunner unit.

characters.name: Natam
characters.summary: Named Bridge Four veteran and member of the Windrunner organization at Urithiru.

characters.name: Huio
characters.summary: Lopen’s Herdazian cousin and Bridge Four member, frequently underestimated because he speaks little Alethi.

status.label: Swears the Third Ideal while protecting Lopen

characters.name: Bisig
characters.summary: Member of Bridge Four’s enlarged Windrunner unit during the Urithiru period.

characters.name: Rlain
characters.summary: A listener sent into the Alethi bridge crews as Shen. Bridge Four’s acceptance becomes genuine; after revealing himself as Rlain, he struggles with being the last known listener among humans and with both cultures’ assumptions.

status.label: Listener spy assigned to Bridge Four under the name Shen
Reveals his identity and returns toward Narak
Survives the transformed listeners and rejoins Bridge Four
Bridge Four scout and cultural intermediary at Urithiru
Helps resistance and cares for unconscious Radiants
Bonds the enlightened mistspren Tumi as a Truthwatcher

characters.name: Dunny
characters.summary: Young Bridge Four member killed during a bridge run, one of the losses that hardens the crew’s determination to escape Sadeas’s system.

characters.name: Maps
characters.summary: Bridge Four member known for spatial memory and navigation; killed during the Battle of the Tower.

characters.name: Narm
characters.summary: Named Bridge Four member from the period before the crew’s rescue.

characters.name: Mart
characters.summary: Named bridgeman in Bridge Four during the Shattered Plains campaign.

characters.name: Gaz
characters.summary: The one-eyed sergeant who initially abuses Bridge Four. After deserting, he joins Shallan’s caravan, is given responsibility rather than punishment, and begins manifesting Lightweaver-squire abilities.

characters.name: Matal
characters.summary: Lighteyed officer overseeing bridge crews under Sadeas, with authority over Gaz and the brutal running system.

characters.name: Lamaril
characters.summary: Officer in Sadeas’s bridge organization who is removed during internal political maneuvering.

characters.name: Hashal
characters.summary: Officer assigned over the bridge crews after Lamaril, hostile to Kaladin and willing to use Bridge Four as expendable bait.

characters.name: Helaran Davar
characters.summary: Shallan’s eldest brother, absent from home and believed connected to the Ghostbloods before later evidence points to the Skybreakers. Kaladin kills him in battle without initially knowing his identity; Amaram steals his Shards.

status.label: Leaves the Davar household and acquires Shards through Skybreaker activity
Killed by Kaladin while attacking Amaram’s army

characters.name: Lin Davar
characters.summary: Abusive patriarch of House Davar, drawn into debt and political schemes after taking blame for his wife’s death. Shallan kills him to stop his violence against the family.

status.label: Takes public blame for his wife’s death and begins controlling the household through fear
Killed by Shallan during an attack on Balat

characters.name: Malise Gevelmar
characters.summary: Shallan’s mother, who attempts to kill her young daughter after discovering Surgebinding. Shallan kills her with a living Shardblade and represses the memory.

characters.name: Nan Balat Davar
characters.summary: Shallan’s older brother, physically injured and psychologically scarred by the Davar household. He escapes to Urithiru with the remaining family.

characters.name: Wikim Davar
characters.summary: One of Shallan’s brothers, bookish and vulnerable to his father’s control; later reunited with Shallan at Urithiru.

characters.name: Jushu Davar
characters.summary: One of Shallan’s brothers, whose gambling debts deepen the family’s financial crisis before the brothers escape to Urithiru.

characters.name: Eylita
characters.summary: Balat’s loyal betrothed, part of the Davar household that eventually reaches Urithiru.

characters.name: Kabsal
characters.summary: An apparently affable ardent who courts Jasnah through Shallan while secretly trying to poison her for the Ghostbloods. His own poison kills him when Jasnah substitutes Soulcast food.

characters.name: Yalb
characters.summary: Sociable sailor on the Wind’s Pleasure who helps Shallan navigate Kharbranth. He is missing after the ship attack within this spoiler boundary.

characters.name: Tozbek
characters.summary: Captain of the Wind’s Pleasure, hired by Shallan’s family and later carrying Jasnah and Shallan toward the Shattered Plains when the ship is attacked.

characters.name: Tvlakv
characters.summary: Slave trader who sells Kaladin to Sadeas and later transports Shallan through the Frostlands. Shallan takes control of his caravan after bandit attacks.

characters.name: Bluth
characters.summary: One of Tvlakv’s guards. Shallan’s idealized sketch helps him choose a better self, and he dies protecting the caravan.

characters.name: Vathah
characters.summary: Leader of Alethi deserters recruited by Shallan. He becomes a loyal officer and begins developing Lightweaver-squire abilities.

characters.name: Red
characters.summary: Red-haired member of Vathah’s deserters who joins Shallan’s household and covert operations.

characters.name: Grund
characters.summary: Urithiru street child recruited through Veil’s attempt to help the city’s poor; murdered during the conflict around the Midnight Mother, intensifying Shallan’s guilt.

characters.name: Ishnah
characters.summary: Woman with espionage experience who seeks membership in Shallan’s organization and becomes part of the growing Lightweaver network.

characters.name: Tyn
characters.summary: Experienced con artist who mentors Shallan in disguise while secretly ordered to recruit or kill her. Shallan kills Tyn after learning the truth.

characters.name: Mraize
characters.summary: Cosmopolitan Ghostblood operative who recruits Shallan through tests and controlled information. His trophy room signals extensive offworld travel and his orders focus on secrets, Radiants, and the Unmade.

status.label: Tests Shallan through Tyn’s cell and the warcamp meeting
Accepts Veil as an operative
Directs investigation of Re-Shephir and other Urithiru mysteries
Directs Shallan to identify/kill Restares and trades with Raboniel during the occupation
Loses Shallan as a willing Ghostblood operative after she rejects the mission

characters.name: Iyatil
characters.summary: Masked Ghostblood operative and Mraize’s mentor. Her culture and ancestry are offworld-linked, though the novels through Oathbringer leave most details implicit.

characters.name: Luesh
characters.summary: House Davar steward whose death leaves behind signs of Ghostblood affiliation and a Soulcaster central to the family’s debt crisis.

characters.name: Vathah's deserters
characters.summary: Collective entry for Vathah’s surviving deserters when individual names are not foregrounded; they become Shallan’s guards and later Lightweaver-associated personnel.

characters.name: Eshonai
characters.summary: Listener explorer and war leader who sought peaceful understanding with humans. Pressured into stormform, she loses control to Odium’s influence and falls into a chasm during Narak; Oathbringer confirms her death.

status.label: Flashbacks reveal the path from explorer to war leader
Listener general seeking alternatives to extermination
Takes stormform and becomes dominated by its new rhythms
Died after Narak; Stormfather grants a final Cognitive journey across Roshar
Falls during the Battle of Narak
Body recovered; death confirmed

characters.name: Venli
characters.summary: Eshonai’s ambitious sister, manipulated for years by Ulim into rediscovering forms of power. After the listeners are devastated, she serves Odium as an envoy while secretly bonding Timbre and beginning to reject the role built for her.

status.label: Scholar experimenting with new forms under Ulim’s direction
Engineers stormform adoption and suppresses doubts
One of few surviving listeners; claimed as Odium’s envoy
Regal traveling with the Fused, secretly sheltering Timbre
Begins using Radiant power against Odium’s expectations
Serves Raboniel while secretly practicing Radiant powers with Timbre
Learns surviving listeners remain on the Shattered Plains
Openly sides with humans/listeners against Odium’s hardliners
Leaves to rejoin the surviving listeners and pursue a freer future

characters.name: Timbre
characters.summary: A lightspren who first sought Eshonai and later bonds Venli. She traps and suppresses the voidspren in Venli’s gemheart, allowing a secret Radiant bond to grow.

characters.name: Ulim
characters.summary: Voidspren smuggled to the listeners before the Everstorm. He cultivates Venli’s ambition, directs form experiments, and helps prepare Odium’s return.

status.label: Flashbacks show his gemstone arrival and manipulation of Venli before the Everstorm

characters.name: Demid
characters.summary: Venli’s mate and fellow scholar, later carrying a Fused soul after the Everstorm’s transformations.

characters.name: Thude
characters.summary: Listener officer loyal to Eshonai who helps listeners resisting stormform escape into the chasms before Narak.

characters.name: Jaxlim
characters.summary: Mother of Eshonai and Venli. Her decline and the sisters’ different responses form an emotional center of the listener flashbacks.

characters.name: Klade
characters.summary: Listener leader who hires Szeth for Gavilar’s assassination after receiving the idea through a mysterious voice; later part of the listener leadership during the war.

characters.name: Abronai
characters.summary: One of the listener Five and a military leader during the final Shattered Plains campaign.

characters.name: Listener dissenters
characters.summary: Listeners led away from stormform by Thude and others. Their exact fate remains unresolved at the end of Oathbringer.

characters.name: Leshwi
characters.summary: A high-ranking flying Fused of the shanay-im. She values capable opponents and commands singer forces around Kholinar and Thaylen Field.

status.label: Recognizes Venli’s Radiant bond as a sign of old singer-spren relationships returning and turns against Odium’s hardliners
Leaves with listeners and a small group of Fused seeking another path

characters.name: Hariel
characters.summary: One of the returning Fused encountered during the new Desolation.

characters.name: Sadeas soldiers under the Thrill
characters.summary: Amaram’s troops, overwhelmed by Nergaoul’s Thrill and turned against the coalition during the Battle of Thaylen Field.

characters.name: Sah
characters.summary: Freed singer Kaladin meets after Hearthstone. A former parshman and father who humanizes the singer side of the conflict; killed during the chaotic Kholinar palace battle.

characters.name: Khen
characters.summary: Member of the singer group Kaladin travels with toward Kholinar, illustrating the newly awakened people’s varied goals.

characters.name: Norl
characters.summary: One of the awakened singers in the group Kaladin accompanies on the road to Kholinar.

characters.name: Vai
characters.summary: Singer traveling with Sah’s group during Kaladin’s attempt to understand the transformed social order.

characters.name: Maru
characters.summary: Singer in the group Kaladin joins after Hearthstone.

characters.name: Re-Shephir
characters.summary: An Unmade hiding in Urithiru who imitates violence through Midnight Essence. Shallan confronts and drives her away by recognizing her imitative, almost childlike hunger to understand.

characters.name: Nergaoul
characters.summary: The Unmade responsible for the Thrill, the intoxicating bloodlust long normalized in Alethi warfare. Dalinar identifies it, resists it, and traps it in the King’s Drop at Thaylen Field.

characters.name: Moelach
characters.summary: Unmade whose presence produces prophetic Death Rattles near death. Taravangian’s hospitals secretly murder patients to record them; Moelach later moves toward Jah Keved.

characters.name: Ashertmarn
characters.summary: Unmade occupying the Kholinar Oathgate platform and feeding a cult of endless indulgence that drains resistance from the city.

characters.name: Sja-anat
characters.summary: Unmade capable of changing or 'enlightening' spren. She communicates with Shallan and implies her interests no longer perfectly align with Odium; Glys and some Oathgate spren bear her touch.

status.label: Helps create uncertainty in Odium’s futures and sends enlightened spren toward Renarin/Rlain

characters.name: Yelig-nar
characters.summary: Unmade that grants a host access to many Surges after swallowing a gemstone, at the risk of being consumed. Aesudan fails to contain it; Amaram later becomes its host.

characters.name: Ba-Ado-Mishram
characters.summary: Powerful Unmade named in the gemstone archive as the leader who supplied Voidlight and forms to singers during the False Desolation before being imprisoned by the ancient Radiants.

characters.name: Chemoarish
characters.summary: One of the Unmade, known largely through names, folklore, and imperfect historical records at this point.

characters.name: Dai-Gonarthis
characters.summary: One of the Unmade, associated in fragmentary lore with consuming sorrow; little is confirmed by the end of Oathbringer.

characters.name: Adrotagia
characters.summary: Senior Diagram member and one of Taravangian’s closest planners, helping interpret the document and manage its political program.

characters.name: Mrall
characters.summary: Taravangian’s calm bodyguard and trusted Diagram agent, notable for unusual control over emotional state.

characters.name: Graves
characters.summary: Diagram operative who recruits Moash into an assassination attempt against Elhokar, arguing that Dalinar should rule. Flees after the plot fails and later dies among singer forces.

characters.name: Malata
characters.summary: Dustbringer bonded to Spark and secretly loyal to the Diagram. She cooperates with the coalition while sabotaging Oathgate equipment on Taravangian’s orders.

characters.name: Spark
characters.summary: Malata’s ashspren partner, resentful of how humans remember the Recreance and willing to support the Diagram’s destructive agenda.

characters.name: Dova
characters.summary: The Diagram’s scholar Dova is identified by Taravangian as the Herald Battar, one of the ancient oath-bound figures now acting outside her original role.

characters.name: Noura
characters.summary: Influential Azish vizier involved in selecting and advising Prime Gawx, skeptical of Lift but increasingly forced to accept Radiant realities.

characters.name: Gawx
characters.summary: A street thief whom Lift saves with Regrowth after Nale attacks him. Bureaucratic procedure elevates him as Prime Yanagawn, and he later joins Dalinar’s coalition.

status.label: Prime Yanagawn supports the Emul campaign and coalition strategy

characters.name: The Stump
characters.summary: Gruff orphanage keeper in Yeddaw whose apparently miraculous recoveries reveal a hidden Truthwatcher bond. Lift protects her from Nale.

characters.name: Mik
characters.summary: Child at the Stump’s orphanage whose condition and recovery help Lift understand the supposed miracle.

characters.name: Arclo
characters.summary: A Dysian Aimian composed of many cremling hordelings. He observes Lift, explains part of the Sleepless nature, and warns that hidden guardians monitor dangerous knowledge.

characters.name: Nale
characters.summary: Herald associated with the Skybreakers. Convinced new Radiants will cause Desolation, he uses local law to execute them; Lift forces him to confront evidence that the Desolation has already returned, after which he sides with the singers as Roshar’s original legal claimants.

status.label: Hunts Lift and other nascent Radiants under legal pretexts
Accepts that the Desolation has returned and stops the specific purge
Trains Szeth among the Skybreakers
Declares allegiance to the singers’ side based on his legal interpretation

characters.name: Fen Rnamdi
characters.summary: Pragmatic ruler of Thaylenah. Initially wary of Dalinar’s authority, she joins the coalition and defends her city through Odium’s assault.

characters.name: Kmakl
characters.summary: Queen Fen’s husband and political partner, involved in Thaylen coalition decisions.

characters.name: Tarah
characters.summary: Quartermaster in Amaram’s army and Kaladin’s past romantic partner. Flashbacks show Kaladin choosing responsibility for his squad over leaving with her.

characters.name: Rushu
characters.summary: Brilliant, easily distracted ardent who works with Navani on fabrials, Shardplate observations, and Urithiru systems.

characters.name: Rial
characters.summary: Plainspoken, often intoxicated Kholin officer whose casual manner belies competence and loyalty.

characters.name: Teshav
characters.summary: Navani’s senior scribe and a reliable member of the Kholin administrative network.

characters.name: Jochi
characters.summary: Member of the Azish bureaucracy around Gawx and Lift’s disruptive appearances.

characters.name: Jezrien
characters.summary: Leader of the Heralds in ancient tradition. By Oathbringer he lives as the broken beggar Ahu in Kholinar; Moash kills him with a gemstone-pommel dagger that traps or destroys his Cognitive Shadow.

status.label: Oathpact Herald and bearer of the Windrunner Honorblade
Abandons the Oathpact at Aharietiam with most Heralds
Killed by Moash in Kholinar

characters.name: Ishar
characters.summary: Herald associated with Bondsmiths, now ruling Tukar as the god-priest Tezim. Nale treats his judgment as authoritative, but his sanity and motives are deeply suspect.

status.label: Demonstrates unbound Bondsmith power, attempts to steal Dalinar’s bond, and conducts disturbing Physical-Realm spren experiments

characters.name: Shalash
characters.summary: Herald who compulsively destroys images and statues of herself. She is located and brought toward Thaylen Field, where she senses Jezrien’s death.

characters.name: Talenel
characters.summary: The one Herald who did not abandon the Oathpact. He returns from millennia of torture on Braize, nearly catatonic but still warning humanity; a lucid moment expresses joy that humans had time to advance.

status.label: Alone returns to Braize after Aharietiam
Appears at Kholinar’s gate with a Shardblade and warning
Taken to the Shattered Plains; mostly unresponsive
Briefly lucid with Shalash after Thaylen Field

characters.name: Kalak
characters.summary: Prelude viewpoint Herald who witnesses Aharietiam and accepts abandonment of the Oathpact. His present-day location and role are not resolved by Oathbringer.

status.label: Revealed as Restares and High Judge in Lasting Integrity; wants a way to leave Roshar
Becomes entangled in Ghostblood and honorspren politics around Adolin/Shallan

characters.name: Battar
characters.summary: Herald associated with Elsecallers. Taravangian identifies the Diagram scholar Dova as Battar, though details remain limited.

characters.name: Pailiah
characters.summary: Herald associated with Truthwatchers. A woman in the Palanaeum is suggested by authorial clues to be Pailiah, but the novels do not foreground confirmation.

characters.name: Chanarach
characters.summary: Herald associated with Dustbringers, known chiefly through doctrine and historical references at this spoiler boundary.

characters.name: Vedel
characters.summary: Herald associated with Edgedancers, known mainly through Vorin iconography and ancient order structure by Oathbringer.

characters.name: Nightwatcher
characters.summary: Powerful spren cultivated by Cultivation. Petitioners seek a boon and receive a curse, though Dalinar’s encounter is taken over directly by Cultivation.

characters.name: Glys
characters.summary: Renarin’s mistspren, altered by Sja-anat. Their bond grants healing and unusual future-oriented visions that make Renarin a blind spot in Odium’s predictions.

characters.name: Ivory
characters.summary: Jasnah’s inkspren partner, formal and wary of human unpredictability. Enables her Elsecalling and living Shardblade.

characters.name: Mayalaran
characters.summary: The deadeye spren of Adolin’s Shardblade. In Shadesmar she appears as a damaged cultivationspren; Adolin’s care elicits limited response, including giving her name and summoning unusually quickly.

status.label: Adolin’s unnamed dead Shardblade
Seen in Shadesmar as a deadeye; identifies herself as Mayalaran
Responds to Adolin during the Thaylen Field crisis
Increasingly responsive to Adolin during his trial preparation
Speaks publicly and testifies that the deadeyes’ sacrifice was chosen

characters.name: Notum
characters.summary: Honorspren captain of the ship Honor’s Path. He transports the human group in Shadesmar while debating Syl’s bond and honorspren law.

status.label: Testifies under pressure but ultimately defends renewed human-spren bonds

characters.name: Phendorana
characters.summary: Honorspren who begins associating closely with Bridge Four and Teft during the growth of the Windrunner order.

status.label: Permanently killed by Moash using a raysium/anti-Light weapon

characters.name: The ancient honorspren generation
characters.summary: Historical generation of honorspren created before the Recreance; Syl is the only surviving member known to the modern honorspren.

characters.name: Oathgate spren
characters.summary: Paired large spren governing each Oathgate. Some refuse or restrict travel; the Kholinar pair are corrupted by Sja-anat and send the strike team into Shadesmar rather than Urithiru.

characters.name: Cusicesh
characters.summary: Enormous spren appearing on a regular schedule in Kasitor Bay, seen in an Axies interlude.

characters.name: Axies the Collector
characters.summary: Immortal-seeming Siah Aimian who catalogs spren, can alter his body markings, and appears in interludes studying unusual manifestations.

characters.name: Zahel
characters.summary: Adolin and Renarin’s irritable swordmaster, secretly Vasher of Nalthis. He sustains himself with Stormlight rather than consuming a weekly Breath and uses color metaphors and Awakening-informed habits that mark his origin.

characters.name: Azure
characters.summary: Foreign commander leading Kholinar’s Wall Guard, secretly Vivenna of Nalthis. She carries a nonstandard sentient-looking sword, uses Awakening, seeks Zahel and Nightblood, and separates from the group in Shadesmar.

characters.name: Felt
characters.summary: Kholin scout who accompanied Dalinar to the Nightwatcher and whose phrasing hints he is not Rosharan. He previously appeared on Scadrial.

characters.name: Demoux
characters.summary: One of three foreigners searching the Purelake for Hoid; identifiable across the Cosmere as the Scadrian Demoux.

characters.name: Galladon
characters.summary: One of Ishikk’s three foreign visitors, recognizable as Galladon from Sel through speech patterns and appearance.

characters.name: Baon
characters.summary: Third member of the Purelake search party seeking Hoid, originating from Taldain.

characters.name: Nazh
characters.summary: Khriss’s field agent, responsible for many handwritten annotations attached to maps and documents. Often complains about the danger and inconvenience of collecting them.

characters.name: Khrissalla
characters.summary: Leading independent scholar of Investiture. The planetary essays in Arcanum Unbounded provide the pre-Oathbringer reader with explicit system-level context.

characters.name: Vasher / Zahel continuity
characters.summary: Identity bridge: Warbreaker’s Vasher is the Rosharan swordmaster Zahel. The novels signal this through idiom, life-sense behavior, Breath concepts, and his relationship to Nightblood.

characters.name: Vivenna / Azure continuity
characters.summary: Identity bridge: Warbreaker’s Vivenna appears in Oathbringer as Azure, older, martial, and searching for Vasher and Nightblood.

characters.name: Ishikk
characters.summary: Purelaker fisherman employed by three offworld visitors to watch for Hoid. His viewpoint shows Purelake religion, food, and local resistance to outsiders.

characters.name: Rysn Ftori
characters.summary: Thaylen merchant apprentice whose interludes explore Shinovar, the Reshi Isles, and trade culture. A fall leaves her unable to walk; she receives the larkin Chiri-Chiri and helps protect the King’s Drop during Thaylen Field.

status.label: Vstim’s apprentice trading in Shinovar
Injured after falling from a Reshi greatshell island; given Chiri-Chiri
Thaylen merchant responsible for the King’s Drop during invasion
Owner/leader of the Wandersail expedition; Chiri-Chiri is ill
Bonds the Dawnshard Command in Akinah
Returns under a Sleepless compact; heightened perception begins

characters.name: Vstim
characters.summary: Rysn’s demanding but caring Thaylen babsk, using difficult trade missions as education in cultural perspective.

characters.name: Chiri-Chiri
characters.summary: Small larkin given to Rysn by the Reshi. She can drain Investiture and helps counter a Fused attack on the King’s Drop.

status.label: Ill and needs to return to the larkin homeland at Akinah
Recovers among luckspren and helps protect Rysn
Growing rapidly and beginning to form spoken words

characters.name: Relu-na
characters.summary: Ruler of a Reshi greatshell island encountered by Rysn; cultural assumptions about title and gender challenge the Thaylen delegation.

characters.name: Puuli
characters.summary: Natan lighthouse keeper who watches the sea for prophesied sailors arriving from the Origin, illustrating local apocalyptic expectations.

characters.name: Ellista
characters.summary: Ardent researching the Dawnchant in Urithiru, irritated by interruptions but part of the team that reveals humanity’s migration from Ashyn.

characters.name: Kaza
characters.summary: Terminally transformed Soulcaster on an expedition toward Akinah. She is poisoned before reaching the island’s secrets, showing both Soulcasting’s bodily cost and the Sleepless defense of Aimia.

characters.name: Sheler
characters.summary: Cruel officer captured in Herdaz and offered a grim choice of punishments, in an interlude displaying Herdazian resistance.

characters.name: Mem
characters.summary: Young worker whose interlude around Mraize’s household exposes mundane access to Ghostblood spaces and a piece of strange cleaning magic.

characters.name: Noro
characters.summary: Named member of the human resistance and Wall Guard structure under Azure during the siege.

characters.name: Riino
characters.summary: Elantrian operating a Shadesmar lighthouse. He uses a fortune-telling device, recognizes Kaladin as Invested, and directs the travelers toward Celebrant.

characters.name: Nohadon
characters.summary: Ancient ruler associated with the book The Way of Kings. Dalinar meets him in visions that may be more complex than simple historical recordings; his moral legacy shapes Dalinar’s reform project.

characters.name: Melishi
characters.summary: Bondsmith named in the gemstone archive as central to the plan to capture Ba-Ado-Mishram near the end of the False Desolation.

characters.name: Nikli
characters.summary: A Sleepless swarm using a human-shaped body as Rysn’s porter. Nikli accompanies the expedition under false pretenses, then reveals that the Sleepless engineered the mission’s dangers to protect Akinah and its Dawnshard.

status.label: Embedded with Rysn as a porter and observer
Revealed as Sleepless guardian; negotiates after Rysn becomes a Dawnshard
Bound by compact to guard Rysn and preserve the Akinah cover story

characters.name: Cord
characters.summary: Rock’s daughter. She accompanies Rysn’s Aimia expedition, can perceive spren unusually well, helps Rysn survive the Sleepless confrontation, and returns from Akinah with ancient Shardplate.

status.label: Joins the expedition to Akinah
Helps Rysn reach and negotiate in the Dawnshard chamber
Returns with ancient Shardplate from Akinah

characters.name: Rua
characters.summary: Lopen’s honorspren. Their bond matures during the Akinah expedition, and Rua can become a living Shardweapon after Lopen’s Third Ideal.

status.label: Living Shardweapon after Lopen swears the Third Ideal

characters.name: Caelinora
characters.summary: Huio’s honorspren. When Huio swears the Third Ideal to protect Lopen, Caelinora can manifest as a living Shardweapon.

status.label: Can manifest as a living Shardweapon after Huio’s Third Ideal

characters.name: Ral-na
characters.summary: A Reshi ruler who arrives at Urithiru after bonding an ashspren and becoming a Dustbringer, illustrating how rapidly Radiant bonds are spreading beyond the Alethi center.

status.label: Newly bonded Dustbringer visiting Urithiru

characters.name: Talik
characters.summary: Reshi envoy familiar with larkin. He identifies Chiri-Chiri’s illness as a reason to seek Akinah, helping launch Rysn’s expedition.

characters.name: Raboniel
characters.summary: A brilliant ancient Fused scholar who leads the occupation of Urithiru. Rather than treating Navani only as a prisoner, she becomes her scientific counterpart; together they discover Warlight and the principles that lead to anti-Light. Raboniel’s deeper aim is an irreversible end to the cycle of war.

status.label: Wins approval from the Nine to seize Urithiru
Controls the tower and directs corruption of the Sibling
Collaborates with Navani on mixed Lights and anti-Light research
Mortally wounded during liberation; asks Navani for a permanent death

characters.name: The Sibling
characters.summary: The great spren of Urithiru, associated with both Honor and Cultivation. The Sibling powers the tower’s integrated fabrial systems, resists Raboniel’s corruption, communicates secretly with Kaladin and Navani, and eventually bonds Navani.

status.label: Awakens enough to warn Navani as Urithiru is invaded
Partially corrupted and weakened; most Radiants suppressed
Bonds Navani as a Bondsmith and creates Towerlight
Restored control of Urithiru and tower defenses

characters.name: Lezian
characters.summary: A Fused who makes a tradition of killing anyone who kills him, becoming obsessed with Kaladin. His teleport-like Transportation lets him shed bodies and reappear nearby. Kaladin finally breaks his legend during the liberation of Urithiru.

status.label: Killed by Kaladin at Hearthstone and begins a personal pursuit
Hunts Kaladin through occupied Urithiru
Defeated and humiliated by Kaladin during the tower uprising
Permanently killed by El using anti-Stormlight

characters.name: Design
characters.summary: The Cryptic Wit rescued in occupied Kholinar at the end of Oathbringer, now named Design. She is irreverent, perceptive, and fully established as Wit’s bonded spren by Rhythm of War.

status.label: Bond begins in the Oathbringer epilogue
Active Lightweaver spren accompanying Wit

characters.name: Testament
characters.summary: The Cryptic Shallan bonded as a child before Pattern. Shallan broke her oaths after killing her mother, leaving Testament as a deadeye; acknowledging this buried bond becomes one of her central Rhythm of War revelations.

status.label: Bonded to child Shallan; bond later broken
Seen as a deadeye in Shadesmar without Shallan recognizing the full truth
Shallan consciously acknowledges Testament and her responsibility

characters.name: Tumi
characters.summary: An enlightened mistspren sent through Sja-anat’s network. Tumi chooses Rlain, making him a Truthwatcher with a corrupted/enlightened spren bond.

status.label: Bonds Rlain near the end of Rhythm of War

characters.name: Blended
characters.summary: An inkspren who tutors Adolin in honorspren legal procedure and watches Maya’s changing condition closely. She becomes an important neutral observer of the trial’s implications.

characters.name: Sekeir
characters.summary: A senior honorspren and hardline opponent of renewed human bonds. He tries to use Maya as evidence against Adolin, only for Maya’s testimony to overturn his framing of the Recreance.

status.label: Leads the anti-human case during Adolin’s trial
Discredited when Maya testifies that the ancient spren chose the Recreance

characters.name: El
characters.summary: An ancient Fused stripped of title and rhythms who studies humanity with unusual interest. In the closing chapters he receives Navani and Raboniel’s research and demonstrates anti-Stormlight by permanently killing Lezian.

status.label: Uses anti-Stormlight to permanently kill Lezian and studies the Rhythm of War notebook

characters.name: Axindweth
characters.summary: A mysterious offworld woman in Venli’s flashbacks who provides the gemstone containing Ulim and helps create the conditions for Odium’s influence among the listeners.

characters.name: Noril
characters.summary: A man suffering severe battle shock and depression whom Kaladin helps through structured peer support. His response helps Kaladin recognize a non-combat path for protecting people.

status.label: Patient in Kaladin’s emerging mental-health support group
Survives the occupation and remains part of Kaladin’s new work

characters.name: Godeke
characters.summary: An Edgedancer chosen for Adolin and Shallan’s diplomatic mission to the honorspren stronghold in Shadesmar.

characters.name: Zu
characters.summary: A Stoneward Radiant who accompanies the honorspren diplomatic mission through Shadesmar.

characters.name: Beryl
characters.summary: A Lightweaver in Shallan’s circle who becomes one of the suspected Ghostblood infiltrators during the Lasting Integrity mission.

characters.name: Dieno
characters.summary: The celebrated Herdazian general known as the Mink. After escaping occupation, he becomes a key coalition strategist and redirects the main military effort toward Emul.

status.label: Joins the coalition and helps design the Emul campaign
Coalition general after victory on the Emuli front

factions.name: House Kholin
factions.summary: Royal Alethi house founded politically by Gavilar’s unification and led militarily by Dalinar after the assassination. Its internal tensions drive much of the first three books.

status.label: Royal house at war on the Shattered Plains
Controls Urithiru but lacks secure Alethkar
Elhokar dead; Kholinar lost
Jasnah selected as queen; Dalinar leads supranational coalition

factions.name: Bridge Four
factions.summary: Former Sadeas bridge crew transformed by Kaladin into a mutually protective unit, then Dalinar’s guard and the core of the restored Windrunners.

status.label: Expendable slave crew
Freed and transferred to Dalinar
Royal guard and Windrunner squire group
Expanding military order at Urithiru

factions.name: Order of Windrunners
factions.summary: Radiants bonded to honorspren, using Adhesion and Gravitation. Their Ideals center on protection and its moral limits.
goals: Protect those who cannot protect themselves

status.label: Extinct in public understanding
Kaladin independently revives the order
Squires begin using Stormlight
Several active Windrunners and a growing support corps
Kaladin reaches the Fourth Ideal and manifests living Shardplate

factions.name: Order of Lightweavers
factions.summary: Radiants bonded to Cryptics, using Illumination and Transformation. Progress is expressed through personal truths rather than a uniform sequence of spoken Ideals.

status.label: Reemerging privately through Shallan
Shallan acts openly enough to operate the Narak Oathgate
A small network of potential squires forms around her

factions.name: Order of Bondsmiths
factions.summary: Rare order bonded to vast spren, using Adhesion and Tension with unusual powers over Connection and unification.
goals: Maintain bonds larger than individual combat

status.label: Dalinar bonds the Stormfather
Dalinar manifests unprecedented unifying power at Thaylen Field
Navani bonds the Sibling, creating a second active Bondsmith

factions.name: Order of Elsecallers
factions.summary: Radiants bonded to inkspren, using Transformation and Transportation. Jasnah is the only confirmed active member in this scope.

factions.name: Order of Truthwatchers
factions.summary: Radiants associated with mistspren, Progression, and Illumination. Renarin and the Stump manifest different-looking examples.

factions.name: Order of Edgedancers
factions.summary: Cultivationspren Radiants using Abrasion and Progression. Their oaths emphasize remembering, listening to, and protecting overlooked people.

factions.name: Order of Skybreakers
factions.summary: Highspren Radiants led in practice by Nale, using Gravitation and Division. They pursue external legal codes but are distorted by their Herald’s damaged judgment.

status.label: Secretly executes emerging Radiants
Nale accepts the Desolation has returned
Most follow Nale in siding with the singers; Szeth chooses Dalinar instead

factions.name: Order of Dustbringers
factions.summary: Also called Releasers; bonded to ashspren and using Division and Abrasion. Malata is the only active example foregrounded by Oathbringer.

factions.name: Order of Willshapers
factions.summary: Lightspren Radiants associated with Transportation and Cohesion and a drive toward freedom. Venli’s bond with Timbre is only beginning at the cutoff.

factions.name: Order of Stonewards
factions.summary: Order associated with Cohesion and Tension, ancient patron Taln, reliability, endurance, and battlefield resolve.

factions.name: Ghostbloods
factions.summary: Cross-world organization pursuing information, leverage, and control of Investiture-related opportunities. On Roshar, Mraize and Iyatil recruit Shallan while concealing the group’s full hierarchy.

status.label: Hidden behind House Davar’s Soulcaster and Kabsal’s attack
Shallan accepted as an operative under Mraize
Uses Shallan to investigate Re-Shephir
Shallan rejects Mraize’s assassination mission and openly breaks from his control

factions.name: The Diagram
factions.summary: Taravangian’s organization built around predictions dictated on his day of extraordinary intelligence. It treats controlled catastrophe as the path to saving a remnant.
goals: Preserve humanity at any moral cost

status.label: Runs the Death Rattle hospitals and Szeth’s assassination list
Uses civil collapse to absorb Jah Keved
Infiltrates the coalition
Taravangian trades coalition intelligence and accepts Odium’s limited protection deal

factions.name: Sons of Honor
factions.summary: Organization seeking the return of the Heralds and Vorin dominance by provoking a Desolation. Gavilar and Amaram are central Rosharan leaders.

status.label: Gavilar’s plans survive him in fragments
Amaram’s leadership and goals are exposed

factions.name: Listeners
factions.summary: Singer-descended people who rejected their gods and forms of power, preserving themselves on the Shattered Plains. Alethi call them Parshendi. Their attempt to escape genocide through stormform enables the Everstorm and nearly destroys them.

status.label: At war with Alethkar under the Vengeance Pact
Leadership adopts stormform
Narak disaster; most become stormform hosts or die, dissenters escape

factions.name: Singers
factions.summary: The awakened people humans had enslaved as parshmen. The Everstorm restores minds and forms, but freedom quickly becomes entangled with Fused rule and Odium’s war.
goals: Survive control by Fused and humans

factions.name: The Fused
factions.summary: Ancient singer souls repeatedly reborn into living singer bodies through the Everstorm. They serve Odium, retain specialized Surges, and vary in sanity and honor.

status.label: Return through the Everstorm
Command singer occupation forces across Alethkar and Marat
Lead the assault on Thaylen Field
Urithiru occupation fails; divisions emerge among Fused including Leshwi’s defection
Anti-Light makes permanent Fused death demonstrably possible

factions.name: The Unmade
factions.summary: Nine ancient spren altered by Odium. Each manifests a different influence; several act semi-independently and are central to Oathbringer’s investigations.
goals: Serve or evade Odium according to individual nature

factions.name: Odium’s forces
factions.summary: Umbrella for Odium, Fused, Regals, loyal voidspren, Unmade, and human collaborators during the True Desolation.

factions.name: Coalition of Monarchs
factions.summary: Dalinar’s Oathgate-linked alliance among Urithiru, Alethkar’s loyalists, Thaylenah, Azir, Kharbranth/Jah Keved, and other states—compromised by hidden agendas.

status.label: Initial remote meetings through visions and spanreeds
Formal but fragile alliance
Survives Thaylen Field despite Taravangian’s betrayal

factions.name: Alethi highprinces
factions.summary: Ten princedoms whose competition, gemheart economy, and warcamps dominate the Shattered Plains. Dalinar’s reforms challenge their incentives.

factions.name: Sadeas principality
factions.summary: Military-political bloc built around Torol and Ialai Sadeas; after Torol’s death, Amaram takes military command and the army eventually falls to the Thrill.

factions.name: Vorin Ardentia
factions.summary: Nominally enslaved priestly order handling scholarship, engineering, monasteries, and doctrine. Individual ardents range from sincere caregivers to political actors.

factions.name: The Heralds
factions.summary: Ten Cognitive Shadows who carried Honorblades and upheld the Oathpact. Nine abandoned Taln at Aharietiam; millennia of strain have left all encountered Heralds psychologically damaged.

factions.name: Honorspren
factions.summary: Sapient spren associated with Honor and Windrunners. Modern honorspren distrust humans because of the Recreance; Syl’s bond is politically contentious.
goals: Preserve honor as understood by their society

status.label: Maya’s testimony forces Lasting Integrity to reconsider the claim that humans alone caused the Recreance

factions.name: Cryptics
factions.summary: Pattern-like sapient spren attracted to complex truths and lies, serving as Lightweaver bond partners.

factions.name: Cultivationspren
factions.summary: Vine-like sapient spren that bond Edgedancers. Wyndle’s circle selected Lift under unusual Cultivation-linked circumstances.

factions.name: Inkspren
factions.summary: Orderly sapient spren associated with Elsecallers; Ivory’s bond with Jasnah is exceptional and closely guarded.

factions.name: The Sleepless
factions.summary: Dysian Aimians composed of hordelings. They protect Aimia and dangerous secrets, observing Radiants through ordinary-looking cremlings.

factions.name: Thaylenah
factions.summary: Maritime trading kingdom centered on Thaylen City, ruled by Queen Fen and connected to Urithiru by Oathgate.

factions.name: Azir
factions.summary: Bureaucratic imperial center where written process and viziers constrain the Prime. Gawx’s unlikely accession links Lift to high politics.

factions.name: Kharbranth
factions.summary: Hospital and scholarly city ruled by Taravangian, home to the Palanaeum and the hidden Death Rattle project.

factions.name: Kholinar resistance
factions.summary: Wall Guard, palace loyalists, and civilians resisting singer occupation and Unmade influence under Azure and the infiltrating Kholin team.

factions.name: Worldhoppers
factions.summary: Individuals able to travel between worlds, usually through the Cognitive Realm. Not a single aligned faction.

factions.name: Seventeenth Shard
factions.summary: Noninterventionist-leaning travelers searching for Hoid on Roshar, represented in TWoK by three Purelake visitors.

factions.name: Nalthian connection
factions.summary: Characters and magic originating in Warbreaker’s world of Nalthis who appear under new roles on Roshar.
goals: Individual goals: retrieve Nightblood, avoid old conflicts, survive

factions.name: Aimia / Aimian peoples
factions.summary: Umbrella for Siah and Dysian Aimians and the ruined island nation.

factions.name: Alethkar
factions.summary: Alethi kingdom and its civil institutions outside a particular house.

factions.name: Amaram’s army
factions.summary: Army in which Kaladin served before Amaram’s betrayal.

factions.name: Shalash’s hired agents
factions.summary: Temporary thieves and helpers hired around Shalash’s destruction of art.

factions.name: Cultivation-aligned powers
factions.summary: Cultivation, the Nightwatcher, and interventions serving long-term growth.

factions.name: Graves’s Diagram cell
factions.summary: Diagram faction that recruits Moash for Elhokar’s assassination.

factions.name: Hearthstone community
factions.summary: Human and singer residents around Kaladin’s home town.

factions.name: Herdaz
factions.summary: Herdazian people and resistance networks.

factions.name: Honor-aligned legacy
factions.summary: Honor’s surviving systems: oaths, spren, Stormfather, Honorblades, and Radiants.

factions.name: House Davar
factions.summary: Shallan’s indebted and traumatized family, entangled with Ghostbloods.

factions.name: Independent actors
factions.summary: Entities whose goals do not fit one durable political alignment.

factions.name: Natanatan legacy
factions.summary: Ruined eastern civilization around Stormseat and the Shattered Plains.

factions.name: Navani’s artifabrians
factions.summary: Engineers and ardents supporting Kholin fabrial research.

factions.name: Oathgate network
factions.summary: Spren, platforms, and operators controlling Urithiru’s transport network.

factions.name: Purelake communities
factions.summary: Independent lake settlements and fishing culture.

factions.name: Reshi peoples
factions.summary: Communities living on and around greatshell islands.

factions.name: Rysn’s household
factions.summary: Rysn and companions including Chiri-Chiri.

factions.name: Sadeas’s army
factions.summary: Forces organized around expendable bridge tactics and later inherited by Amaram.

factions.name: Scadrian connection
factions.summary: People and systems originating on Scadrial.

factions.name: Sebarial principality
factions.summary: Sebarial and Palona’s commercially focused princedom.

factions.name: Selish connection
factions.summary: People and systems originating on Sel.

factions.name: Veil’s Urithiru network
factions.summary: Street contacts and helpers recruited by Shallan/Veil.

factions.name: Shallan’s retinue
factions.summary: Caravan survivors, deserters, and guards who become Shallan’s personnel.

factions.name: Silverlight scholars
factions.summary: Khriss, Nazh, and related Cosmere researchers.

factions.name: Skybreaker informants
factions.summary: Agents and contacts used to identify and prosecute emerging Surgebinders.

factions.name: Spren
factions.summary: General category for Roshar’s Cognitive entities.

factions.name: The Stump’s orphanage
factions.summary: Children and caretakers protected during Edgedancer.

factions.name: Taldain connection
factions.summary: People and Investiture from Taldain.

factions.name: Tukar
factions.summary: State ruled by Ishar under the identity Tezim.

factions.name: Tvlakv’s caravan
factions.summary: Slave and trade caravan later taken over by Shallan.

factions.name: Vstim’s merchant caravan
factions.summary: Thaylen trading operation that trains Rysn.

factions.name: Wind’s Pleasure crew
factions.summary: Tozbek’s sailors carrying Shallan and Jasnah.

factions.name: Ancient Knights Radiant
factions.summary: Radiants active before the Recreance.

factions.name: Knights Radiant
factions.summary: All ten Nahel-bonded orders collectively.

factions.name: Shin Stone Shamans
factions.summary: Shin institution that holds most Honorblades and enforces Truthless judgment.

factions.name: Alethi armies
factions.summary: Armies of Alethkar’s highprinces.

factions.name: Alethi soldiers
factions.summary: Soldiers and guards in Alethi forces.

factions.name: Shardbearers
factions.summary: People bonded to dead Shardblades and/or Shardplate.

factions.name: Szeth’s successive masters
factions.summary: People who possess Szeth’s Oathstone before the Diagram.

factions.name: Jah Keved armies
factions.summary: Veden military forces and elite Half-shard units.

factions.name: Urithiru scholars
factions.summary: Scribes and ardents translating the Dawnchant and gemstone archive.

factions.name: Coalition logistics
factions.summary: Operational staff of Dalinar’s coalition.

factions.name: Wandersail Expedition
factions.summary: Rysn’s sea expedition to Akinah, combining Thaylen sailors, scholars, Horneater support, and Windrunners under a deliberately negotiated charter.
goals: Investigate the lost expedition and Akinah Oathgate

status.label: Departs for Aimia aboard the Wandersail
Returns under a negotiated Sleepless cover story

factions.name: Urithiru Occupation Force
factions.summary: Raboniel’s Fused/singer strike force that inverts the tower defenses, suppresses most Radiants, and occupies Urithiru.

status.label: Captures the tower and disables most Radiants
Defeated when Navani bonds the Sibling and the tower reactivates

factions.name: Urithiru Resistance
