factions.summary: Loose network inside occupied Urithiru centered on Kaladin, Dabbid, Rlain, Teft, Navani’s hidden communications, civilians, and later sympathetic singers.
goals: Prevent complete corruption of the Sibling

status.label: Forms after the occupation
Succeeds as Urithiru is restored

factions.name: Lasting Integrity Envoy
factions.summary: Coalition mission led by Adolin and Shallan to persuade honorspren to bond new Windrunners, while Shallan secretly pursues Ghostblood objectives.
goals: Convince honorspren to renew Radiant bonds

status.label: Travels through Shadesmar
Trial outcome transforms the political argument about the Recreance

factions.name: Surviving Listeners
factions.summary: Listeners who escaped the Everstorm transformation and survived apart from Odium’s singer state. Their continued existence becomes Venli’s alternative to both human rule and Fused domination.
goals: Build a future outside Odium’s control

status.label: Venli learns a surviving group exists on the Shattered Plains
Venli and allied Fused depart to find them

factions.name: Unseen Court
factions.summary: Shallan's Lightweaver organization, used for intelligence work and counterespionage while its members also confront Ghostblood infiltration.

status.label: Investigates Ialai and Ghostblood activity
Continues after Shallan rejects Mraize's assassination order

factions.name: Horneaters
factions.summary: People of the Horneater Peaks, including Cord and Rock; their culture and access to Cultivation's Perpendicularity give them unusual Cosmere relevance.

factions.name: Reshi Isles communities
factions.summary: Communities living on the greatshell islands of the Reshi Sea, represented in the Dawnshard expedition by Ral-na and Talik.

factions.name: Sja-anat’s enlightened spren
factions.summary: Spren changed by Sja-anat rather than simply destroyed, increasingly acting with independent agendas during Rhythm of War.

factions.name: Urithiru civilians
factions.summary: Noncombatants and workers living in Urithiru whose experience becomes central during the occupation and Kaladin’s resistance.

factions.name: Kaladin’s Mental-Health Clinic / Support Groups
factions.summary: Kaladin’s non-military Urithiru work combines surgery with structured group support for people suffering battle shock, depression, and institutional neglect.
goals: Find forms of protection beyond combat

status.label: Established before the occupation
Kaladin receives permission to continue developing the work

locations.name: Roshar
locations.summary: Storm-battered world and supercontinent shaped around east-to-west highstorms, spren ecology, gemstone economics, and the conflict among Honor, Cultivation, and Odium.

locations.name: Alethkar
locations.summary: Militarized Vorin kingdom unified by Gavilar. Its capital Kholinar falls to singer forces during Oathbringer.

locations.name: Kholinar
locations.summary: Alethkar’s capital, built around windblades and an Oathgate. In Oathbringer it is divided between singer occupation, the Wall Guard, palace loyalists, and Unmade influence.

locations.name: Hearthstone
locations.summary: Kaladin’s home town, governed by Roshone before the Desolation and occupied by newly awakened singers when Kaladin returns.

locations.name: Shattered Plains
locations.summary: Maze of plateaus and chasms around the ruins of Stormseat, site of the Alethi-listener war, gemheart hunts, bridge crews, and the Battle of Narak.

locations.name: Alethi warcamps
locations.summary: Ten highprince camps functioning as rival cities, linked to plateau assaults and political competition.

locations.name: The Tower
locations.summary: Large plateau where Sadeas abandons Dalinar’s army. Bridge Four returns to save the Kholins, transforming the political alliance.

locations.name: Narak / Stormseat
locations.summary: Listener center among ancient ruins and the location of an Oathgate. The Battle of Narak summons the Everstorm and sends the human army to Urithiru.

locations.name: Urithiru
locations.summary: Ancient Knights Radiant city, physically high in the mountains and connected by ten Oathgates. Becomes the coalition capital, though much of its machinery is dormant.

locations.name: Jah Keved
locations.summary: Veden kingdom and Shallan’s homeland. Civil war and Szeth’s assassinations allow Taravangian to take its crown.

locations.name: Vedenar
locations.summary: Capital of Jah Keved, devastated by succession violence and influenced by the Thrill during the kingdom’s collapse.

locations.name: Davar estate
locations.summary: Shallan’s childhood home and the setting of the Davar family flashbacks, hidden Shardblade trauma, abuse, and Ghostblood debt.

locations.name: Kharbranth
locations.summary: Vertical city of bells, hospitals, the Palanaeum, and Taravangian’s court. Shallan studies here under Jasnah.

locations.name: The Palanaeum
locations.summary: Vast underground library administered through fees and ardents; central to Jasnah and Shallan’s research into the Voidbringers.

locations.name: Diagram hospitals
locations.summary: Publicly charitable hospitals that secretly include rooms where terminal patients are killed to record Death Rattles.

locations.name: Thaylenah
locations.summary: Maritime merchant nation controlling major trade routes and an Oathgate.

locations.name: Thaylen City
locations.summary: Walled port city with a gemstone reserve and Oathgate. Site of Oathbringer’s climactic battle and Dalinar’s confrontation with Odium.

locations.name: Purelake
locations.summary: Warm, shallow lake culture where Ishikk meets three worldhoppers searching for Hoid.

locations.name: Shinovar
locations.summary: Sheltered western land with soil, ordinary plants, and cultural reverence for stone. Szeth’s homeland and a major Rysn trading destination.

locations.name: Azir
locations.summary: Bureaucratic imperial center of the Makabaki region, governed by a Prime selected through legal procedure.

locations.name: Azimir
locations.summary: Capital where Lift infiltrates a palace, saves Gawx, and inadvertently helps him become Prime.

locations.name: Yeddaw
locations.summary: Canal city cut into the ground, setting of Edgedancer. Lift investigates stolen food, the Stump’s orphanage, and Nale’s killings.

locations.name: Tashikk
locations.summary: Makabaki nation containing Yeddaw, culturally linked to trade, bureaucracy, and information networks.

locations.name: Herdaz
locations.summary: Herdazian homeland northwest of Alethkar, known for resistance fighters and Lopen’s vast extended family.

locations.name: Horneater Peaks
locations.summary: Volcanic mountain lakes and perpendicularity-associated region, homeland of Rock and a known route between realms.

locations.name: Iri
locations.summary: Western kingdom with distinct religion and culture; Axies is arrested here, and Iri’s rulers align with Odium by Oathbringer.

locations.name: Rira
locations.summary: Small western nation culturally related to Iri and Evi’s homeland.

locations.name: Reshi Isles
locations.summary: Living greatshell islands with distinctive rulers and customs. Rysn is injured here and receives Chiri-Chiri.

locations.name: Rall Elorim
locations.summary: Lift’s home city, called the City of Shadows. It is mostly background at this spoiler boundary.

locations.name: Aimia
locations.summary: Destroyed island nation guarded by the Sleepless, associated with both Siah and Dysian Aimians and dangerous hidden knowledge.

locations.name: Akinah
locations.summary: Ancient Aimian city hidden behind dangerous weather and Sleepless defenses. Its apparent Oathgate is a decoy; caverns below contain Shardplate, Soulcasters, and the mural housing the Dawnshard that bonds Rysn.

locations.name: Tukar
locations.summary: Kingdom ruled by Ishar as Tezim. Dalinar’s party confronts Ishar here and discovers evidence of his experiments forcing spren into Physical bodies.

locations.name: Emul
locations.summary: Primary coalition military front during much of Rhythm of War, where Dalinar, Jasnah, the Mink, and Azish forces fight while Urithiru is left comparatively exposed.

locations.name: Marat
locations.summary: Region used by Odium’s forces as a staging area where Venli serves the Fused before Thaylen Field.

locations.name: Babatharnam
locations.summary: Makabaki-area nation known through interludes and trade; peripheral to the main first-three-book plot.

locations.name: Tu Bayla
locations.summary: Central Rosharan nation referenced in geopolitics and travel.

locations.name: Natanatan
locations.summary: Ancient kingdom whose lands include the Shattered Plains and Stormseat ruins.

locations.name: New Natanan / Origin coast
locations.summary: Eastern coast facing the mythical Origin of storms; Puuli keeps a lighthouse here.

locations.name: Frostlands
locations.summary: Harsh territory crossed by Shallan’s caravan en route to the Shattered Plains.

locations.name: Valley of the Nightwatcher
locations.summary: Remote valley where petitioners seek the Nightwatcher. Dalinar instead meets Cultivation, who removes and later restores selected memories.

locations.name: Rathalas / the Rift
locations.summary: Rebellious city destroyed by Dalinar during Alethkar’s unification. Evi dies in the fire, the central suppressed event of Oathbringer’s flashbacks.

locations.name: Feverstone Keep
locations.summary: Location in Dalinar’s vision where ancient Radiants abandon Shards during the Recreance. Its exact modern position is not established in the books.

locations.name: Stormseat
locations.summary: Ancient city whose shattered remains are Narak and the central Plains ruins; linked to an Oathgate and Radiant history.

locations.name: Celebrant
locations.summary: Major Cognitive Realm market city visited by the stranded Kholinar team while seeking passage toward Thaylen City.

locations.name: Riino’s lighthouse
locations.summary: Cognitive Realm lighthouse where the travelers meet Riino and use a fortune-reading device.

locations.name: Sea of Souls
locations.summary: Shadesmar’s dark bead ocean, where beads represent Physical objects and solid land corresponds broadly to Physical water.

locations.name: Honor’s Path
locations.summary: Notum’s ship carrying Kaladin, Shallan, Adolin, Azure, Pattern, and Syl toward Celebrant.

locations.name: Shadesmar
locations.summary: Roshar’s Cognitive Realm: obsidian-like land, bead oceans, spren cities, and routes used by Elsecallers and worldhoppers.

locations.name: Braize
locations.summary: Planet called Damnation in Rosharan religion, where Heralds and Fused were bound between Desolations.

locations.name: Ashyn
locations.summary: Humans’ original Rosharan-system world, later remembered as the Tranquiline Halls. Oathbringer’s Dawnchant translation reveals humanity arrived on Roshar as refugees after destroying Ashyn through uncontrolled powers.

locations.name: Nalthis
locations.summary: World of Warbreaker, Breath, Awakening, Returned, Vasher/Zahel, Vivenna/Azure, and Nightblood.

locations.name: Scadrial
locations.summary: World of Mistborn and metal-based magic; origin of Felt and Demoux.

locations.name: Sel
locations.summary: World of Elantris and The Emperor’s Soul; origin of Galladon and Riino.

locations.name: Taldain
locations.summary: World/system of White Sand; origin of Baon and the invested sand used as a detector in Oathbringer.

locations.name: Silverlight
locations.summary: Scholarly worldhopper center associated with Khriss and Nazh; background knowledge available through Arcanum Unbounded rather than a Stormlight plot location.

locations.name: Threnody
locations.summary: Setting of Shadows for Silence; included for chronological Cosmere context, not a direct Oathbringer dependency.

locations.name: First of the Sun
locations.summary: Setting of Sixth of the Dusk; included as pre-Oathbringer Cosmere context.

locations.name: Kholinar palace
locations.summary: Royal palace corrupted by Yelig-nar and the setting of Elhokar’s death during the failed Oathgate operation.

locations.name: Heart of the Revel
locations.summary: Ashertmarn’s zone of compulsive indulgence surrounding the city’s Oathgate platform.

locations.name: Urithiru lower markets
locations.summary: Refugee and working districts where Veil builds informant networks and where Re-Shephir’s murders emerge.

locations.name: Urithiru gemstone archive
locations.summary: Hidden gemstone records left by ancient Radiants, containing firsthand concerns about the orders, the False Desolation, and the Recreance.

locations.name: Sea of Storms
locations.summary: Storm-lashed southern ocean crossed by the Wind’s Pleasure and other trade vessels.

locations.name: Kasitor Bay
locations.summary: Iri location where Cusicesh manifests on a regular schedule and Axies attempts to study it.

locations.name: The Cosmere
locations.summary: Shared setting containing Roshar, Nalthis, Scadrial, Sel, Taldain, and other worlds.

locations.name: Lasting Integrity
locations.summary: Honorspren stronghold in Shadesmar, isolationist after the Recreance. Adolin’s diplomatic mission and trial take place here, with Kalak serving as High Judge.

locations.name: Urithiru Crystal Pillar
locations.summary: Gemstone/fabrial heart of Urithiru and physical locus of the Sibling’s systems. Raboniel corrupts it with Voidlight; Navani later restores the Sibling through a Bondsmith bond and Towerlight.

locations.name: Nameless
locations.summary: A Shadesmar settlement used as a waypoint by Adolin, Shallan, and the envoy en route to Lasting Integrity.

magic.name: Investiture
magic.summary: The common substrate of Cosmere magic: spiritual power expressed differently by world, Shard, intent, and access method.
limits: Cannot be treated as unlimited energy
Its behavior depends on Identity, Connection, Intent, and local systems

magic.name: Three Realms
magic.summary: Reality has Physical, Cognitive, and Spiritual aspects. Shadesmar is Roshar’s Cognitive Realm; bonds, Identity, Connection, and Shardic power involve Spiritual structure.

magic.name: Stormlight
magic.summary: Investiture carried by highstorms and stored in cut gemstones. Radiants inhale it for healing, physical enhancement, and Surgebinding; it leaks from imperfect containers.
limits: Leaks from ordinary gemstones and bodies
Use is constrained by bond, oath, skill, and available gems

magic.name: Voidlight
magic.summary: Odium-aligned Investiture used by the Fused, Regals, and some voidspren-linked systems. It has a different feel and visual signature from Stormlight.
limits: Access generally depends on Odium-aligned bonds or supply

magic.name: Highstorm recharge
magic.summary: East-to-west storms recharge exposed gemstones with Stormlight. The Stormfather is the storm’s great spren and the cycle underpins Roshar’s economy and ecology.
limits: Physically catastrophic without shelter
Timing and geography matter

magic.name: Everstorm
magic.summary: Storm moving west-to-east, summoned at Narak. It restores singer minds, supplies transformations, and permits Fused returns without waiting for the old Desolation cycle.
limits: Regularly circles the world but differs from highstorms

magic.name: Nahel bond
magic.summary: A mutual bond between sapient spren and human or singer that grants Surges, Shardblade access, and increasing integration as truths or Ideals progress.
limits: Broken oaths can wound or kill the spren
Capabilities depend on order and progression

magic.name: Radiant Ideals and truths
magic.summary: Spiritual commitments that structure Radiant growth. Most orders speak ordered Ideals; Lightweavers advance through difficult personal truths.
limits: Words require genuine intent and acceptance
Exact forms vary by order

magic.name: Adhesion
magic.summary: Surge of pressure and binding, used by Windrunners for Full Lashings and by Bondsmiths in deeper forms involving Connection.
limits: Bondsmith expression differs from ordinary Windrunner use

magic.name: Gravitation
magic.summary: Changes the direction and strength of apparent gravity. Windrunners and Skybreakers use it for Basic and Reverse Lashings, flight, and projectile control.
limits: Consumes Stormlight/Voidlight
Momentum and training still matter

magic.name: Division
magic.summary: Breaks, burns, or degrades matter. Associated with Skybreakers and Dustbringers; used sparingly or indirectly in the books through Oathbringer.
limits: Dangerous and often gated by order progression

magic.name: Abrasion
magic.summary: Controls friction. Edgedancers use it to become nearly frictionless; Dustbringers share the Surge with different order emphasis.
limits: Low friction reduces control as well as resistance

magic.name: Progression
magic.summary: Manipulates biological growth and healing. Regrowth can restore recent injuries within spiritual constraints; Edgedancers and Truthwatchers use it.
limits: Not simple resurrection
Healing follows the target’s Spiritual self-image and available power

magic.name: Illumination
magic.summary: Manipulates light, sound, and waveform-like information. Lightweavers create complex illusions; Truthwatcher expression is less clearly understood by Oathbringer.
limits: Convincing illusions require observation, memory, and power

magic.name: Transformation
magic.summary: Soulcasting: persuading or forcing matter’s Cognitive aspect to become another substance. Shared by Lightweavers and Elsecallers.
limits: Requires skill, Stormlight, and negotiation or command of Cognitive identity
Repeated fabrial use can transform the user

magic.name: Transportation
magic.summary: Movement between Physical and Cognitive Realms. Elsecallers use it directly; Willshapers share the Surge, though Venli is only beginning her bond.
limits: Realm transitions require power, location, and expertise

magic.name: Cohesion
magic.summary: Manipulates the strong axial connections within solid matter, associated with Willshapers and Stonewards. Mostly historical or theoretical in this cutoff.
limits: Detailed modern use is not yet established

magic.name: Tension
magic.summary: Manipulates the stiffness of materials, associated with Stonewards and Bondsmiths. Dalinar’s bond hints at applications, but the system remains incompletely demonstrated.
limits: Detailed boundaries remain uncertain by Oathbringer

magic.name: Lashings
magic.summary: Rosharan terminology for Gravitation and Adhesion techniques: Basic Lashings redirect gravity; Full Lashings bind surfaces; Reverse Lashings draw nearby objects.
limits: Require Investiture and control
Multiple Lashings compound effects

magic.name: Lightweaving
magic.summary: Illusions woven from light and sound, often anchored to drawings, memories, or a chosen identity. Shallan can combine images and later coordinate many illusions at once.
limits: Mental coherence and truthful observation affect quality

magic.name: Soulcasting
magic.summary: Transformation of material into another Essence. Jasnah performs it directly; Shallan learns; ancient Soulcaster fabrials allow non-Radiants to specialize at severe long-term bodily cost.
limits: Substances have Cognitive resistance
Fabrial users tend toward the transformed substance

magic.name: Elsecalling
magic.summary: Jasnah’s use of Transportation to enter or exit Shadesmar, often paired with precise Soulcasting and Cognitive navigation.
limits: Dangerous without preparation, Stormlight, and a route back

magic.name: Regrowth
magic.summary: Progression-based healing applied to another person, used by Lift, Renarin, and hidden Truthwatchers.
limits: Works best before injury becomes integrated into self-image
Consumes substantial Investiture

magic.name: Connection manipulation
magic.summary: Spiritual relationships among people, places, languages, and powers. Dalinar can temporarily forge linguistic understanding and unify realms in ways tied to Connection.
limits: Broad effects are exceptional and poorly understood

magic.name: Stormlight self-healing
magic.summary: Stormlight repairs a Radiant according to Spiritual identity, including old wounds when the person no longer accepts them as defining.
limits: Identity can preserve scars or disability
Power and time limit recovery

magic.name: Living Shardblade
magic.summary: A sufficiently advanced Radiant spren can become a weapon or tool instantly and in changing shapes, unlike dead Shardblades’ delayed summoning.
limits: Depends on a healthy bond

magic.name: Dead Shardblade
magic.summary: Corpse-like Physical manifestation of a spren whose Radiant broke oaths during the Recreance. Gemstones added later enable bonding and ten-heartbeat summoning.
limits: Screams can be heard by bonded Radiants
Cannot freely change shape

magic.name: Shardplate
magic.summary: Ancient powered armor that enhances strength and resists damage, recharged by Stormlight gemstones. Its full relationship to Radiant bonds is not yet explained by Oathbringer.
limits: Cracked sections consume Stormlight to regrow
Interferes with some Lashings

magic.name: Oathgate travel
magic.summary: Paired spren and platforms teleport groups between Urithiru and ten cities. A living Shardblade normally unlocks the mechanism.
limits: Spren can refuse, redirect, or be corrupted
Most routes depend on control of both endpoints

magic.name: Fabrials
magic.summary: Devices using trapped spren and gemstone configurations to create repeatable effects such as communication, heating, pain reduction, detection, or paired motion.
limits: Gem type, metal, cut, spren, and alignment change behavior
Stormlight supply is required

magic.name: Spanreeds
magic.summary: Paired writing reeds whose movement is conjoined at distance, enabling written communication when aligned and supplied with Stormlight.
limits: Need coordinated setup and stable surfaces
Range and motion constraints apply

magic.name: Painrial
magic.summary: Fabrial that reduces or transfers the perception of pain without repairing underlying injury.
limits: Can hide dangerous damage
Does not heal

magic.name: Conjoiner fabrials
magic.summary: Paired gemstones that reproduce motion in linked ways, foundation of spanreeds and Navani’s transport experiments.
limits: Direction, distance, and mass introduce engineering problems

magic.name: Soulcaster fabrials
magic.summary: Ancient devices shaped like hand ornaments that grant narrow Transformation capabilities to non-Radiants. Modern artifabrians cannot reproduce them.
limits: Long use transforms the body
Often limited to specific Essences

magic.name: Half-shards
magic.summary: Shields reinforced by fabrials enough to block several Shardblade strikes, developed in Jah Keved and used by elite troops.
limits: Far weaker than Shardplate and eventually break

magic.name: Perfect gemstones
magic.summary: Exceptionally cut gemstones that leak little or no Stormlight and can imprison powerful spren. The King’s Drop is the key example.
limits: Rare and strategically valuable

magic.name: Singer forms
magic.summary: Singers take different forms by bonding spren in their gemhearts during highstorms, changing body, temperament, skills, and accessible rhythms.
limits: Form influences but does not erase agency
Suitable spren and transformation conditions are required

magic.name: Rhythms of Roshar
magic.summary: Perceived rhythms used by singers to express emotion, coordinate, and interpret experience. Forms of power introduce new Odium-aligned rhythms.
limits: Humans generally do not hear them naturally

magic.name: Forms of power / Regals
magic.summary: Singer forms gained by bonding voidspren, granting abilities such as stormform lightning and linking the user to Odium’s rhythms and influence.
limits: Can strongly shape emotion and loyalty
Not identical to Fused reincarnation

magic.name: Fused Surgebinding
magic.summary: Fused use one specialized Surge-like ability per type, powered by Voidlight and refined across repeated lives.
limits: Each brand specializes rather than combining two Surges like Radiant orders

magic.name: Old Magic
magic.summary: Boon-and-curse encounters associated with the Nightwatcher. Cultivation sometimes intervenes directly for more deliberate long-term changes.
limits: Outcomes are personal and not safely predictable

magic.name: Cultivation’s memory pruning
magic.summary: Cultivation removes Dalinar’s memory of Evi and then arranges for it to return gradually, giving him time to become someone able to face it.
limits: Not a simple permanent erasure

magic.name: Awakening
magic.summary: Using Breath, color, visualization, and Commands to animate objects. Azure demonstrates it in Kholinar and Shadesmar; Zahel’s identity links the system to Warbreaker.
limits: Usually consumes color and requires Breath plus precise Intent/Command

magic.name: BioChromatic Breath
magic.summary: Transferable unit of innate Investiture on Nalthis. Large quantities grant Heightenings; Returned require a continuing supply. Zahel adapts to Roshar’s Stormlight ecosystem.
limits: Normally transferred by willing Command
Breath and Stormlight are not operationally identical

magic.name: Nightblood’s consumption
magic.summary: When drawn, Nightblood consumes the wielder’s available Investiture, then life, while destroying matter and spiritual structure with extreme force.
limits: Dangerous to wielder and surroundings
Moral judgment is naïve and command-bound

magic.name: Allomancy
magic.summary: Metal-burning magic from Mistborn. Included as background for Scadrian worldhoppers; no overt Allomantic set piece is required to understand Oathbringer.
limits: Specific metals produce specific effects

magic.name: Feruchemy
magic.summary: Stores personal attributes in metalminds for later retrieval. Useful background for Cosmere Identity and Connection discussions.
limits: Requires storing before tapping

magic.name: Hemalurgy
magic.summary: Transfers spiritual attributes using metal spikes at severe moral and spiritual cost. Included only as pre-2017 Cosmere context.
limits: Requires damaging souls and creates vulnerabilities

magic.name: Invested white sand
magic.summary: Sand from Taldain changes appearance when it absorbs nearby Investiture, making it useful as a detector. A jar in Oathbringer helps reveal anomalous activity.
limits: Must be recharged by suitable Investiture/light conditions

magic.name: Fortune
magic.summary: Spiritual mechanism associated with glimpsing or positioning oneself toward possible futures. Riino’s device and Odium/Renarin future sight imply distinct applications.
limits: Future sight is probabilistic and mutually interfering

magic.name: Death Rattles
magic.summary: Cryptic statements spoken near death under Moelach’s influence, gathered systematically by Taravangian’s secret hospitals.
limits: Fragmentary, metaphorical, and ethically obtained through murder in the Diagram project

magic.name: The Thrill
magic.summary: Nergaoul’s enhancement of aggression, pleasure in combat, and loss of inhibition. Alethi culture mistakes it for normal warrior experience until Dalinar identifies the source.
limits: Can be resisted through recognition and choice
Can overwhelm armies

magic.name: Midnight Essence
magic.summary: Black imitative creatures formed by Re-Shephir to copy violence and anatomy she observes.
limits: Imitative rather than truly alive
Controlled through the Unmade

magic.name: Oathpact
magic.summary: Ancient agreement binding Heralds and Fused to a cycle involving Braize. Nine Heralds abandon it at Aharietiam, leaving Taln alone to maintain the barrier.
limits: Broken and weakened by abandonment

magic.name: Desolation cycle
magic.summary: Repeated wars triggered when Heralds returned from Braize and Fused followed. The Everstorm creates a new route that no longer depends on the old timing.
limits: Historical records are distorted by millennia

magic.name: Gemstones and polestones
magic.summary: Cut gemstones store Stormlight; gem type, cut, and trapped spren determine many fabrial and Soulcasting properties.
limits: Ordinary cuts leak Stormlight

magic.name: Ten Essences
magic.summary: Vorin-linked material categories used in Soulcasting theory, each associated with properties, gemstones, and Heraldic symbolism.
limits: Classification is culturally useful rather than a complete chemistry

magic.name: Dawnshard / Command
magic.summary: One of the ancient Commands associated with the deepest pre-Shattering history of the Cosmere. In Akinah, a Dawnshard leaves its mural and bonds Rysn, changing her perception and making her strategically important far beyond Roshar.
limits: The Sleepless insist Rysn must not become a Radiant while bearing it
Its full capabilities are not explained by the Rhythm of War boundary

magic.name: Lifelight
magic.summary: Cultivation-associated Light. Lift metabolizes food into Lifelight rather than drawing ordinary Stormlight, and the Sibling combines Cultivation’s tone with Honor’s to create Towerlight.
limits: Distinct tone/rhythm from Stormlight and Voidlight

magic.name: Towerlight
magic.summary: The Sibling’s native hybrid Investiture, created from the tones/powers of Honor and Cultivation. Navani and the Sibling restore it when they form their Bondsmith bond.
limits: Tied to the Sibling and Urithiru’s systems

magic.name: Warlight
magic.summary: Stable mixture of Stormlight and Voidlight created when Navani and Raboniel bring Honor’s and Odium’s tones/rhythms into harmony. Its creation disproves Raboniel’s assumption that the Lights must annihilate one another.
limits: Requires correct tone/rhythm and controlled transfer

magic.name: Pure Tones of Roshar
magic.summary: Fundamental tones associated with Roshar’s Shards and their Lights. Navani’s research shows Light responds to tone and rhythm, allowing transfer, mixing, inversion, and eventually anti-Light production.
limits: Requires precision and Intent; different Lights resonate with different tones

magic.name: Anti-Light
magic.summary: Investiture placed into a phase/opposition corresponding to a Light’s tone. When Light and its anti-Light meet through the correct medium, the reaction can annihilate Investiture and permanently kill normally returning Fused or bonded spren.
limits: Must be created from the matching Light
Dangerous explosive interaction
Weaponization requires specialized delivery

magic.name: Anti-Voidlight
magic.summary: Anti-phase counterpart to Odium’s Voidlight, first deliberately produced by Navani. It can force reactions with Voidlight and permanently destroy a Fused soul when delivered effectively.
limits: Highly dangerous in contact with Voidlight

magic.name: Anti-Stormlight
magic.summary: Anti-phase counterpart to Stormlight. Raboniel applies Navani’s method to produce it; it enables the permanent killing of spren and is demonstrated against Phendorana and later Lezian’s Investiture.
limits: Highly dangerous in contact with Stormlight/spren Investiture

magic.name: Raysium conduction
magic.summary: Odium-associated metal used in specialized daggers to conduct Investiture between a target and gemstone, making it central to Jezrien-style capture weapons and anti-Light delivery.
limits: Rare
Direction depends on weapon construction

magic.name: Radiant suppression fabrials
magic.summary: Devices using corrupted spren and principles related to Urithiru’s defenses to suppress Radiant powers. Study of a captured device helps Navani understand the tower’s vulnerability.
limits: Different Radiant powers are suppressed unevenly
Urithiru’s integrated system is much larger and more complex

magic.name: Sibling-integrated fabrials
magic.summary: Urithiru itself functions as a vast living fabrial complex through the Sibling: pressure, heat, water, lighting, defenses, communications, and power suppression are integrated into the tower.
limits: Dependent on the Sibling’s health and bond
Can be corrupted/inverted

magic.name: Fabrial metal interactions
magic.summary: Rhythm of War makes explicit that metals placed around trapped spren alter fabrial behavior in systematic ways; aluminum can block or isolate effects, and other metals push/pull or otherwise modify responses.
limits: Behavior depends on metal, geometry, spren, and gemstone

magic.name: Living Shardplate
magic.summary: At the Fourth Ideal, Kaladin gains Shardplate formed from windspren. The living Plate can move between people under his intent, contrasting with dead traditional Plate.
limits: Requires advanced oath progression and associated lesser spren
examples: Kaladin protecting Lirin, Dabbid, and others

magic.name: Enlightened spren
magic.summary: Spren altered by Sja-anat retain agency while changing nature and capabilities. Renarin’s Glys and Rlain’s Tumi demonstrate Radiant bonds with enlightened spren that can disturb Odium’s future sight.
limits: Individual spren choose whether to accept Sja-anat’s change

items.name: Oathbringer
items.summary: Dalinar’s famous dead Shardblade, won during his youth and named for his reputation. He trades it to Sadeas for Bridge Four; it later passes to Amaram. Dalinar ultimately refuses to wield it as he confronts what the name once meant.

status.label: Won by Dalinar in single combat
Given to Sadeas in exchange for every bridgeman
Given by Sadeas to Amaram
Dalinar summons it only through extraordinary circumstances to escape a vision, then rejects possession

items.name: Mayalaran / Adolin’s Blade
items.summary: Adolin’s dead Shardblade, later identified in Shadesmar as the cultivationspren Mayalaran. His habit of speaking to and respecting the Blade precedes unusual responsiveness.

status.label: Bonded dead Blade with ten-heartbeat summon
Seen as deadeye Mayalaran
Summons in fewer than ten heartbeats when Adolin desperately asks

items.name: Sunraiser
items.summary: Elhokar’s ornate Shardblade, carried as the king’s weapon through the Shattered Plains and Kholinar mission.

items.name: Helaran’s Shardblade
items.summary: Blade carried by Helaran during his attack on Amaram’s army. After Kaladin kills him, Amaram murders Kaladin’s surviving squad, steals the Blade, and pretends to have won it.

status.label: Helaran carries it with Shardplate
Claimed by Amaram after his betrayal

items.name: Sylblade
items.summary: Syl’s ability to become weapons and tools once Kaladin reaches the required bond level. She shifts shape rapidly rather than remaining a fixed sword.

items.name: Patternblade
items.summary: Pattern’s weapon form. Shallan’s relationship to multiple childhood memories makes the exact history emotionally complicated, but by WoR Pattern can act as her living Blade.

items.name: Ivory’s Blade form
items.summary: Ivory’s living weapon manifestation for Jasnah, with the adaptable properties of a healthy Nahel bond.

items.name: Wyndle’s Blade form
items.summary: Wyndle reluctantly manifests as a weapon/tool for Lift, often shaped into a fork-like form to suit her reluctance to kill.

items.name: Jezrien’s Honorblade
items.summary: Ancient Blade granting Adhesion and Gravitation without a spren bond. Szeth wields it as Truthless until Kaladin defeats him at Narak; it then comes into Kholin possession.

status.label: Abandoned at Aharietiam with the other Honorblades
Wielded by Szeth under the Oathstone system
Recovered after Szeth’s defeat

items.name: Blade carried by Taln
items.summary: Taln arrives in Kholinar carrying a Blade that is later swapped before Dalinar receives it. The identity and chain of custody remain deliberately unresolved within Oathbringer.

items.name: Nightblood
items.summary: Sentient Nalthian sword created to destroy evil, with catastrophic Investiture consumption. It passes from Nale to Szeth and is used at Thaylen Field.

items.name: Azure’s sword
items.summary: A distinctive silvery weapon used by Azure. It is not a conventional Rosharan Shardblade; its behavior and origin connect to Nalthian experimentation, though details remain unrevealed by Oathbringer.

items.name: Gavilar’s black sphere
items.summary: Dark, violet-black gemstone Gavilar gives Szeth while dying, asking that it be kept from 'them.' It contains unfamiliar light associated with Odium’s forces; deeper technical explanation belongs beyond this spoiler boundary.

items.name: The King’s Drop
items.summary: Huge, exceptionally cut ruby in Thaylenah’s reserve. It stores Investiture without leakage; Rysn protects it and Dalinar uses it to imprison Nergaoul.

status.label: Target of Fused infiltration
Recovered and used as Nergaoul’s prison

items.name: Jezrien-killing dagger
items.summary: Special knife with a gemstone pommel supplied by Odium’s forces. Moash uses it to kill Jezrien and capture or disrupt the Herald’s essence.

items.name: Szeth’s Oathstone
items.summary: Ordinary stone invested with cultural authority rather than magical compulsion. Szeth believes Truthless law requires absolute obedience to its holder.

status.label: Passed among masters who command assassinations
Its authority collapses when Szeth accepts he was never Truthless

items.name: Adolin’s Shardplate
items.summary: Kholin Shardplate used in hunts, duels, and war. Damaged segments can be regrown with Stormlight.

items.name: Dalinar’s Shardplate
items.summary: Blackthorn-era and modern battle armor associated with Dalinar. He increasingly rejects personal Shardbearing as his Bondsmith role develops.

items.name: Helaran’s Shardplate
items.summary: Plate worn by Helaran during the battlefield attack where Kaladin kills him; stolen along with the Blade by Amaram.

items.name: Shardbows
items.summary: Oversized bows normally requiring Shardplate strength. Rock uses one without Plate at Thaylen Field to kill Amaram, assisted by his unusual Horneater strength and position.

items.name: The Way of Kings
items.summary: Nohadon’s moral-political text. Gavilar’s final message directs Dalinar to it; Dalinar tries to shape his rule around its principles despite uncertainty about their historical application.

items.name: Words of Radiance
items.summary: In-world history of the Knights Radiant, used by Jasnah and Shallan and quoted in epigraphs to recover order structure and Urithiru clues.

items.name: Oathbringer: My Glory and My Shame
items.summary: Dalinar’s autobiographical work, dictated and written publicly without a feminine undertext, confronting the Blackthorn’s crimes and arguing that responsibility begins by owning pain rather than surrendering it.

items.name: The Diagram
items.summary: Enormous collection of instructions, deductions, and diagrams dictated by Taravangian on his most intelligent day, then interpreted by a secret organization.

items.name: Mythica
items.summary: Jasnah-associated text cataloging the Unmade, used by the coalition to identify phenomena such as the Midnight Mother and the Thrill.

items.name: Dawnchant translations
items.summary: Ancient language decoded through Urithiru scholarship. Its records reveal humans came from Ashyn and were the original invaders relative to the singers.

items.name: Urithiru gemstone archive
items.summary: Gemstones carrying ancient Radiant messages, each recorded in a gemstone associated with the speaker’s order. They document internal doubts before the Recreance and the danger of Ba-Ado-Mishram.

items.name: Listener songs
items.summary: Rhythm-preserved songs carrying listener history, forms, warnings, and fragmented knowledge of old gods and humans.

items.name: Shallan’s sketchbooks
items.summary: Drawings used for scholarship, memory, emotional insight, disguise design, and Lightweaving. They often capture truths Shallan consciously avoids.

items.name: Wit’s flute
items.summary: Flute Wit gives Kaladin after a story. Kaladin loses or abandons it during his transition from the warcamps, making it a symbol of neglected parts of himself.

items.name: Jasnah’s Soulcaster decoy
items.summary: Fabrial-like ornament Jasnah wears to conceal that she Soulcasts through a Nahel bond. Shallan steals and damages it before learning it was a decoy.

items.name: Davar Soulcaster
items.summary: Broken Soulcaster tied to House Davar’s Ghostblood debt. Shallan hopes Jasnah’s apparent device can replace it and restore the family’s finances.

items.name: Coalition spanreed network
items.summary: Paired writing devices used for politics, intelligence, and logistics across Roshar before and alongside Oathgate travel.

items.name: Navani’s painrial
items.summary: Portable pain-reduction device used in medical and battlefield situations. It suppresses sensation rather than healing damage.

items.name: Jar of white sand
items.summary: Offworld sand that changes when exposed to Investiture, used as an alarm or diagnostic clue in Urithiru.

items.name: Aluminum-lined materials
items.summary: Rare offworld-linked metal that blocks or interferes with several magical effects. Oathbringer uses it in covert and protective contexts without fully systematizing the science.

items.name: Oathgate platforms
items.summary: Ten city platforms and the central Urithiru controls, each governed by paired spren and activated through Shardblade interfaces.

items.name: The Honorblades
items.summary: Ten Blades given to the Heralds by Honor, granting Surges without spren bonds at greater Stormlight cost. Most are held in Shinovar after Aharietiam.

items.name: Half-shard shields
items.summary: Fabrial-reinforced shields that can survive limited Shardblade impacts, fielded by elite Veden/Alethi troops.

items.name: Soulcast blood antidote
items.summary: Jasnah transforms Shallan’s blood to remove poison after the failed Kabsal attack, demonstrating precise biological Soulcasting.

items.name: Bridge crews and mobile bridges
items.summary: Heavy bridges carried by expendable enslaved crews to span chasms under fire, central to Sadeas’s tactics and Bridge Four’s trauma.

items.name: Gemstone Shardbearer bond set
items.summary: Gemstone and ritual apparatus used to bond dead Shardblades for summoning; a later human adaptation rather than part of original living Radiant bonds.

items.name: Akinah Dawnshard mural
items.summary: Ancient mural/container in Akinah that houses a Dawnshard Command until it leaves the artwork and bonds Rysn.

status.label: Dawnshard leaves the mural and bonds Rysn

items.name: Wandersail (Rysn’s ship)
items.summary: Rysn’s Thaylen vessel, adapted for her mobility and used for the expedition to Akinah.

status.label: Carries the Akinah expedition
Returns safely under the Sleepless compact

items.name: Rhythm of War notebook
items.summary: Joint scientific notebook of Navani and Raboniel documenting Light, tones, Warlight, and anti-Light. Copies allow both sides to retain the discoveries.

status.label: Co-authored during Navani’s captivity
Research survives the liberation in copies on both sides

items.name: Anti-Voidlight dagger
items.summary: Raysium-assisted dagger configuration carrying anti-Voidlight, capable of permanently killing Fused rather than merely sending them back to Braize.

status.label: Weapon principle demonstrated on Raboniel’s daughter
Navani uses one to grant Raboniel permanent death

items.name: Anti-Stormlight dagger
items.summary: Weaponized anti-Stormlight delivery system. Moash uses it to permanently kill Phendorana; El later applies the research against Lezian.

status.label: Used against Phendorana
Principle demonstrated again by El against Lezian

items.name: Kaladin’s fabrial flight glove
items.summary: Navani-designed conjoiner-based glove that gives Kaladin limited directional lift while Urithiru suppresses his Gravitation, allowing him to move through and outside the tower.

status.label: Issued during the occupation and used in resistance operations

items.name: Captured Radiant suppressor
items.summary: Portable Fused suppression device captured early in Rhythm of War. Navani studies its corrupted-spren construction and notices parallels to Urithiru’s gemstone pillar.

status.label: Captured after the Hearthstone operation
Studied in Urithiru, revealing structural parallels to the tower

items.name: Cord’s Akinah Shardplate
items.summary: Ancient Shardplate recovered from Akinah and claimed by Cord during the expedition.

status.label: Recovered from Akinah caches and taken by Cord

items.name: Akinah Soulcaster cache
items.summary: Multiple ancient Soulcasters discovered in Akinah’s hidden stores and divided among allied powers under the expedition’s negotiated cover story.

status.label: Recovered from Akinah and distributed under the negotiated settlement

items.name: Rysn’s fabrial mobility device
items.summary: A fabrial-assisted mobility solution developed during the voyage after Huio’s observations about aluminum and fabrial behavior, designed to make movement aboard ship easier for Rysn.

status.label: Prototype developed aboard the Wandersail

events.title: Shattering of Adonalsium
events.summary: Adonalsium is shattered into sixteen Shards; Honor, Cultivation, and Odium become three of the resulting powers relevant to Roshar.
events.explanation: Pre-2017 Cosmere books and Arcanum Unbounded make Shards an explicit framework, while Stormlight reveals the local conflict gradually.

events.title: Honor and Cultivation shape Rosharan civilization
events.summary: Honor and Cultivation become Roshar’s resident Shards and interact with singers, spren, and the existing ecology.
events.explanation: Exact dates and all causal details remain uncertain at this spoiler boundary.

events.title: Human catastrophe on Ashyn
events.dateLabel: Thousands of years before the main story
events.summary: Human use of powerful Surges destroys or devastates Ashyn, remembered later as the Tranquiline Halls.
events.explanation: The Oathbringer-era Dawnchant translation reverses Vorin myth: humans, not singers, were the newcomers to Roshar.

events.title: Humans migrate from Ashyn to Roshar
events.summary: Refugees arrive on Roshar and are initially given Shinovar; expansion and conflict follow.
events.explanation: This becomes a political weapon for Odium and a moral shock to the coalition.

events.title: First Desolation and human–singer war
events.summary: Odium’s alignment with human arrivals and later singer conflict evolves into the first Desolation; exact early sequence remains fragmentary.
events.explanation: The books intentionally preserve uncertainty about how roles shifted.

events.title: Oathpact formed
events.summary: Ten Heralds accept a cycle of return, war, death, torture on Braize, and renewed Desolation, supported by Honorblades.
events.explanation: The Oathpact delays Fused returns but depends on Herald endurance.

events.title: Knights Radiant organized
events.summary: Humans bonding spren are organized into ten orders around Ideals, Surges, and Heraldic models.
events.explanation: Nohadon’s legacy and Ishar’s role are part history, part legend.

events.title: Aharietiam: nine Heralds abandon the Oathpact
events.summary: After a Desolation, nine Heralds leave their Honorblades and tell humanity the war is over, leaving Taln alone on Braize.
events.explanation: This false 'Last Desolation' creates the long historical gap before the main saga.

events.title: False Desolation led by Ba-Ado-Mishram
events.summary: Ba-Ado-Mishram connects to singers broadly, supplies forms and Voidlight, and leads war despite Odium’s confinement.
events.explanation: Ancient Radiants plan her imprisonment, fearing the scale of her Connection.

events.title: Ba-Ado-Mishram imprisoned
events.summary: A strike team imprisons Ba-Ado-Mishram. The event damages singer populations connected to her, producing the slaveform/parshman state remembered by humans.
events.explanation: The books provide the consequence but not a complete technical account.

events.title: The Recreance
events.summary: Most Knights Radiant deliberately abandon their oaths and Shards, creating deadeye spren and ending the orders as public institutions.
events.explanation: Oathbringer reveals a major motive: discovery that humans were the original invaders and that Surges had destroyed Ashyn, combined with Honor’s instability and other pressures.

events.title: Vorin Hierocracy rises and falls
events.summary: Vorin church attempts direct rule and manipulates records; the Sunmaker defeats it, leaving lasting distrust of priestly political power.
events.explanation: Important for understanding why ardents are legally owned and why historical sources are unreliable.

events.title: Gavilar and Dalinar unify Alethkar
events.summary: Gavilar’s political ambition and Dalinar’s Blackthorn campaigns force the princedoms into a kingdom.
events.explanation: The campaign creates loyalty, trauma, enemies, and the militarized identity that later obstructs coalition-building.

events.title: Dalinar wins the Blade Oathbringer
events.summary: Dalinar defeats a Shardbearer and claims the Blade later named Oathbringer.
events.explanation: The scene defines the Blackthorn’s appetite for risk and the weapon’s morally compromised history.

events.title: Dalinar marries Evi
events.summary: Political marriage links the Kholins with Riran interests. Evi tries to humanize Dalinar but remains isolated in Alethi culture.
events.explanation: Adolin and Renarin are born from the marriage.

events.title: Dalinar destroys Rathalas; Evi dies
events.summary: After rebellion and an ambush, Dalinar orders the Rift sealed and burned. Evi enters the city to negotiate and dies with its inhabitants.
events.explanation: This is the atrocity Dalinar could not bear to remember and the moral center of his later refusal to give pain to Odium.

events.title: Dalinar seeks the Nightwatcher and meets Cultivation
events.summary: Dalinar asks for release from his pain. Cultivation removes Evi’s memory and prepares it to regrow later rather than granting simple oblivion.
events.explanation: The intervention creates a protected period in which Dalinar can change before confronting the truth.

events.title: Gavilar’s expedition meets the listeners
events.summary: Alethi explorers encounter the listeners on the Shattered Plains; diplomacy turns toward manipulation and war planning.
events.explanation: Gavilar’s secret goals diverge sharply from the public treaty project.

events.title: Gavilar assassinated during treaty feast
events.summary: The listeners hire Szeth to kill Gavilar after learning enough of his plans to fear the return of their gods.
events.explanation: Each prologue viewpoint adds a different layer: Szeth’s mission, Jasnah’s secret actions, and Eshonai’s conversation with Gavilar.

events.title: Kaladin’s squad fails to save Cenn
events.summary: Young recruit Cenn joins Kaladin’s unusually protective squad, but the battle is lost and Kaladin is later enslaved.
events.explanation: The chapter establishes Kaladin’s leadership before the reader learns how he fell.

events.title: Kaladin transported as a slave
events.summary: After Amaram’s betrayal, Kaladin repeatedly escapes and is recaptured; Tvlakv purchases him for sale to the warcamps.
events.explanation: His brands and learned helplessness frame the Bridge Four arc.

events.title: Shallan arrives in Kharbranth
events.summary: Shallan seeks Jasnah, intending to become her ward while stealing a Soulcaster to rescue House Davar.
events.explanation: The wardship plot is simultaneously scholarly apprenticeship, family heist, and the first visible return of Shallan’s bond.

events.title: Royal chasmfiend hunt nearly becomes a disaster
events.dateLabel: Dalinar main line, day aligned separately
events.summary: A chasmfiend hunt exposes Elhokar’s fear, Dalinar and Adolin’s combat coordination, and apparently cut saddle straps.
events.explanation: Official continuity notes use this chapter as a timeline anchor distinct from Kaladin’s earlier-relative chapters.

events.title: Kaladin begins rebuilding Bridge Four
events.summary: Kaladin shifts from suicidal isolation to medical care, food redistribution, spear training, and collective escape planning.
events.explanation: The crew’s transformation is social before it becomes magical.

events.title: Jasnah accepts Shallan as ward
events.summary: After testing Shallan’s scholarship and persistence, Jasnah accepts her, giving Shallan access to the Palanaeum and the object she plans to steal.
events.explanation: Their research increasingly points toward parshmen and the Voidbringers.

events.title: Three worldhoppers hire Ishikk
events.summary: Demoux, Galladon, and Baon search the Purelake for Hoid using assumed names.
events.explanation: This is the clearest early cross-Cosmere cluster in Stormlight.

events.title: Rysn trades in Shinovar
events.summary: Vstim teaches Rysn that successful trade requires understanding what another culture values, not merely imposing Thaylen assumptions.
events.explanation: The interlude foregrounds cultural translation rather than magical plot mechanics.

events.title: Axies records Cusicesh
events.summary: Axies studies a massive scheduled spren while dealing with Iri’s authorities.
events.explanation: A worldbuilding anchor for spren taxonomy and Aimian biology.

events.title: Baxil witnesses Shalash destroying her own image
events.summary: A patron later identifiable as Herald Shalash pays thieves while compulsively destroying depictions of herself.
events.explanation: The patron’s identity is not stated plainly in the scene but is established by the Oathbringer-era reference context.

events.title: Kaladin survives being strung up in a highstorm
events.summary: Bridge officers leave Kaladin exposed as punishment. He survives by drawing Stormlight while Syl defies the Stormfather’s pull.
events.explanation: This makes his impossible healing visible to Bridge Four and strengthens the bond’s stakes.

events.title: Kaladin Ch. 40 aligns with Dalinar Ch. 12
events.summary: The novel’s viewpoint lines are not presented in one shared starting order; Kaladin’s Chapter 40 occurs on the day of Dalinar’s Chapter 12 chasmfiend hunt.
events.explanation: The UI keeps book order and in-world relative order separate to avoid false sequencing.

events.title: Kabsal’s poisoning attempt exposes Soulcasting
events.summary: Kabsal’s attempt to poison Jasnah instead poisons Shallan. Jasnah Soulcasts Shallan’s blood and reveals the stolen ornament was not the source of her power.
events.explanation: Shallan’s own accidental Soulcasting and the Cryptics can no longer be dismissed.

events.title: Dalinar witnesses the Recreance at Feverstone Keep
events.summary: In a vision, Radiants abandon Plate and Blade before stunned soldiers.
events.explanation: The scene establishes that Shardblades are the remains of a deliberate institutional collapse, though deadeye truth comes later.

events.title: Shallan confesses theft and family crisis
events.summary: Shallan admits stealing the Soulcaster and explains House Davar’s danger. Jasnah recognizes Shallan as a fellow Surgebinder and keeps her as ward.
events.explanation: The relationship shifts from deception to a difficult alliance.

events.title: Sadeas abandons Dalinar at the Tower
events.summary: Sadeas withdraws his bridges, trapping the Kholin army against listener forces.
events.explanation: Dalinar’s political strategy collapses and Bridge Four must choose between escape and rescue.

events.title: Kaladin speaks the Second Windrunner Ideal
events.summary: Kaladin commits to protect people who cannot protect themselves, draws Stormlight, and leads Bridge Four back across the chasm.
events.explanation: The choice transforms an escape plan into the rescue that earns the crew’s freedom.

events.title: Dalinar trades Oathbringer for the bridgemen
events.summary: Dalinar gives Sadeas his Shardblade in exchange for ownership of every bridgeman, immediately freeing them and hiring Bridge Four.
events.explanation: It is both a practical rescue and a rejection of Alethi valuation: thousands of enslaved lives over one priceless weapon.

events.title: Taravangian is revealed as Szeth’s master
events.summary: The kindly king’s hidden hospitals and control of Szeth reveal a second large conspiracy behind the assassination campaign.
events.explanation: Death Rattles and the Diagram become central threats rather than atmospheric mystery.

events.title: Taln arrives at Kholinar
events.summary: A broken man carrying a Shardblade appears at the city gate and announces the Desolation.
events.explanation: He is Talenel, the Herald who remained on Braize.

events.title: Jasnah’s perspective on Gavilar’s assassination
events.dateLabel: Same assassination night as other prologues
events.summary: Jasnah survives an attempted arranged engagement, enters Shadesmar, meets Ivory, and receives Gavilar’s warning amid the assassination.
events.explanation: The prologue expands the secret-society and spren-bond context without resolving Gavilar’s full plan.

events.title: The Wind’s Pleasure is attacked
events.summary: Assassins attack Jasnah’s ship. Shallan Soulcasts to survive and believes Jasnah killed, while Jasnah escapes through Shadesmar.
events.explanation: Shallan is forced into independent leadership before reaching the Plains.

events.title: Shallan takes control of Tvlakv’s caravan
events.summary: Stranded in the Frostlands, Shallan uses Lightweaving, social improvisation, and selective confidence to recruit guards and deserters.
events.explanation: Bluth’s arc demonstrates her power to show people a version of themselves they can choose to become.

events.title: Bridge Four tests Kaladin’s powers
events.summary: Sigzil and the crew measure Lashings, Stormlight use, and the relationship between Kaladin’s proximity and squire abilities.
events.explanation: The magic becomes an experimental practice rather than a solitary miracle.

events.title: Shallan kills Tyn and meets the Ghostblood trail
events.summary: Tyn reveals herself as part of the plot against Jasnah and attacks Shallan. Shallan summons a Blade and kills her, then assumes Tyn’s place in Ghostblood communications.
events.explanation: This is the bridge from caravan survival to active infiltration.

events.title: Shallan reaches the Shattered Plains
events.summary: Shallan enters Kholin politics, meets Adolin formally, begins mapping the Plains, and creates Veil for Ghostblood work.
events.explanation: Her scholarly, romantic, and covert roles now occupy the same location.

events.title: Lift saves Gawx and makes an unlikely Prime
events.summary: Nale kills Gawx while hunting Lift; Lift returns and heals him. Azish law and politics then elevate the revived youth to Prime.
events.explanation: This interlude is reused as Edgedancer’s prologue.

events.title: Eshonai takes stormform
events.summary: Eshonai tests stormform intending controlled evaluation, but the form and its rhythms overwhelm her and drive a coup within listener leadership.
events.explanation: Venli’s manipulation and Ulim’s groundwork make this the decisive listener tragedy.

events.title: Rysn is injured in the Reshi Isles
events.summary: Rysn climbs from a greatshell island, falls, and loses use of her legs. The Reshi give her Chiri-Chiri.
events.explanation: Her arc shifts from apprenticeship through bodily loss toward a new kind of independence.

events.title: Adolin’s disadvantaged duel becomes four against one
events.summary: A political trap turns Adolin’s duel into a lethal group contest. Renarin enters despite little chance, and Kaladin joins with the declaration that honor is already dead.
events.explanation: Kaladin and Adolin’s cooperation wins, but Kaladin’s public demand against Amaram leads to imprisonment.

events.title: Kaladin is imprisoned after challenging Amaram
events.summary: Elhokar reacts to Kaladin’s accusation as a challenge to lighteyed authority. Kaladin’s bitterness deepens and Moash’s assassination argument becomes more persuasive.
events.explanation: Wit’s Fleet story reframes failure as continuing to choose direction.

events.title: Shallan and Kaladin survive the chasms
events.summary: A highstorm traps them below the Plains. They share selective truths, fight a chasmfiend, and reach relative understanding.
events.explanation: Their abilities and traumas become visible to each other without full confession.

events.title: Kaladin’s conflicting promises nearly kill Syl
events.summary: Kaladin has promised both to protect Elhokar and to allow Moash’s assassination. The contradiction violates his bond’s moral center, draining his powers and leaving Syl nearly mindless.
events.explanation: The crisis shows that oaths are not passwords; their lived intent matters.

events.title: Kaladin speaks the Third Windrunner Ideal
events.summary: Kaladin chooses to protect Elhokar even though he hates him, restores Syl, and opposes Moash and Graves.
events.explanation: Syl becomes a living Shardblade and Kaladin then flies toward Dalinar’s battlefield.

events.title: Battle of Narak and summoning of the Everstorm
events.summary: Alethi forces attack Narak as stormform listeners summon the Everstorm. Szeth attacks Dalinar; Kaladin defeats him; Shallan activates the Oathgate.
events.explanation: The warcamp era ends as the army transfers to Urithiru and the True Desolation begins.

events.title: Nale restores Szeth and gives him Nightblood
events.summary: After Szeth’s defeat, Nale uses a fabrial to restore him, explains the Desolation’s return, and offers a new sword.
events.explanation: Szeth moves from Truthless obedience toward Skybreaker judgment.

events.title: Adolin kills Sadeas
events.summary: Sadeas promises continued sabotage. In an unplanned confrontation, Adolin kills him and hides the body and weapon.
events.explanation: The murder removes an overt rival while creating a concealed moral and political liability.

events.title: Jasnah returns from Shadesmar and meets Wit
events.summary: Jasnah finally exits the Cognitive Realm near the Plains and finds Wit waiting.
events.explanation: Her survival closes the ship mystery while preserving a large unseen journey.

events.title: Lift leaves Azimir
events.summary: Uncomfortable with palace life and the idea of changing, Lift follows reports of a strange man killing people with powers and heads toward Yeddaw.
events.explanation: The journey extends her conflict between staying 'the same' and accepting responsibility.

events.title: Lift investigates Yeddaw and the Stump
events.summary: Lift steals food, follows missing supplies, and discovers an orphanage whose sick children recover in ways the Stump does not understand.
events.explanation: The supposed food theft and hidden healing point to another nascent Radiant.

events.title: Lift encounters Arclo, a Sleepless
events.summary: A man disassembles into cremlings and explains that the Sleepless are observing dangerous developments.
events.explanation: The encounter reframes background cremlings as potential surveillance and connects the novella to Aimia.

events.title: Lift protects the Stump and speaks her Third Ideal
events.summary: Lift chooses to listen to and remember someone Nale dismisses, heals the Stump, and forces Nale to confront the Everstorm’s proof.
events.explanation: Nale ends his campaign against budding Radiants and reveals more of the Skybreaker crisis.

events.title: Eshonai’s perspective on Gavilar’s final feast
events.summary: Eshonai meets Gavilar, learns he intends to restore the listeners’ old gods, and helps trigger the decision to assassinate him.
events.explanation: The third prologue turns the assassination from unexplained treachery into a desperate preventative act.

events.title: Kaladin returns to Hearthstone
events.summary: Kaladin finds his family alive under singer occupation, meets his baby brother, and tries to protect both humans and newly awakened singers.
events.explanation: The return makes the war morally symmetrical at village scale rather than a simple monster invasion.

events.title: Dalinar begins building the monarch coalition
events.summary: Dalinar uses visions, spanreeds, and Oathgate access to contact rulers who distrust Alethi conquest and his Blackthorn reputation.
events.explanation: The central problem is credibility: unity cannot simply be ordered by the man famous for forced unification.

events.title: Kaladin travels with awakened singers
events.summary: Separated from easy lines of allegiance, Kaladin joins Sah’s group and learns how parshmen experienced human ownership and family separation.
events.explanation: He cannot reduce them to enemies even while trying to reach Kholinar.

events.title: Copycat murders reveal Re-Shephir in Urithiru
events.summary: Violent deaths and impossible imitations lead Shallan into the tower’s depths, where the Midnight Mother has been learning from human cruelty.
events.explanation: Shallan drives Re-Shephir away by confronting her with recognition and a stronger constructed identity.

events.title: Dalinar and Navani marry
events.summary: The Stormfather officiates a direct marriage despite Vorin political and religious objections.
events.explanation: The union formalizes a partnership already central to coalition leadership.

events.title: Coalition rulers meet through Honor’s vision
events.summary: Dalinar brings multiple monarchs into a shared vision to prove the Desolation and negotiate cooperation.
events.explanation: The use of visions becomes diplomatic infrastructure rather than private prophecy.

events.title: Dawnchant translation reveals human origins
events.summary: Urithiru scholars translate records showing humans arrived from Ashyn and conquered land belonging to singers.
events.explanation: Odium times the revelation to fracture coalition legitimacy and Radiant confidence.

events.title: Strike team infiltrates Kholinar
events.summary: Elhokar, Kaladin, Shallan, Adolin, Azure’s contacts, and squires enter the occupied capital using disguises and covert routes.
events.explanation: Objectives compete: rescue Gavinor, secure the Oathgate, support the Wall Guard, and understand the Unmade.

events.title: The team meets Highmarshal Azure
events.summary: Azure commands the Wall Guard with an unusual sword and offworld idiom. She is searching for Zahel and Nightblood while defending the city.
events.explanation: Warbreaker readers can identify her as Vivenna, but the Stormlight plot works without that recognition.

events.title: Shallan enters the Heart of the Revel
events.summary: Undercover personas investigate Ashertmarn’s feast cult around the Oathgate. Shallan tries to become whatever each suffering person needs, multiplying identities faster than she can integrate them.
events.explanation: The Revel externalizes surrender through excess, paralleling Shallan’s internal avoidance.

events.title: Wit tells Shallan the Girl Who Looked Up
events.summary: Wit uses story and Lightweaving to help Shallan distinguish acknowledging pain from becoming only the masks built around it.
events.explanation: The scene supports rather than resolves her identity fragmentation.

events.title: Kholinar palace battle and Oathgate failure
events.summary: Singers, Fused, palace troops, the Wall Guard, and the infiltrators collide. Sja-anat-corrupted Oathgate spren redirect the surviving team into Shadesmar.
events.explanation: The human and singer groups Kaladin knows kill one another, leaving him unable to act decisively.

events.title: Moash kills Elhokar
events.summary: Elhokar protects Gavinor and begins speaking the first Lightweaver Ideal, but Moash kills him and gives Kaladin the Bridge Four salute.
events.explanation: The act fuses personal revenge, political collapse, and Moash’s rejection of his former community.

events.title: Kholinar survivors are trapped in Shadesmar
events.summary: Kaladin, Shallan, Adolin, Azure, Syl, and Pattern must reach Thaylen City through the Cognitive Realm while carrying limited Stormlight and coping with deadeye Maya.
events.explanation: Physical geography reverses: land becomes bead ocean and water becomes traversable ground.

events.title: The group visits Riino’s lighthouse
events.summary: Riino recognizes Kaladin’s Investiture, offers a future-reading device, and points the travelers toward Celebrant.
events.explanation: The lighthouse provides an explicit Elantris connection and a practical navigation waypoint.

events.title: Notum carries the group on Honor’s Path
events.summary: The travelers negotiate passage with honorspren, learn more about deadeyes and Syl’s political status, and struggle with limited resources.
events.explanation: Adolin’s attention to Maya begins producing signs that the deadeye is not entirely unreachable.

events.title: The travelers reach Celebrant
events.summary: At the spren market city, the group seeks transport toward Thaylenah while Fused pursuit closes in.
events.explanation: Azure separates to continue her own search and help delay pursuers.

events.title: Dalinar fully remembers Evi and the Rift
events.summary: Cultivation’s pruning ends. Dalinar relives the burning of Rathalas and Evi’s death while political pressure and alcohol threaten to collapse him.
events.explanation: Odium’s strategy depends on converting acknowledged guilt into surrendered responsibility.

events.title: Taravangian bargains with Odium and betrays the coalition
events.summary: With the Diagram’s predictions failing, Taravangian offers information and service in exchange for protection of Kharbranth and its people.
events.explanation: His definition of saving humanity contracts to a negotiated remnant.

events.title: Odium attacks Thaylen City
events.summary: Fused strike the gemstone reserve and Oathgate while the Thrill corrupts Amaram’s Sadeas army. Coalition forces are scattered or trapped.
events.explanation: The battle combines military invasion, Unmade influence, Diagram sabotage, and Odium’s attempt to claim Dalinar.

events.title: Dalinar refuses to give Odium his pain
events.summary: Odium frames the Blackthorn’s atrocities as something external he can remove. Dalinar accepts that the crimes are his, insists responsibility still permits change, and rejects becoming Odium’s champion.
events.explanation: The climax turns moral ownership into magical and political resistance.

events.title: Dalinar opens Honor’s Perpendicularity
events.summary: Dalinar unites the three Realms, flooding the battlefield with Stormlight and creating a path that returns the Shadesmar group.
events.explanation: The act exceeds what the Stormfather expected and becomes the tactical reversal.

events.title: Radiants and coalition counterattack at Thaylen Field
events.summary: Kaladin fights Amaram, Shallan fields an illusion army, Jasnah Soulcasts at scale, Renarin resists prediction, Lift supports Dalinar, Szeth chooses Dalinar, and Bridge Four joins the defense.
events.explanation: Rock kills Amaram; Adolin and Maya survive; the Oathgate and city are saved.

events.title: Dalinar captures Nergaoul in the King’s Drop
events.summary: Dalinar confronts the Thrill as a familiar influence and traps the Unmade in the perfect ruby.
events.explanation: Alethi bloodlust is revealed as culturally reinforced but supernaturally amplified, not an excuse for individual choices.

events.title: Jasnah is selected as queen of Alethkar
events.summary: With Elhokar dead and Gavinor a child, Alethi leadership chooses Jasnah rather than simply transferring power to Dalinar or Adolin.
events.explanation: This separates Alethkar’s monarchy from Dalinar’s coalition role.

events.title: Shallan and Adolin marry
events.summary: Shallan chooses a life with Adolin while acknowledging Veil and Radiant remain parts of her rather than problems instantly solved by marriage.
events.explanation: The relationship provides an anchor but not a cure.

events.title: Moash kills Jezrien and becomes Vyre
events.summary: Odium’s servants give Moash a specialized dagger. He kills the broken Herald Ahu/Jezrien and accepts a new name and role.
events.explanation: The act suggests the ancient immortality cycle can be attacked directly.

events.title: Wit rescues and bonds Elhokar’s Cryptic
events.summary: In occupied Kholinar, Wit retrieves a Cryptic that had been moving toward Elhokar and begins a Lightweaver bond while evading Fused patrols.
events.explanation: This is the final event within the artifact’s spoiler boundary.

events.title: Ghost ship First Dreams returns from Aimia
events.summary: Yalb and another crew discover the First Dreams drifting back from the direction of Aimia with its expedition crew missing, triggering concern that Akinah may have become a strategic threat.
events.explanation: This is the practical trigger for Navani and Thaylenah to authorize a new expedition.

events.title: Rysn negotiates command of the Akinah expedition
events.summary: Chiri-Chiri’s illness points toward Akinah, while Navani needs the island investigated. Rysn negotiates pay, authority, Windrunner support, and scholarly participation before agreeing to sail.
events.explanation: The mission combines Rysn’s personal need to save Chiri-Chiri with coalition strategic interests.

events.title: Voyage research produces a mobility fabrial for Rysn
events.summary: Huio’s observations about aluminum and fabrial behavior give Rushu a practical route toward a fabrial-assisted mobility device adapted for Rysn aboard ship.
events.explanation: The sequence links accessibility engineering to the broader metal/fabrial rules later made explicit in Rhythm of War.

events.title: Wandersail penetrates Akinah’s storm barrier
events.summary: The expedition reaches the hidden city, discovers deliberate false structures around the Oathgate, and realizes Akinah is defended by deception as much as by weather.
events.explanation: The apparent archaeological expedition becomes a controlled encounter with Sleepless defenses.

events.title: Nikli reveals himself as a Sleepless guardian
events.summary: Nikli dissolves the human disguise into hordelings and moves to eliminate the expedition after the hidden caverns are breached.
events.explanation: Rysn learns that the Sleepless have been shaping events to keep outsiders away from Akinah’s deeper secrets.

events.title: The Dawnshard bonds Rysn
events.summary: A Command housed in the Akinah mural leaves its container and attaches to Rysn, making her the bearer of a Dawnshard.
events.explanation: This shifts Rysn from negotiator caught in the Sleepless defense plan to the person whose continued survival is itself strategically vital.

events.title: Huio swears the Third Ideal
events.summary: While the Windrunners fight Sleepless hordelings, Huio’s need to protect Lopen pushes him to the Third Ideal and Caelinora manifests as a living Shardweapon.
events.explanation: The oath reframes Huio’s quiet presence and his complicated relationship with Lopen.

events.title: Rysn negotiates a compact with the Sleepless
events.summary: Rysn bargains for the expedition’s survival and safe return. The Sleepless accept a layered cover story, continued guardianship of Rysn, and the removal of selected Akinah artifacts while the Dawnshard remains hidden on her person.
events.explanation: Rysn wins by making herself and secrecy more valuable alive than dead.

events.title: Lopen swears the Third Ideal
events.summary: Reflecting on how his humor can hurt people he means to help, Lopen finds the personal form of the Third Ideal; Rua can now become a living Shardweapon.
events.explanation: This closes Lopen’s novella arc with a protection oath focused inward on the harm he himself can cause.

events.title: Navani’s view of Gavilar’s final night reframes his secret project
events.dateLabel: Six years before ROW main story; assassination night
events.summary: Navani’s perspective reveals Gavilar’s secret meetings, his cruelty toward her scholarly identity, unusual Light-related spheres, and his deeper involvement with Heralds and offworld-scale ambitions.
events.explanation: The same assassination night is revisited again, but now from Navani’s position and with clues that become relevant to anti-Light research.

events.title: Coalition rescues Hearthstone and captures Fused suppression technology
events.summary: Kaladin and the Windrunners evacuate Hearthstone while fighting Leshwi and Lezian. A suppression device that interferes with Radiant powers is captured for Navani’s study.
events.explanation: The opening demonstrates how quickly the war has become a contest of magical technology rather than only battlefield skill.

events.title: Ialai dies and Shallan inherits a Ghostblood/Restares trail
events.summary: During Shallan’s operation against Ialai Sadeas, Ialai is poisoned and leaves behind notes pointing toward Restares, Thaidakar, and wider Cosmere connections. Shallan initially assumes an infiltrator is responsible.
events.explanation: The murder becomes a pressure point in Shallan’s persona conflict and the Ghostblood plot.

events.title: Dalinar relieves Kaladin from frontline command
events.summary: Recognizing that repeated combat trauma is impairing Kaladin’s ability to function, Dalinar removes him from active battlefield command despite Kaladin’s identity being built around protecting through fighting.
events.explanation: This is not a demotion for cowardice; it begins Kaladin’s difficult search for ways to protect that do not require endless combat.

events.title: Kaladin builds a clinic and peer-support model
events.summary: Working again as a surgeon, Kaladin recognizes that many soldiers and civilians need community, routine, listening, and humane treatment rather than confinement. He begins structured group support, including Noril.
events.explanation: This becomes a new expression of the Windrunner ethic: protection can mean helping people live with wounds that cannot be solved by a spear or Stormlight.

events.title: Adolin and Shallan depart for Lasting Integrity
events.summary: The coalition sends a mixed Radiant delegation through Shadesmar to persuade honorspren to renew bonds. Shallan simultaneously pursues Mraize’s order to identify Restares.
events.explanation: The mission fuses diplomacy, espionage, Shallan’s identity crisis, and Adolin’s developing bond with Maya.

events.title: Raboniel convinces the Nine to attack Urithiru
events.summary: Raboniel argues that human Radiants and fabrial science are advancing faster than the Fused can tolerate and that the tower must be seized before its full ancient defenses are restored.
events.explanation: Taravangian’s intelligence and the captured-suppressor arms race make the tower a time-sensitive target.

events.title: Raboniel captures Urithiru and inverts the tower defenses
events.summary: Fused infiltrators reach the crystal pillar, infuse it with Voidlight, and invert the Sibling’s protections. Most Radiants in the tower collapse unconscious while singer forces enter through the Oathgates and balconies.
events.explanation: The occupation succeeds because Dalinar and Jasnah are committed to Emul, the tower is not fully awake, and the invaders exploit technology related to the tower’s own defense system.

events.title: Kaladin becomes the tower’s mobile resistance fighter
events.summary: Because Adhesion and his advanced bond are suppressed differently, Kaladin retains limited capability. Guided by the Sibling and aided by Dabbid and later fabrials, he sabotages corruption nodes, protects unconscious Radiants, and evades Lezian.
events.explanation: The arc strips away the normal Windrunner advantages and forces Kaladin to operate as an exhausted insurgent inside a hostile city.

events.title: Navani and Raboniel become scientific collaborators under occupation
