events.summary: Raboniel turns Navani’s captivity into a research partnership. Their experiments establish that Lights respond to tones and rhythms and that apparently opposed forms of Investiture can be manipulated with wave-like precision.
events.explanation: The relationship is adversarial, coercive, respectful, and intellectually generative at the same time; each scientist knows the other may weaponize every discovery.

events.title: Navani and Raboniel create Warlight
events.summary: Navani matches Honor’s tone while Raboniel sings Odium’s; instead of destroying one another, Stormlight and Voidlight harmonize into a stable hybrid Light associated with the Rhythm of War.
events.explanation: The experiment proves that Shardic Lights can combine through harmony, a conceptual step that also suggests destructive interference can have an opposite result.

events.title: Restares is revealed as the Herald Kalak
events.summary: The elusive Sons of Honor leader Restares is revealed to be Kalak, one of the Heralds and the High Judge of Lasting Integrity. He is desperate to escape Roshar and the cycle trapping the Heralds.
events.explanation: The Ghostblood target, honorspren judge, and Prelude viewpoint collapse into one identity.

events.title: Adolin accepts trial by witness in Lasting Integrity
events.summary: The honorspren put the human-spren relationship itself on trial through Adolin. Witnesses, politics, Notum’s conscience, and Maya’s growing responsiveness turn the proceeding into a referendum on the meaning of the Recreance.
events.explanation: Adolin cannot win by legal mastery; his strongest evidence is the relationship he has patiently built with Maya.

events.title: Maya testifies: the ancient spren chose the Recreance
events.summary: Drawing strength through her connection with Adolin, Maya speaks and rejects the claim that ancient Radiants alone betrayed helpless spren. The spren knowingly joined the decision to break the bonds, though neither side expected deadeyes to result.
events.explanation: This does not make the Recreance harmless, but it overturns a foundational assumption driving modern honorspren hostility to humans.

events.title: Shallan learns Radiant killed Ialai and integrates Veil
events.summary: Shallan’s feared “Formless” is not a new external personality taking over. She confronts the truth that Radiant poisoned Ialai to protect her, and Veil’s role as a protective partition reaches an end as Shallan integrates those memories.
events.explanation: The reveal changes Shallan’s model of her own personas while leaving an even older buried truth—the first Cryptic bond—still unresolved.

events.title: Navani produces anti-Voidlight
events.summary: Using destructive-interference reasoning, isolated transfer, and a precisely inverted tone, Navani creates a form of Light that reacts catastrophically with Voidlight.
events.explanation: Raboniel immediately recognizes that this can end the rebirth cycle of Fused; the discovery turns Light acoustics into an existential weapon.

events.title: Raboniel permanently releases her daughter with anti-Voidlight
events.summary: Raboniel weaponizes the new anti-Voidlight in a raysium dagger and uses it on her deeply damaged Fused daughter, ending the cycle of rebirth rather than sending her back to Braize.
events.explanation: The act exposes Raboniel’s personal motive: she wants an end to an immortal war whose participants can no longer heal psychologically.

events.title: Moash permanently kills Phendorana and murders Teft
events.summary: During the final collapse of the occupation, Moash uses an anti-Stormlight weapon to destroy Phendorana permanently, then kills Teft. Teft dies knowing he is loved and that his life had become worth fighting for.
events.explanation: The attack is designed to break Kaladin psychologically at the exact moment the tower resistance is reaching its limit.

events.title: Kaladin accepts the Fourth Ideal and manifests living Shardplate
events.summary: After a vision/connection with Tien helps him face the truth that some people cannot be saved, Kaladin stops treating every death as proof of personal failure. He swears the Fourth Ideal and windspren form living Shardplate around him.
events.explanation: The oath is an acceptance of limits, not abandonment of responsibility. It directly resolves the Ideal he could not speak at Thaylen Field.

events.title: Navani bonds the Sibling and restores Towerlight
events.summary: Navani rejects Gavilar’s old dismissal of her scholarship, matches Honor’s tone against the Sibling’s Cultivation tone, and forms a Bondsmith bond. Together they restore Towerlight and retake the tower systems.
events.explanation: The Bondsmith bond is also a scientific reconciliation: Navani’s knowledge and the Sibling’s living system become one operational partnership.

events.title: Urithiru awakens and the occupation collapses
events.summary: The Sibling reactivates tower fabrials and defenses, waking Radiants and suppressing hostile forces. Kaladin’s public return and singer defections turn the occupation into a rout.
events.explanation: Liberation is the combined outcome of resistance, Navani’s bond, singer dissent, and Kaladin’s Fourth Ideal rather than a single duel.

events.title: Dalinar confronts Ishar and discovers Physical spren experiments
events.summary: In Tukar, Ishar demonstrates terrifying unbound Bondsmith control over Connection, tries to take Dalinar’s bond, and retreats after Nightblood disrupts the attack. His camp contains dead spren given unnatural Physical bodies.
events.explanation: The encounter shows what Bondsmith powers can do without Honor’s old constraints and establishes why Dalinar thinks Ishar may still be necessary to understand his abilities.

events.title: Rlain bonds Tumi and becomes a Truthwatcher
events.summary: Tumi, an enlightened mistspren from Sja-anat’s network, chooses Rlain. The bond gives Rlain a Radiant path that is neither a token human appointment nor a surrender of listener identity.
events.explanation: It also expands the group of Radiants whose spren have been transformed by Sja-anat.

events.title: Dalinar and Odium agree to a contest of champions in ten days
events.summary: Dalinar and Rayse formalize terms: either outcome stops the immediate war and keeps Odium bound to the system, while territorial control and Dalinar’s future service as a Fused depend on the champion result.
events.explanation: The agreement creates a fixed ten-day horizon and constrains what the Shard can openly do—while leaving room for interpretation and loopholes.

events.title: Venli and sympathetic Fused leave to seek the surviving listeners
events.summary: After learning that listeners survived on the Shattered Plains and openly using her Radiant bond, Venli chooses a future outside Odium’s hierarchy. Leshwi and several Fused join the break.
events.explanation: The singer/listener conflict is no longer a simple humans-versus-Odium binary; a third political and spiritual direction becomes visible.

events.title: Taravangian kills Rayse with Nightblood and becomes Odium
events.summary: Taravangian’s most emotional and least intelligent day aligns him with Odium’s Intent. As Szeth attacks his mortal body and Rayse pulls his mind into a vision, Taravangian uses Nightblood to kill Rayse, then takes up the Shard.
events.explanation: The Shard survives; its Vessel changes. This means Dalinar’s contract remains relevant, but the mind searching for ways around it is no longer Rayse.

events.title: Shallan acknowledges Testament as her first Cryptic
events.summary: Shallan finally admits that she had bonded a Cryptic before Pattern, broke those oaths after killing her mother, and left Testament a deadeye. She tells Adolin rather than hiding the truth behind another persona.
events.explanation: This recontextualizes Shallan’s childhood Surgebinding, Shardblade memories, and the unusually complicated state of her oaths.

events.title: El permanently kills Lezian using anti-Stormlight research
events.summary: After Lezian returns furious from defeat, El uses the newly shared anti-Light discoveries to kill him permanently, demonstrating that the technology is already propagating beyond Navani and Raboniel.
events.explanation: The discovery that promised an end to immortal war is immediately usable as a tool of internal discipline.

events.title: Stormfather gives Eshonai one final journey across Roshar
events.dateLabel: ROW ch. 117; flashback to Narak aftermath
events.summary: The book returns to Eshonai’s actual death after Narak. The Stormfather accepts her final struggle as enough for the First Ideal to briefly sustain her Cognitive self, then carries her across Roshar so the explorer can finally see the world before passing Beyond.
events.explanation: This closes the listener-sisters flashback structure with Eshonai defined by exploration rather than only by warform and defeat.

events.title: The new Odium alters Wit’s Breath-stored memories and replays their meeting
events.summary: Wit notices that Odium does not behave like Rayse and nearly identifies the Vessel change. Taravangian-Odium removes some memories stored in Wit’s Breaths, resets the encounter, and performs Rayse’s expected manner more convincingly.
events.explanation: Wit leaves without consciously knowing why the meeting felt wrong, though loss of perfect pitch and inconsistencies imply something happened. This is the atlas’s hard spoiler boundary.

graphNodes.name: Kaladin Stormblessed
graphNodes.summary: A surgeon’s son turned soldier, slave, and leader. His bond with Syl restores Windrunner powers, while his central conflict is how to protect people when opposing sides both contain people worth saving.

graphNodes.name: Sylphrena
graphNodes.summary: Kaladin’s honorspren. Curious and empathetic, she gradually recovers identity and memory as their bond strengthens. She represents the moral rather than merely technical side of Windrunner oaths.

graphNodes.name: Dalinar Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Gavilar’s brother and former conqueror. Visions, the Codes, and his bond with the Stormfather push him from Alethi warlord toward coalition builder; Oathbringer restores the memories he surrendered to survive his guilt.

graphNodes.name: Navani Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Engineer, political organizer, and widow of Gavilar. She coordinates fabrial research and the Oathgate network, marries Dalinar, and supplies much of the coalition’s practical infrastructure.

graphNodes.name: Adolin Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Dalinar’s elder son, an elite duelist and unusually socially perceptive soldier. His killing of Sadeas remains concealed through Oathbringer; in Shadesmar, his respectful relationship with his deadeye Blade becomes visibly unusual.

graphNodes.name: Renarin Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Dalinar’s younger son. Quiet, medically stigmatized, and eager to contribute, he secretly bonds Glys. By Oathbringer, his visions differ from ordinary Truthwatcher expectations because Glys has been altered by Sja-anat.

graphNodes.name: Jasnah Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Historian, philosopher, and accomplished Elsecaller. She researches the returning Desolation, survives the attack on the Wind’s Pleasure by entering Shadesmar, and becomes queen of Alethkar after Elhokar’s death.

graphNodes.name: Shallan Davar
graphNodes.summary: A Veden artist who seeks Jasnah to steal a Soulcaster and save her family. Her Cryptic bond, repressed trauma, Ghostblood infiltration, and personas—especially Veil and Radiant—become inseparable from her growing Lightweaver skill.

graphNodes.name: Pattern
graphNodes.summary: Shallan’s Cryptic partner. Fascinated by lies, truth, and human contradiction, he helps her Soulcast and Lightweave while pushing her to acknowledge memories she has buried.

graphNodes.name: Szeth-son-son-Vallano
graphNodes.summary: A Shin man declared Truthless and compelled to obey whoever holds his Oathstone. He assassinates rulers with Jezrien’s Honorblade, is defeated at Narak, restored by Nale, takes up Nightblood, and ultimately chooses Dalinar as the authority he will follow.

graphNodes.name: Nightblood
graphNodes.summary: A sentient Awakened sword from Nalthis, created under a dangerously vague command to destroy evil. It consumes enormous Investiture and can kill far beyond ordinary physical damage. Nale gives it to Szeth.

graphNodes.name: Wit
graphNodes.summary: A worldhopping storyteller who appears across the Cosmere. On Roshar he serves as Alethi Wit, advises or provokes major characters, uses several non-Rosharan arts, and at Oathbringer’s end rescues a Cryptic from occupied Kholinar.

graphNodes.name: Taravangian
graphNodes.summary: A ruler whose visit to the Nightwatcher/Cultivation produces alternating intelligence and compassion. On his most intelligent day he dictates the Diagram, a plan to save a remnant of humanity through controlled atrocities and political domination.

graphNodes.name: Lift
graphNodes.summary: A young Edgedancer who metabolizes food into usable Investiture rather than relying on Stormlight in the normal way. Her irreverence masks a fierce commitment to people institutions overlook.

graphNodes.name: Wyndle
graphNodes.summary: Lift’s cultivated, anxious spren companion. He forms plantlike trails in the Physical Realm and can become her living Shardfork/Blade despite preferring civilized restraint.

graphNodes.name: Odium
graphNodes.summary: The Shard of divine hatred and passion. Rayse holds it through nearly all of Rhythm of War, still bound to the Rosharan system and increasingly strained by setbacks. Near the end, Taravangian kills Rayse with Nightblood and takes up the Shard; the power remains Odium but its Vessel and strategy change.

graphNodes.name: Stormfather
graphNodes.summary: Vast spren of the highstorm and a repository of Honor’s power and impressions. Reluctantly bonds Dalinar, gives visions, and becomes the core of Dalinar’s Bondsmith abilities.

graphNodes.name: Cultivation
graphNodes.summary: One of Roshar’s resident Shards. Often conflated with the Nightwatcher, but personally intervened in Dalinar’s and Taravangian’s boons and curses as part of long-term plans.

graphNodes.name: Honor
graphNodes.summary: The dead Shard once held by Tanavast. His power remains in the Stormfather, honorspren, Honorblades, oaths, and Rosharan systems; his recorded visions warn of Odium and urge unity.

graphNodes.name: Gavilar Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Dalinar’s brother, Navani’s first husband, and the king whose assassination begins the war on the Shattered Plains. Oathbringer reveals his secret dealings with listeners, Heraldic knowledge, unusual gemstones, and plans to force a Desolation.

graphNodes.name: Elhokar Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Gavilar’s son, an insecure king who slowly recognizes his failures. He joins the mission to retake Kholinar and begins speaking a Lightweaver oath while protecting his child, but Moash kills him before he completes it.

graphNodes.name: Aesudan Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Elhokar’s wife and Gavinor’s mother. Left as regent in Kholinar, she embraces excess and attempts to bond the Unmade Yelig-nar; the bond consumes her.

graphNodes.name: Gavinor Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Young son of Elhokar and Aesudan. Rescued from the palace during Kholinar’s fall and taken toward safety with the surviving mission.

graphNodes.name: Evi Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Dalinar’s first wife and mother of Adolin and Renarin. Gentle and culturally isolated at the Alethi court; she dies in the burning of Rathalas after trying to negotiate peace, a truth Dalinar had asked Cultivation to remove from his memory.

graphNodes.name: Tien
graphNodes.summary: Kaladin’s younger brother, whose optimism and death in battle define Kaladin’s protective drive. Oathbringer’s Spiritual vision lets Kaladin speak with an impression of him during the Battle of Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Lirin
graphNodes.summary: Hearthstone’s surgeon and Kaladin’s father. His strict medical pacifism shaped Kaladin, while his conflict with Roshone helped trigger the family’s losses.

graphNodes.name: Hesina
graphNodes.summary: Kaladin’s perceptive mother, skilled at balancing Lirin’s principles with emotional practicality. Reunited with Kaladin when he returns to occupied Hearthstone.

graphNodes.name: Oroden
graphNodes.summary: The baby born to Lirin and Hesina after Kaladin left Hearthstone; his existence surprises Kaladin on his return.

graphNodes.name: Brightlord Roshone
graphNodes.summary: Exiled lighteyes made citylord of Hearthstone. His feud with Lirin and manipulation of conscription contribute to Tien’s death; by Oathbringer he is a diminished figure under singer occupation.

graphNodes.name: Laral
graphNodes.summary: Kaladin’s childhood friend, later Roshone’s wife and de facto local authority. She challenges Kaladin’s simplified memory of Hearthstone and helps manage civilians during occupation.

graphNodes.name: Meridas Amaram
graphNodes.summary: An admired Alethi general who murders Kaladin’s surviving squad and steals their Shards. Exposed but politically protected, he later inherits Sadeas’s army, accepts Yelig-nar, and dies fighting Kaladin at Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Torol Sadeas
graphNodes.summary: Dalinar’s old war companion and chief political rival. He abandons Dalinar at the Tower, weaponizes public perception, and refuses reconciliation; Adolin kills him after Narak.

graphNodes.name: Ialai Sadeas
graphNodes.summary: Sadeas’s politically formidable wife. After his death she retains control of his faction and tries to obstruct Dalinar’s coalition while investigating who killed him.

graphNodes.name: Teleb
graphNodes.summary: Veteran archer and officer who served Dalinar from the unification wars through the Shattered Plains; killed before the main Oathbringer campaign, with flashbacks expanding his history.

graphNodes.name: Kadash
graphNodes.summary: A former soldier who became an ardent after witnessing the Rift. He debates Dalinar’s rejection of Vorin orthodoxy and embodies the cost of Dalinar’s old campaigns.

graphNodes.name: Sebarial
graphNodes.summary: A deliberately eccentric highprince whose practical commerce and logistics repeatedly prove more useful than his reputation suggests. Patron and partner of Palona.

graphNodes.name: Palona
graphNodes.summary: A Herdazian darkeyes who manages Sebarial’s household and commercial affairs with blunt competence.

graphNodes.name: Aladar
graphNodes.summary: One of the first highprinces to support Dalinar’s reforms after seeing Sadeas’s destructive politics; commands coalition forces.

graphNodes.name: Roion
graphNodes.summary: Cautious highprince who joins the Narak expedition and is killed by Szeth during the battle.

graphNodes.name: Ruthar
graphNodes.summary: Aggressive, obstructionist highprince who resists Dalinar’s coalition and exploits Alethi custom.

graphNodes.name: Hatham
graphNodes.summary: Diplomatic highprince whose wife’s social network and his relative moderation make him a useful coalition participant.

graphNodes.name: Bethab
graphNodes.summary: One of Alethkar’s highprinces, generally a secondary political actor in the Plains and Urithiru councils.

graphNodes.name: Thanadal
graphNodes.summary: One of the ten Alethi highprinces; mostly present through council and campaign politics.

graphNodes.name: Vamah
graphNodes.summary: An Alethi highprince who participates in the political realignment around Dalinar and the coalition.

graphNodes.name: Dukar
graphNodes.summary: An ardent associated with Kharbranth’s Soulcasters and the examination of Jasnah’s supposed fabrial.

graphNodes.name: Baxil
graphNodes.summary: Interlude thief who works for the woman later identifiable as the Herald Shalash, destroying depictions of herself.

graphNodes.name: Av
graphNodes.summary: Baxil’s cousin and partner during the interlude involving the destruction of Heraldic art.

graphNodes.name: Teft
graphNodes.summary: One of Kaladin’s earliest supporters and the source of old Radiant lore through the Envisagers. Addiction and shame isolate him in Oathbringer, but he returns to protect Bridge Four and speaks a Windrunner Ideal.

graphNodes.name: Lunamor
graphNodes.summary: Horneater member of Bridge Four, usually called Rock. Serves as cook, storyteller, emotional center, and reluctant fighter; at Thaylen Field he breaks a personal taboo to save Kaladin by killing Amaram.

graphNodes.name: Sigzil
graphNodes.summary: Azish former apprentice of Wit who becomes Bridge Four’s record keeper, experimenter, and organizational officer. His precision helps turn a survivor group into a functioning military unit.

graphNodes.name: The Lopen
graphNodes.summary: One-armed Herdazian bridgeman whose relentless humor and enormous cousin network conceal sharp resilience. Stormlight regrows his arm, and he develops Windrunner powers as a squire.

graphNodes.name: Moash
graphNodes.summary: A capable bridgeman whose grandparents died through Roshone and Elhokar’s failures. His revenge plot breaks his bond with Kaladin; among the singers he kills Elhokar, later kills Jezrien with a special dagger, and accepts the name Vyre.

graphNodes.name: Skar
graphNodes.summary: Bridge Four veteran who becomes a squire and instructor. He initially struggles to draw Stormlight, then succeeds while helping others rather than focusing on himself.

graphNodes.name: Drehy
graphNodes.summary: Bridge Four member and Windrunner squire. He and Skar survive Kholinar’s fall and carry Gavinor away from the palace.

graphNodes.name: Hobber
graphNodes.summary: Bridge Four member whose legs are severed by Szeth. Windrunner squiring and Stormlight eventually restore his ability to stand and walk.

graphNodes.name: Leyten
graphNodes.summary: Bridge Four member who takes responsibility for equipment and uniforms as the group professionalizes.

graphNodes.name: Dabbid
graphNodes.summary: Quiet Bridge Four member, long assumed unable or unwilling to speak. He remains observant and loyal, often handling practical work others miss.

graphNodes.name: Peet
graphNodes.summary: Bridge Four member and Windrunner squire who serves as a dependable guard and field operative as the unit expands beyond its original crew.

graphNodes.name: Torfin
graphNodes.summary: Named Bridge Four member who survives the bridge crews and joins the expanding Windrunner unit.

graphNodes.name: Natam
graphNodes.summary: Named Bridge Four veteran and member of the Windrunner organization at Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Huio
graphNodes.summary: Lopen’s Herdazian cousin and Bridge Four member, frequently underestimated because he speaks little Alethi.

graphNodes.name: Bisig
graphNodes.summary: Member of Bridge Four’s enlarged Windrunner unit during the Urithiru period.

graphNodes.name: Rlain
graphNodes.summary: A listener sent into the Alethi bridge crews as Shen. Bridge Four’s acceptance becomes genuine; after revealing himself as Rlain, he struggles with being the last known listener among humans and with both cultures’ assumptions.

graphNodes.name: Dunny
graphNodes.summary: Young Bridge Four member killed during a bridge run, one of the losses that hardens the crew’s determination to escape Sadeas’s system.

graphNodes.name: Maps
graphNodes.summary: Bridge Four member known for spatial memory and navigation; killed during the Battle of the Tower.

graphNodes.name: Narm
graphNodes.summary: Named Bridge Four member from the period before the crew’s rescue.

graphNodes.name: Mart
graphNodes.summary: Named bridgeman in Bridge Four during the Shattered Plains campaign.

graphNodes.name: Gaz
graphNodes.summary: The one-eyed sergeant who initially abuses Bridge Four. After deserting, he joins Shallan’s caravan, is given responsibility rather than punishment, and begins manifesting Lightweaver-squire abilities.

graphNodes.name: Matal
graphNodes.summary: Lighteyed officer overseeing bridge crews under Sadeas, with authority over Gaz and the brutal running system.

graphNodes.name: Lamaril
graphNodes.summary: Officer in Sadeas’s bridge organization who is removed during internal political maneuvering.

graphNodes.name: Hashal
graphNodes.summary: Officer assigned over the bridge crews after Lamaril, hostile to Kaladin and willing to use Bridge Four as expendable bait.

graphNodes.name: Helaran Davar
graphNodes.summary: Shallan’s eldest brother, absent from home and believed connected to the Ghostbloods before later evidence points to the Skybreakers. Kaladin kills him in battle without initially knowing his identity; Amaram steals his Shards.

graphNodes.name: Lin Davar
graphNodes.summary: Abusive patriarch of House Davar, drawn into debt and political schemes after taking blame for his wife’s death. Shallan kills him to stop his violence against the family.

graphNodes.name: Malise Gevelmar
graphNodes.summary: Shallan’s mother, who attempts to kill her young daughter after discovering Surgebinding. Shallan kills her with a living Shardblade and represses the memory.

graphNodes.name: Nan Balat Davar
graphNodes.summary: Shallan’s older brother, physically injured and psychologically scarred by the Davar household. He escapes to Urithiru with the remaining family.

graphNodes.name: Wikim Davar
graphNodes.summary: One of Shallan’s brothers, bookish and vulnerable to his father’s control; later reunited with Shallan at Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Jushu Davar
graphNodes.summary: One of Shallan’s brothers, whose gambling debts deepen the family’s financial crisis before the brothers escape to Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Eylita
graphNodes.summary: Balat’s loyal betrothed, part of the Davar household that eventually reaches Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Kabsal
graphNodes.summary: An apparently affable ardent who courts Jasnah through Shallan while secretly trying to poison her for the Ghostbloods. His own poison kills him when Jasnah substitutes Soulcast food.

graphNodes.name: Yalb
graphNodes.summary: Sociable sailor on the Wind’s Pleasure who helps Shallan navigate Kharbranth. He is missing after the ship attack within this spoiler boundary.

graphNodes.name: Tozbek
graphNodes.summary: Captain of the Wind’s Pleasure, hired by Shallan’s family and later carrying Jasnah and Shallan toward the Shattered Plains when the ship is attacked.

graphNodes.name: Tvlakv
graphNodes.summary: Slave trader who sells Kaladin to Sadeas and later transports Shallan through the Frostlands. Shallan takes control of his caravan after bandit attacks.

graphNodes.name: Bluth
graphNodes.summary: One of Tvlakv’s guards. Shallan’s idealized sketch helps him choose a better self, and he dies protecting the caravan.

graphNodes.name: Vathah
graphNodes.summary: Leader of Alethi deserters recruited by Shallan. He becomes a loyal officer and begins developing Lightweaver-squire abilities.

graphNodes.name: Red
graphNodes.summary: Red-haired member of Vathah’s deserters who joins Shallan’s household and covert operations.

graphNodes.name: Grund
graphNodes.summary: Urithiru street child recruited through Veil’s attempt to help the city’s poor; murdered during the conflict around the Midnight Mother, intensifying Shallan’s guilt.

graphNodes.name: Ishnah
graphNodes.summary: Woman with espionage experience who seeks membership in Shallan’s organization and becomes part of the growing Lightweaver network.

graphNodes.name: Tyn
graphNodes.summary: Experienced con artist who mentors Shallan in disguise while secretly ordered to recruit or kill her. Shallan kills Tyn after learning the truth.

graphNodes.name: Mraize
graphNodes.summary: Cosmopolitan Ghostblood operative who recruits Shallan through tests and controlled information. His trophy room signals extensive offworld travel and his orders focus on secrets, Radiants, and the Unmade.

graphNodes.name: Iyatil
graphNodes.summary: Masked Ghostblood operative and Mraize’s mentor. Her culture and ancestry are offworld-linked, though the novels through Oathbringer leave most details implicit.

graphNodes.name: Luesh
graphNodes.summary: House Davar steward whose death leaves behind signs of Ghostblood affiliation and a Soulcaster central to the family’s debt crisis.

graphNodes.name: Vathah's deserters
graphNodes.summary: Collective entry for Vathah’s surviving deserters when individual names are not foregrounded; they become Shallan’s guards and later Lightweaver-associated personnel.

graphNodes.name: Eshonai
graphNodes.summary: Listener explorer and war leader who sought peaceful understanding with humans. Pressured into stormform, she loses control to Odium’s influence and falls into a chasm during Narak; Oathbringer confirms her death.

graphNodes.name: Venli
graphNodes.summary: Eshonai’s ambitious sister, manipulated for years by Ulim into rediscovering forms of power. After the listeners are devastated, she serves Odium as an envoy while secretly bonding Timbre and beginning to reject the role built for her.

graphNodes.name: Timbre
graphNodes.summary: A lightspren who first sought Eshonai and later bonds Venli. She traps and suppresses the voidspren in Venli’s gemheart, allowing a secret Radiant bond to grow.

graphNodes.name: Ulim
graphNodes.summary: Voidspren smuggled to the listeners before the Everstorm. He cultivates Venli’s ambition, directs form experiments, and helps prepare Odium’s return.

graphNodes.name: Demid
graphNodes.summary: Venli’s mate and fellow scholar, later carrying a Fused soul after the Everstorm’s transformations.

graphNodes.name: Thude
graphNodes.summary: Listener officer loyal to Eshonai who helps listeners resisting stormform escape into the chasms before Narak.

graphNodes.name: Jaxlim
graphNodes.summary: Mother of Eshonai and Venli. Her decline and the sisters’ different responses form an emotional center of the listener flashbacks.

graphNodes.name: Klade
graphNodes.summary: Listener leader who hires Szeth for Gavilar’s assassination after receiving the idea through a mysterious voice; later part of the listener leadership during the war.

graphNodes.name: Abronai
graphNodes.summary: One of the listener Five and a military leader during the final Shattered Plains campaign.

graphNodes.name: Listener dissenters
graphNodes.summary: Listeners led away from stormform by Thude and others. Their exact fate remains unresolved at the end of Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Leshwi
graphNodes.summary: A high-ranking flying Fused of the shanay-im. She values capable opponents and commands singer forces around Kholinar and Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Hariel
graphNodes.summary: One of the returning Fused encountered during the new Desolation.

graphNodes.name: Sadeas soldiers under the Thrill
graphNodes.summary: Amaram’s troops, overwhelmed by Nergaoul’s Thrill and turned against the coalition during the Battle of Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Sah
graphNodes.summary: Freed singer Kaladin meets after Hearthstone. A former parshman and father who humanizes the singer side of the conflict; killed during the chaotic Kholinar palace battle.

graphNodes.name: Khen
graphNodes.summary: Member of the singer group Kaladin travels with toward Kholinar, illustrating the newly awakened people’s varied goals.

graphNodes.name: Norl
graphNodes.summary: One of the awakened singers in the group Kaladin accompanies on the road to Kholinar.

graphNodes.name: Vai
graphNodes.summary: Singer traveling with Sah’s group during Kaladin’s attempt to understand the transformed social order.

graphNodes.name: Maru
graphNodes.summary: Singer in the group Kaladin joins after Hearthstone.

graphNodes.name: Re-Shephir
graphNodes.summary: An Unmade hiding in Urithiru who imitates violence through Midnight Essence. Shallan confronts and drives her away by recognizing her imitative, almost childlike hunger to understand.

graphNodes.name: Nergaoul
graphNodes.summary: The Unmade responsible for the Thrill, the intoxicating bloodlust long normalized in Alethi warfare. Dalinar identifies it, resists it, and traps it in the King’s Drop at Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Moelach
graphNodes.summary: Unmade whose presence produces prophetic Death Rattles near death. Taravangian’s hospitals secretly murder patients to record them; Moelach later moves toward Jah Keved.

graphNodes.name: Ashertmarn
graphNodes.summary: Unmade occupying the Kholinar Oathgate platform and feeding a cult of endless indulgence that drains resistance from the city.

graphNodes.name: Sja-anat
graphNodes.summary: Unmade capable of changing or 'enlightening' spren. She communicates with Shallan and implies her interests no longer perfectly align with Odium; Glys and some Oathgate spren bear her touch.

graphNodes.name: Yelig-nar
graphNodes.summary: Unmade that grants a host access to many Surges after swallowing a gemstone, at the risk of being consumed. Aesudan fails to contain it; Amaram later becomes its host.

graphNodes.name: Ba-Ado-Mishram
graphNodes.summary: Powerful Unmade named in the gemstone archive as the leader who supplied Voidlight and forms to singers during the False Desolation before being imprisoned by the ancient Radiants.

graphNodes.name: Chemoarish
graphNodes.summary: One of the Unmade, known largely through names, folklore, and imperfect historical records at this point.

graphNodes.name: Dai-Gonarthis
graphNodes.summary: One of the Unmade, associated in fragmentary lore with consuming sorrow; little is confirmed by the end of Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Adrotagia
graphNodes.summary: Senior Diagram member and one of Taravangian’s closest planners, helping interpret the document and manage its political program.

graphNodes.name: Mrall
graphNodes.summary: Taravangian’s calm bodyguard and trusted Diagram agent, notable for unusual control over emotional state.

graphNodes.name: Graves
graphNodes.summary: Diagram operative who recruits Moash into an assassination attempt against Elhokar, arguing that Dalinar should rule. Flees after the plot fails and later dies among singer forces.

graphNodes.name: Malata
graphNodes.summary: Dustbringer bonded to Spark and secretly loyal to the Diagram. She cooperates with the coalition while sabotaging Oathgate equipment on Taravangian’s orders.

graphNodes.name: Spark
graphNodes.summary: Malata’s ashspren partner, resentful of how humans remember the Recreance and willing to support the Diagram’s destructive agenda.

graphNodes.name: Dova
graphNodes.summary: The Diagram’s scholar Dova is identified by Taravangian as the Herald Battar, one of the ancient oath-bound figures now acting outside her original role.

graphNodes.name: Noura
graphNodes.summary: Influential Azish vizier involved in selecting and advising Prime Gawx, skeptical of Lift but increasingly forced to accept Radiant realities.

graphNodes.name: Gawx
graphNodes.summary: A street thief whom Lift saves with Regrowth after Nale attacks him. Bureaucratic procedure elevates him as Prime Yanagawn, and he later joins Dalinar’s coalition.

graphNodes.name: The Stump
graphNodes.summary: Gruff orphanage keeper in Yeddaw whose apparently miraculous recoveries reveal a hidden Truthwatcher bond. Lift protects her from Nale.

graphNodes.name: Mik
graphNodes.summary: Child at the Stump’s orphanage whose condition and recovery help Lift understand the supposed miracle.

graphNodes.name: Arclo
graphNodes.summary: A Dysian Aimian composed of many cremling hordelings. He observes Lift, explains part of the Sleepless nature, and warns that hidden guardians monitor dangerous knowledge.

graphNodes.name: Nale
graphNodes.summary: Herald associated with the Skybreakers. Convinced new Radiants will cause Desolation, he uses local law to execute them; Lift forces him to confront evidence that the Desolation has already returned, after which he sides with the singers as Roshar’s original legal claimants.

graphNodes.name: Fen Rnamdi
graphNodes.summary: Pragmatic ruler of Thaylenah. Initially wary of Dalinar’s authority, she joins the coalition and defends her city through Odium’s assault.

graphNodes.name: Kmakl
graphNodes.summary: Queen Fen’s husband and political partner, involved in Thaylen coalition decisions.

graphNodes.name: Tarah
graphNodes.summary: Quartermaster in Amaram’s army and Kaladin’s past romantic partner. Flashbacks show Kaladin choosing responsibility for his squad over leaving with her.

graphNodes.name: Rushu
graphNodes.summary: Brilliant, easily distracted ardent who works with Navani on fabrials, Shardplate observations, and Urithiru systems.

graphNodes.name: Rial
graphNodes.summary: Plainspoken, often intoxicated Kholin officer whose casual manner belies competence and loyalty.

graphNodes.name: Teshav
graphNodes.summary: Navani’s senior scribe and a reliable member of the Kholin administrative network.

graphNodes.name: Jochi
graphNodes.summary: Member of the Azish bureaucracy around Gawx and Lift’s disruptive appearances.

graphNodes.name: Jezrien
graphNodes.summary: Leader of the Heralds in ancient tradition. By Oathbringer he lives as the broken beggar Ahu in Kholinar; Moash kills him with a gemstone-pommel dagger that traps or destroys his Cognitive Shadow.

graphNodes.name: Ishar
graphNodes.summary: Herald associated with Bondsmiths, now ruling Tukar as the god-priest Tezim. Nale treats his judgment as authoritative, but his sanity and motives are deeply suspect.

graphNodes.name: Shalash
graphNodes.summary: Herald who compulsively destroys images and statues of herself. She is located and brought toward Thaylen Field, where she senses Jezrien’s death.

graphNodes.name: Talenel
graphNodes.summary: The one Herald who did not abandon the Oathpact. He returns from millennia of torture on Braize, nearly catatonic but still warning humanity; a lucid moment expresses joy that humans had time to advance.

graphNodes.name: Kalak
graphNodes.summary: Prelude viewpoint Herald who witnesses Aharietiam and accepts abandonment of the Oathpact. His present-day location and role are not resolved by Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Battar
graphNodes.summary: Herald associated with Elsecallers. Taravangian identifies the Diagram scholar Dova as Battar, though details remain limited.

graphNodes.name: Pailiah
graphNodes.summary: Herald associated with Truthwatchers. A woman in the Palanaeum is suggested by authorial clues to be Pailiah, but the novels do not foreground confirmation.

graphNodes.name: Chanarach
graphNodes.summary: Herald associated with Dustbringers, known chiefly through doctrine and historical references at this spoiler boundary.

graphNodes.name: Vedel
graphNodes.summary: Herald associated with Edgedancers, known mainly through Vorin iconography and ancient order structure by Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Nightwatcher
graphNodes.summary: Powerful spren cultivated by Cultivation. Petitioners seek a boon and receive a curse, though Dalinar’s encounter is taken over directly by Cultivation.

graphNodes.name: Glys
graphNodes.summary: Renarin’s mistspren, altered by Sja-anat. Their bond grants healing and unusual future-oriented visions that make Renarin a blind spot in Odium’s predictions.

graphNodes.name: Ivory
graphNodes.summary: Jasnah’s inkspren partner, formal and wary of human unpredictability. Enables her Elsecalling and living Shardblade.

graphNodes.name: Mayalaran
graphNodes.summary: The deadeye spren of Adolin’s Shardblade. In Shadesmar she appears as a damaged cultivationspren; Adolin’s care elicits limited response, including giving her name and summoning unusually quickly.

graphNodes.name: Notum
graphNodes.summary: Honorspren captain of the ship Honor’s Path. He transports the human group in Shadesmar while debating Syl’s bond and honorspren law.

graphNodes.name: Phendorana
graphNodes.summary: Honorspren who begins associating closely with Bridge Four and Teft during the growth of the Windrunner order.

graphNodes.name: The ancient honorspren generation
graphNodes.summary: Historical generation of honorspren created before the Recreance; Syl is the only surviving member known to the modern honorspren.

graphNodes.name: Oathgate spren
graphNodes.summary: Paired large spren governing each Oathgate. Some refuse or restrict travel; the Kholinar pair are corrupted by Sja-anat and send the strike team into Shadesmar rather than Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Cusicesh
graphNodes.summary: Enormous spren appearing on a regular schedule in Kasitor Bay, seen in an Axies interlude.

graphNodes.name: Axies the Collector
graphNodes.summary: Immortal-seeming Siah Aimian who catalogs spren, can alter his body markings, and appears in interludes studying unusual manifestations.

graphNodes.name: Zahel
graphNodes.summary: Adolin and Renarin’s irritable swordmaster, secretly Vasher of Nalthis. He sustains himself with Stormlight rather than consuming a weekly Breath and uses color metaphors and Awakening-informed habits that mark his origin.

graphNodes.name: Azure
graphNodes.summary: Foreign commander leading Kholinar’s Wall Guard, secretly Vivenna of Nalthis. She carries a nonstandard sentient-looking sword, uses Awakening, seeks Zahel and Nightblood, and separates from the group in Shadesmar.

graphNodes.name: Felt
graphNodes.summary: Kholin scout who accompanied Dalinar to the Nightwatcher and whose phrasing hints he is not Rosharan. He previously appeared on Scadrial.

graphNodes.name: Demoux
graphNodes.summary: One of three foreigners searching the Purelake for Hoid; identifiable across the Cosmere as the Scadrian Demoux.

graphNodes.name: Galladon
graphNodes.summary: One of Ishikk’s three foreign visitors, recognizable as Galladon from Sel through speech patterns and appearance.

graphNodes.name: Baon
graphNodes.summary: Third member of the Purelake search party seeking Hoid, originating from Taldain.

graphNodes.name: Nazh
graphNodes.summary: Khriss’s field agent, responsible for many handwritten annotations attached to maps and documents. Often complains about the danger and inconvenience of collecting them.

graphNodes.name: Khrissalla
graphNodes.summary: Leading independent scholar of Investiture. The planetary essays in Arcanum Unbounded provide the pre-Oathbringer reader with explicit system-level context.

graphNodes.name: Vasher / Zahel continuity
graphNodes.summary: Identity bridge: Warbreaker’s Vasher is the Rosharan swordmaster Zahel. The novels signal this through idiom, life-sense behavior, Breath concepts, and his relationship to Nightblood.

graphNodes.name: Vivenna / Azure continuity
graphNodes.summary: Identity bridge: Warbreaker’s Vivenna appears in Oathbringer as Azure, older, martial, and searching for Vasher and Nightblood.

graphNodes.name: Ishikk
graphNodes.summary: Purelaker fisherman employed by three offworld visitors to watch for Hoid. His viewpoint shows Purelake religion, food, and local resistance to outsiders.

graphNodes.name: Rysn Ftori
graphNodes.summary: Thaylen merchant apprentice whose interludes explore Shinovar, the Reshi Isles, and trade culture. A fall leaves her unable to walk; she receives the larkin Chiri-Chiri and helps protect the King’s Drop during Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Vstim
graphNodes.summary: Rysn’s demanding but caring Thaylen babsk, using difficult trade missions as education in cultural perspective.

graphNodes.name: Chiri-Chiri
graphNodes.summary: Small larkin given to Rysn by the Reshi. She can drain Investiture and helps counter a Fused attack on the King’s Drop.

graphNodes.name: Relu-na
graphNodes.summary: Ruler of a Reshi greatshell island encountered by Rysn; cultural assumptions about title and gender challenge the Thaylen delegation.

graphNodes.name: Puuli
graphNodes.summary: Natan lighthouse keeper who watches the sea for prophesied sailors arriving from the Origin, illustrating local apocalyptic expectations.

graphNodes.name: Ellista
graphNodes.summary: Ardent researching the Dawnchant in Urithiru, irritated by interruptions but part of the team that reveals humanity’s migration from Ashyn.

graphNodes.name: Kaza
graphNodes.summary: Terminally transformed Soulcaster on an expedition toward Akinah. She is poisoned before reaching the island’s secrets, showing both Soulcasting’s bodily cost and the Sleepless defense of Aimia.

graphNodes.name: Sheler
graphNodes.summary: Cruel officer captured in Herdaz and offered a grim choice of punishments, in an interlude displaying Herdazian resistance.

graphNodes.name: Mem
graphNodes.summary: Young worker whose interlude around Mraize’s household exposes mundane access to Ghostblood spaces and a piece of strange cleaning magic.

graphNodes.name: Noro
graphNodes.summary: Named member of the human resistance and Wall Guard structure under Azure during the siege.

graphNodes.name: Riino
graphNodes.summary: Elantrian operating a Shadesmar lighthouse. He uses a fortune-telling device, recognizes Kaladin as Invested, and directs the travelers toward Celebrant.

graphNodes.name: Nohadon
graphNodes.summary: Ancient ruler associated with the book The Way of Kings. Dalinar meets him in visions that may be more complex than simple historical recordings; his moral legacy shapes Dalinar’s reform project.

graphNodes.name: Melishi
graphNodes.summary: Bondsmith named in the gemstone archive as central to the plan to capture Ba-Ado-Mishram near the end of the False Desolation.

graphNodes.name: Nikli
graphNodes.summary: A Sleepless swarm using a human-shaped body as Rysn’s porter. Nikli accompanies the expedition under false pretenses, then reveals that the Sleepless engineered the mission’s dangers to protect Akinah and its Dawnshard.

graphNodes.name: Cord
graphNodes.summary: Rock’s daughter. She accompanies Rysn’s Aimia expedition, can perceive spren unusually well, helps Rysn survive the Sleepless confrontation, and returns from Akinah with ancient Shardplate.

graphNodes.name: Rua
graphNodes.summary: Lopen’s honorspren. Their bond matures during the Akinah expedition, and Rua can become a living Shardweapon after Lopen’s Third Ideal.

graphNodes.name: Caelinora
graphNodes.summary: Huio’s honorspren. When Huio swears the Third Ideal to protect Lopen, Caelinora can manifest as a living Shardweapon.

graphNodes.name: Ral-na
graphNodes.summary: A Reshi ruler who arrives at Urithiru after bonding an ashspren and becoming a Dustbringer, illustrating how rapidly Radiant bonds are spreading beyond the Alethi center.

graphNodes.name: Talik
graphNodes.summary: Reshi envoy familiar with larkin. He identifies Chiri-Chiri’s illness as a reason to seek Akinah, helping launch Rysn’s expedition.

graphNodes.name: Raboniel
graphNodes.summary: A brilliant ancient Fused scholar who leads the occupation of Urithiru. Rather than treating Navani only as a prisoner, she becomes her scientific counterpart; together they discover Warlight and the principles that lead to anti-Light. Raboniel’s deeper aim is an irreversible end to the cycle of war.

graphNodes.name: The Sibling
graphNodes.summary: The great spren of Urithiru, associated with both Honor and Cultivation. The Sibling powers the tower’s integrated fabrial systems, resists Raboniel’s corruption, communicates secretly with Kaladin and Navani, and eventually bonds Navani.

graphNodes.name: Lezian
graphNodes.summary: A Fused who makes a tradition of killing anyone who kills him, becoming obsessed with Kaladin. His teleport-like Transportation lets him shed bodies and reappear nearby. Kaladin finally breaks his legend during the liberation of Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Design
graphNodes.summary: The Cryptic Wit rescued in occupied Kholinar at the end of Oathbringer, now named Design. She is irreverent, perceptive, and fully established as Wit’s bonded spren by Rhythm of War.

graphNodes.name: Testament
graphNodes.summary: The Cryptic Shallan bonded as a child before Pattern. Shallan broke her oaths after killing her mother, leaving Testament as a deadeye; acknowledging this buried bond becomes one of her central Rhythm of War revelations.

graphNodes.name: Tumi
graphNodes.summary: An enlightened mistspren sent through Sja-anat’s network. Tumi chooses Rlain, making him a Truthwatcher with a corrupted/enlightened spren bond.

graphNodes.name: Blended
graphNodes.summary: An inkspren who tutors Adolin in honorspren legal procedure and watches Maya’s changing condition closely. She becomes an important neutral observer of the trial’s implications.

graphNodes.name: Sekeir
graphNodes.summary: A senior honorspren and hardline opponent of renewed human bonds. He tries to use Maya as evidence against Adolin, only for Maya’s testimony to overturn his framing of the Recreance.

graphNodes.name: El
graphNodes.summary: An ancient Fused stripped of title and rhythms who studies humanity with unusual interest. In the closing chapters he receives Navani and Raboniel’s research and demonstrates anti-Stormlight by permanently killing Lezian.

graphNodes.name: Axindweth
graphNodes.summary: A mysterious offworld woman in Venli’s flashbacks who provides the gemstone containing Ulim and helps create the conditions for Odium’s influence among the listeners.

graphNodes.name: Noril
graphNodes.summary: A man suffering severe battle shock and depression whom Kaladin helps through structured peer support. His response helps Kaladin recognize a non-combat path for protecting people.

graphNodes.name: Godeke
graphNodes.summary: An Edgedancer chosen for Adolin and Shallan’s diplomatic mission to the honorspren stronghold in Shadesmar.

graphNodes.name: Zu
graphNodes.summary: A Stoneward Radiant who accompanies the honorspren diplomatic mission through Shadesmar.

graphNodes.name: Beryl
graphNodes.summary: A Lightweaver in Shallan’s circle who becomes one of the suspected Ghostblood infiltrators during the Lasting Integrity mission.

graphNodes.name: Dieno
graphNodes.summary: The celebrated Herdazian general known as the Mink. After escaping occupation, he becomes a key coalition strategist and redirects the main military effort toward Emul.

graphNodes.name: House Kholin
graphNodes.summary: Royal Alethi house founded politically by Gavilar’s unification and led militarily by Dalinar after the assassination. Its internal tensions drive much of the first three books.

graphNodes.name: Bridge Four
graphNodes.summary: Former Sadeas bridge crew transformed by Kaladin into a mutually protective unit, then Dalinar’s guard and the core of the restored Windrunners.

graphNodes.name: Order of Windrunners
graphNodes.summary: Radiants bonded to honorspren, using Adhesion and Gravitation. Their Ideals center on protection and its moral limits.

graphNodes.name: Order of Lightweavers
graphNodes.summary: Radiants bonded to Cryptics, using Illumination and Transformation. Progress is expressed through personal truths rather than a uniform sequence of spoken Ideals.

graphNodes.name: Order of Bondsmiths
graphNodes.summary: Rare order bonded to vast spren, using Adhesion and Tension with unusual powers over Connection and unification.

graphNodes.name: Order of Elsecallers
graphNodes.summary: Radiants bonded to inkspren, using Transformation and Transportation. Jasnah is the only confirmed active member in this scope.

graphNodes.name: Order of Truthwatchers
graphNodes.summary: Radiants associated with mistspren, Progression, and Illumination. Renarin and the Stump manifest different-looking examples.

graphNodes.name: Order of Edgedancers
graphNodes.summary: Cultivationspren Radiants using Abrasion and Progression. Their oaths emphasize remembering, listening to, and protecting overlooked people.

graphNodes.name: Order of Skybreakers
graphNodes.summary: Highspren Radiants led in practice by Nale, using Gravitation and Division. They pursue external legal codes but are distorted by their Herald’s damaged judgment.

graphNodes.name: Order of Dustbringers
graphNodes.summary: Also called Releasers; bonded to ashspren and using Division and Abrasion. Malata is the only active example foregrounded by Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Order of Willshapers
graphNodes.summary: Lightspren Radiants associated with Transportation and Cohesion and a drive toward freedom. Venli’s bond with Timbre is only beginning at the cutoff.

graphNodes.name: Order of Stonewards
graphNodes.summary: Order associated with Cohesion and Tension, ancient patron Taln, reliability, endurance, and battlefield resolve.

graphNodes.name: Ghostbloods
graphNodes.summary: Cross-world organization pursuing information, leverage, and control of Investiture-related opportunities. On Roshar, Mraize and Iyatil recruit Shallan while concealing the group’s full hierarchy.

graphNodes.name: The Diagram
graphNodes.summary: Taravangian’s organization built around predictions dictated on his day of extraordinary intelligence. It treats controlled catastrophe as the path to saving a remnant.

graphNodes.name: Sons of Honor
graphNodes.summary: Organization seeking the return of the Heralds and Vorin dominance by provoking a Desolation. Gavilar and Amaram are central Rosharan leaders.

graphNodes.name: Listeners
graphNodes.summary: Singer-descended people who rejected their gods and forms of power, preserving themselves on the Shattered Plains. Alethi call them Parshendi. Their attempt to escape genocide through stormform enables the Everstorm and nearly destroys them.

graphNodes.name: Singers
graphNodes.summary: The awakened people humans had enslaved as parshmen. The Everstorm restores minds and forms, but freedom quickly becomes entangled with Fused rule and Odium’s war.

graphNodes.name: The Fused
graphNodes.summary: Ancient singer souls repeatedly reborn into living singer bodies through the Everstorm. They serve Odium, retain specialized Surges, and vary in sanity and honor.

graphNodes.name: The Unmade
graphNodes.summary: Nine ancient spren altered by Odium. Each manifests a different influence; several act semi-independently and are central to Oathbringer’s investigations.

graphNodes.name: Odium’s forces
graphNodes.summary: Umbrella for Odium, Fused, Regals, loyal voidspren, Unmade, and human collaborators during the True Desolation.

graphNodes.name: Coalition of Monarchs
graphNodes.summary: Dalinar’s Oathgate-linked alliance among Urithiru, Alethkar’s loyalists, Thaylenah, Azir, Kharbranth/Jah Keved, and other states—compromised by hidden agendas.

graphNodes.name: Alethi highprinces
graphNodes.summary: Ten princedoms whose competition, gemheart economy, and warcamps dominate the Shattered Plains. Dalinar’s reforms challenge their incentives.

graphNodes.name: Sadeas principality
graphNodes.summary: Military-political bloc built around Torol and Ialai Sadeas; after Torol’s death, Amaram takes military command and the army eventually falls to the Thrill.

graphNodes.name: Vorin Ardentia
graphNodes.summary: Nominally enslaved priestly order handling scholarship, engineering, monasteries, and doctrine. Individual ardents range from sincere caregivers to political actors.

graphNodes.name: The Heralds
graphNodes.summary: Ten Cognitive Shadows who carried Honorblades and upheld the Oathpact. Nine abandoned Taln at Aharietiam; millennia of strain have left all encountered Heralds psychologically damaged.

graphNodes.name: Honorspren
graphNodes.summary: Sapient spren associated with Honor and Windrunners. Modern honorspren distrust humans because of the Recreance; Syl’s bond is politically contentious.

graphNodes.name: Cryptics
graphNodes.summary: Pattern-like sapient spren attracted to complex truths and lies, serving as Lightweaver bond partners.

graphNodes.name: Cultivationspren
graphNodes.summary: Vine-like sapient spren that bond Edgedancers. Wyndle’s circle selected Lift under unusual Cultivation-linked circumstances.

graphNodes.name: Inkspren
graphNodes.summary: Orderly sapient spren associated with Elsecallers; Ivory’s bond with Jasnah is exceptional and closely guarded.

graphNodes.name: The Sleepless
graphNodes.summary: Dysian Aimians composed of hordelings. They protect Aimia and dangerous secrets, observing Radiants through ordinary-looking cremlings.

graphNodes.name: Thaylenah
graphNodes.summary: Maritime trading kingdom centered on Thaylen City, ruled by Queen Fen and connected to Urithiru by Oathgate.

graphNodes.name: Azir
graphNodes.summary: Bureaucratic imperial center where written process and viziers constrain the Prime. Gawx’s unlikely accession links Lift to high politics.

graphNodes.name: Kharbranth
graphNodes.summary: Hospital and scholarly city ruled by Taravangian, home to the Palanaeum and the hidden Death Rattle project.

graphNodes.name: Kholinar resistance
graphNodes.summary: Wall Guard, palace loyalists, and civilians resisting singer occupation and Unmade influence under Azure and the infiltrating Kholin team.

graphNodes.name: Worldhoppers
graphNodes.summary: Individuals able to travel between worlds, usually through the Cognitive Realm. Not a single aligned faction.

graphNodes.name: Seventeenth Shard
graphNodes.summary: Noninterventionist-leaning travelers searching for Hoid on Roshar, represented in TWoK by three Purelake visitors.

graphNodes.name: Nalthian connection
graphNodes.summary: Characters and magic originating in Warbreaker’s world of Nalthis who appear under new roles on Roshar.

graphNodes.name: Aimia / Aimian peoples
graphNodes.summary: Umbrella for Siah and Dysian Aimians and the ruined island nation.

graphNodes.name: Alethkar
graphNodes.summary: Alethi kingdom and its civil institutions outside a particular house.

graphNodes.name: Amaram’s army
graphNodes.summary: Army in which Kaladin served before Amaram’s betrayal.

graphNodes.name: Shalash’s hired agents
graphNodes.summary: Temporary thieves and helpers hired around Shalash’s destruction of art.

graphNodes.name: Cultivation-aligned powers
graphNodes.summary: Cultivation, the Nightwatcher, and interventions serving long-term growth.

graphNodes.name: Graves’s Diagram cell
graphNodes.summary: Diagram faction that recruits Moash for Elhokar’s assassination.

graphNodes.name: Hearthstone community
graphNodes.summary: Human and singer residents around Kaladin’s home town.

graphNodes.name: Herdaz
graphNodes.summary: Herdazian people and resistance networks.

graphNodes.name: Honor-aligned legacy
graphNodes.summary: Honor’s surviving systems: oaths, spren, Stormfather, Honorblades, and Radiants.

graphNodes.name: House Davar
graphNodes.summary: Shallan’s indebted and traumatized family, entangled with Ghostbloods.

graphNodes.name: Independent actors
graphNodes.summary: Entities whose goals do not fit one durable political alignment.

graphNodes.name: Natanatan legacy
graphNodes.summary: Ruined eastern civilization around Stormseat and the Shattered Plains.

graphNodes.name: Navani’s artifabrians
graphNodes.summary: Engineers and ardents supporting Kholin fabrial research.

graphNodes.name: Oathgate network
graphNodes.summary: Spren, platforms, and operators controlling Urithiru’s transport network.

graphNodes.name: Purelake communities
graphNodes.summary: Independent lake settlements and fishing culture.

graphNodes.name: Reshi peoples
graphNodes.summary: Communities living on and around greatshell islands.

graphNodes.name: Rysn’s household
graphNodes.summary: Rysn and companions including Chiri-Chiri.

graphNodes.name: Sadeas’s army
graphNodes.summary: Forces organized around expendable bridge tactics and later inherited by Amaram.

graphNodes.name: Scadrian connection
graphNodes.summary: People and systems originating on Scadrial.

graphNodes.name: Sebarial principality
graphNodes.summary: Sebarial and Palona’s commercially focused princedom.

graphNodes.name: Selish connection
graphNodes.summary: People and systems originating on Sel.

graphNodes.name: Veil’s Urithiru network
graphNodes.summary: Street contacts and helpers recruited by Shallan/Veil.

graphNodes.name: Shallan’s retinue
graphNodes.summary: Caravan survivors, deserters, and guards who become Shallan’s personnel.

graphNodes.name: Silverlight scholars
graphNodes.summary: Khriss, Nazh, and related Cosmere researchers.

graphNodes.name: Skybreaker informants
graphNodes.summary: Agents and contacts used to identify and prosecute emerging Surgebinders.

graphNodes.name: Spren
graphNodes.summary: General category for Roshar’s Cognitive entities.

graphNodes.name: The Stump’s orphanage
graphNodes.summary: Children and caretakers protected during Edgedancer.

graphNodes.name: Taldain connection
graphNodes.summary: People and Investiture from Taldain.

graphNodes.name: Tukar
graphNodes.summary: State ruled by Ishar under the identity Tezim.

graphNodes.name: Tvlakv’s caravan
graphNodes.summary: Slave and trade caravan later taken over by Shallan.

graphNodes.name: Vstim’s merchant caravan
graphNodes.summary: Thaylen trading operation that trains Rysn.

graphNodes.name: Wind’s Pleasure crew
graphNodes.summary: Tozbek’s sailors carrying Shallan and Jasnah.

graphNodes.name: Ancient Knights Radiant
graphNodes.summary: Radiants active before the Recreance.

graphNodes.name: Knights Radiant
graphNodes.summary: All ten Nahel-bonded orders collectively.

graphNodes.name: Shin Stone Shamans
graphNodes.summary: Shin institution that holds most Honorblades and enforces Truthless judgment.

graphNodes.name: Alethi armies
graphNodes.summary: Armies of Alethkar’s highprinces.

graphNodes.name: Alethi soldiers
graphNodes.summary: Soldiers and guards in Alethi forces.

graphNodes.name: Shardbearers
graphNodes.summary: People bonded to dead Shardblades and/or Shardplate.

graphNodes.name: Szeth’s successive masters
graphNodes.summary: People who possess Szeth’s Oathstone before the Diagram.

graphNodes.name: Jah Keved armies
graphNodes.summary: Veden military forces and elite Half-shard units.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru scholars
graphNodes.summary: Scribes and ardents translating the Dawnchant and gemstone archive.

graphNodes.name: Coalition logistics
graphNodes.summary: Operational staff of Dalinar’s coalition.

graphNodes.name: Wandersail Expedition
graphNodes.summary: Rysn’s sea expedition to Akinah, combining Thaylen sailors, scholars, Horneater support, and Windrunners under a deliberately negotiated charter.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru Occupation Force
graphNodes.summary: Raboniel’s Fused/singer strike force that inverts the tower defenses, suppresses most Radiants, and occupies Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru Resistance
graphNodes.summary: Loose network inside occupied Urithiru centered on Kaladin, Dabbid, Rlain, Teft, Navani’s hidden communications, civilians, and later sympathetic singers.

graphNodes.name: Lasting Integrity Envoy
graphNodes.summary: Coalition mission led by Adolin and Shallan to persuade honorspren to bond new Windrunners, while Shallan secretly pursues Ghostblood objectives.

graphNodes.name: Surviving Listeners
graphNodes.summary: Listeners who escaped the Everstorm transformation and survived apart from Odium’s singer state. Their continued existence becomes Venli’s alternative to both human rule and Fused domination.

graphNodes.name: Unseen Court
graphNodes.summary: Shallan's Lightweaver organization, used for intelligence work and counterespionage while its members also confront Ghostblood infiltration.

graphNodes.name: Horneaters
graphNodes.summary: People of the Horneater Peaks, including Cord and Rock; their culture and access to Cultivation's Perpendicularity give them unusual Cosmere relevance.

graphNodes.name: Reshi Isles communities
graphNodes.summary: Communities living on the greatshell islands of the Reshi Sea, represented in the Dawnshard expedition by Ral-na and Talik.

graphNodes.name: Sja-anat’s enlightened spren
graphNodes.summary: Spren changed by Sja-anat rather than simply destroyed, increasingly acting with independent agendas during Rhythm of War.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru civilians
graphNodes.summary: Noncombatants and workers living in Urithiru whose experience becomes central during the occupation and Kaladin’s resistance.

graphNodes.name: Kaladin’s Mental-Health Clinic / Support Groups
graphNodes.summary: Kaladin’s non-military Urithiru work combines surgery with structured group support for people suffering battle shock, depression, and institutional neglect.

graphNodes.name: Roshar
graphNodes.summary: Storm-battered world and supercontinent shaped around east-to-west highstorms, spren ecology, gemstone economics, and the conflict among Honor, Cultivation, and Odium.

graphNodes.name: Alethkar
graphNodes.summary: Militarized Vorin kingdom unified by Gavilar. Its capital Kholinar falls to singer forces during Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Kholinar
graphNodes.summary: Alethkar’s capital, built around windblades and an Oathgate. In Oathbringer it is divided between singer occupation, the Wall Guard, palace loyalists, and Unmade influence.

graphNodes.name: Hearthstone
graphNodes.summary: Kaladin’s home town, governed by Roshone before the Desolation and occupied by newly awakened singers when Kaladin returns.

graphNodes.name: Shattered Plains
graphNodes.summary: Maze of plateaus and chasms around the ruins of Stormseat, site of the Alethi-listener war, gemheart hunts, bridge crews, and the Battle of Narak.

graphNodes.name: Alethi warcamps
graphNodes.summary: Ten highprince camps functioning as rival cities, linked to plateau assaults and political competition.

graphNodes.name: The Tower
graphNodes.summary: Large plateau where Sadeas abandons Dalinar’s army. Bridge Four returns to save the Kholins, transforming the political alliance.

graphNodes.name: Narak / Stormseat
graphNodes.summary: Listener center among ancient ruins and the location of an Oathgate. The Battle of Narak summons the Everstorm and sends the human army to Urithiru.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru
graphNodes.summary: Ancient Knights Radiant city, physically high in the mountains and connected by ten Oathgates. Becomes the coalition capital, though much of its machinery is dormant.

graphNodes.name: Jah Keved
graphNodes.summary: Veden kingdom and Shallan’s homeland. Civil war and Szeth’s assassinations allow Taravangian to take its crown.

graphNodes.name: Vedenar
graphNodes.summary: Capital of Jah Keved, devastated by succession violence and influenced by the Thrill during the kingdom’s collapse.

graphNodes.name: Davar estate
graphNodes.summary: Shallan’s childhood home and the setting of the Davar family flashbacks, hidden Shardblade trauma, abuse, and Ghostblood debt.

graphNodes.name: Kharbranth
graphNodes.summary: Vertical city of bells, hospitals, the Palanaeum, and Taravangian’s court. Shallan studies here under Jasnah.

graphNodes.name: The Palanaeum
graphNodes.summary: Vast underground library administered through fees and ardents; central to Jasnah and Shallan’s research into the Voidbringers.

graphNodes.name: Diagram hospitals
graphNodes.summary: Publicly charitable hospitals that secretly include rooms where terminal patients are killed to record Death Rattles.

graphNodes.name: Thaylenah
graphNodes.summary: Maritime merchant nation controlling major trade routes and an Oathgate.

graphNodes.name: Thaylen City
graphNodes.summary: Walled port city with a gemstone reserve and Oathgate. Site of Oathbringer’s climactic battle and Dalinar’s confrontation with Odium.

graphNodes.name: Purelake
graphNodes.summary: Warm, shallow lake culture where Ishikk meets three worldhoppers searching for Hoid.

graphNodes.name: Shinovar
graphNodes.summary: Sheltered western land with soil, ordinary plants, and cultural reverence for stone. Szeth’s homeland and a major Rysn trading destination.

graphNodes.name: Azir
graphNodes.summary: Bureaucratic imperial center of the Makabaki region, governed by a Prime selected through legal procedure.

graphNodes.name: Azimir
graphNodes.summary: Capital where Lift infiltrates a palace, saves Gawx, and inadvertently helps him become Prime.

graphNodes.name: Yeddaw
graphNodes.summary: Canal city cut into the ground, setting of Edgedancer. Lift investigates stolen food, the Stump’s orphanage, and Nale’s killings.

graphNodes.name: Tashikk
graphNodes.summary: Makabaki nation containing Yeddaw, culturally linked to trade, bureaucracy, and information networks.

graphNodes.name: Herdaz
graphNodes.summary: Herdazian homeland northwest of Alethkar, known for resistance fighters and Lopen’s vast extended family.

graphNodes.name: Horneater Peaks
graphNodes.summary: Volcanic mountain lakes and perpendicularity-associated region, homeland of Rock and a known route between realms.

graphNodes.name: Iri
graphNodes.summary: Western kingdom with distinct religion and culture; Axies is arrested here, and Iri’s rulers align with Odium by Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Rira
graphNodes.summary: Small western nation culturally related to Iri and Evi’s homeland.

graphNodes.name: Reshi Isles
graphNodes.summary: Living greatshell islands with distinctive rulers and customs. Rysn is injured here and receives Chiri-Chiri.

graphNodes.name: Rall Elorim
graphNodes.summary: Lift’s home city, called the City of Shadows. It is mostly background at this spoiler boundary.

graphNodes.name: Aimia
graphNodes.summary: Destroyed island nation guarded by the Sleepless, associated with both Siah and Dysian Aimians and dangerous hidden knowledge.

graphNodes.name: Akinah
graphNodes.summary: Ancient Aimian city hidden behind dangerous weather and Sleepless defenses. Its apparent Oathgate is a decoy; caverns below contain Shardplate, Soulcasters, and the mural housing the Dawnshard that bonds Rysn.

graphNodes.name: Tukar
graphNodes.summary: Kingdom ruled by Ishar as Tezim. Dalinar’s party confronts Ishar here and discovers evidence of his experiments forcing spren into Physical bodies.

graphNodes.name: Emul
graphNodes.summary: Primary coalition military front during much of Rhythm of War, where Dalinar, Jasnah, the Mink, and Azish forces fight while Urithiru is left comparatively exposed.

graphNodes.name: Marat
graphNodes.summary: Region used by Odium’s forces as a staging area where Venli serves the Fused before Thaylen Field.

graphNodes.name: Babatharnam
graphNodes.summary: Makabaki-area nation known through interludes and trade; peripheral to the main first-three-book plot.

graphNodes.name: Tu Bayla
graphNodes.summary: Central Rosharan nation referenced in geopolitics and travel.

graphNodes.name: Natanatan
graphNodes.summary: Ancient kingdom whose lands include the Shattered Plains and Stormseat ruins.

graphNodes.name: New Natanan / Origin coast
graphNodes.summary: Eastern coast facing the mythical Origin of storms; Puuli keeps a lighthouse here.

graphNodes.name: Frostlands
graphNodes.summary: Harsh territory crossed by Shallan’s caravan en route to the Shattered Plains.

graphNodes.name: Valley of the Nightwatcher
graphNodes.summary: Remote valley where petitioners seek the Nightwatcher. Dalinar instead meets Cultivation, who removes and later restores selected memories.

graphNodes.name: Rathalas / the Rift
graphNodes.summary: Rebellious city destroyed by Dalinar during Alethkar’s unification. Evi dies in the fire, the central suppressed event of Oathbringer’s flashbacks.

graphNodes.name: Feverstone Keep
graphNodes.summary: Location in Dalinar’s vision where ancient Radiants abandon Shards during the Recreance. Its exact modern position is not established in the books.

graphNodes.name: Stormseat
graphNodes.summary: Ancient city whose shattered remains are Narak and the central Plains ruins; linked to an Oathgate and Radiant history.

graphNodes.name: Celebrant
graphNodes.summary: Major Cognitive Realm market city visited by the stranded Kholinar team while seeking passage toward Thaylen City.

graphNodes.name: Riino’s lighthouse
graphNodes.summary: Cognitive Realm lighthouse where the travelers meet Riino and use a fortune-reading device.

graphNodes.name: Sea of Souls
graphNodes.summary: Shadesmar’s dark bead ocean, where beads represent Physical objects and solid land corresponds broadly to Physical water.

graphNodes.name: Honor’s Path
graphNodes.summary: Notum’s ship carrying Kaladin, Shallan, Adolin, Azure, Pattern, and Syl toward Celebrant.

graphNodes.name: Shadesmar
graphNodes.summary: Roshar’s Cognitive Realm: obsidian-like land, bead oceans, spren cities, and routes used by Elsecallers and worldhoppers.

graphNodes.name: Braize
graphNodes.summary: Planet called Damnation in Rosharan religion, where Heralds and Fused were bound between Desolations.

graphNodes.name: Ashyn
graphNodes.summary: Humans’ original Rosharan-system world, later remembered as the Tranquiline Halls. Oathbringer’s Dawnchant translation reveals humanity arrived on Roshar as refugees after destroying Ashyn through uncontrolled powers.

graphNodes.name: Nalthis
graphNodes.summary: World of Warbreaker, Breath, Awakening, Returned, Vasher/Zahel, Vivenna/Azure, and Nightblood.

graphNodes.name: Scadrial
graphNodes.summary: World of Mistborn and metal-based magic; origin of Felt and Demoux.

graphNodes.name: Sel
graphNodes.summary: World of Elantris and The Emperor’s Soul; origin of Galladon and Riino.

graphNodes.name: Taldain
graphNodes.summary: World/system of White Sand; origin of Baon and the invested sand used as a detector in Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Silverlight
graphNodes.summary: Scholarly worldhopper center associated with Khriss and Nazh; background knowledge available through Arcanum Unbounded rather than a Stormlight plot location.

graphNodes.name: Threnody
graphNodes.summary: Setting of Shadows for Silence; included for chronological Cosmere context, not a direct Oathbringer dependency.

graphNodes.name: First of the Sun
graphNodes.summary: Setting of Sixth of the Dusk; included as pre-Oathbringer Cosmere context.

graphNodes.name: Kholinar palace
graphNodes.summary: Royal palace corrupted by Yelig-nar and the setting of Elhokar’s death during the failed Oathgate operation.

graphNodes.name: Heart of the Revel
graphNodes.summary: Ashertmarn’s zone of compulsive indulgence surrounding the city’s Oathgate platform.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru lower markets
graphNodes.summary: Refugee and working districts where Veil builds informant networks and where Re-Shephir’s murders emerge.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru gemstone archive
graphNodes.summary: Hidden gemstone records left by ancient Radiants, containing firsthand concerns about the orders, the False Desolation, and the Recreance.

graphNodes.name: Sea of Storms
graphNodes.summary: Storm-lashed southern ocean crossed by the Wind’s Pleasure and other trade vessels.

graphNodes.name: Kasitor Bay
graphNodes.summary: Iri location where Cusicesh manifests on a regular schedule and Axies attempts to study it.

graphNodes.name: The Cosmere
graphNodes.summary: Shared setting containing Roshar, Nalthis, Scadrial, Sel, Taldain, and other worlds.

graphNodes.name: Lasting Integrity
graphNodes.summary: Honorspren stronghold in Shadesmar, isolationist after the Recreance. Adolin’s diplomatic mission and trial take place here, with Kalak serving as High Judge.

graphNodes.name: Urithiru Crystal Pillar
graphNodes.summary: Gemstone/fabrial heart of Urithiru and physical locus of the Sibling’s systems. Raboniel corrupts it with Voidlight; Navani later restores the Sibling through a Bondsmith bond and Towerlight.

graphNodes.name: Nameless
graphNodes.summary: A Shadesmar settlement used as a waypoint by Adolin, Shallan, and the envoy en route to Lasting Integrity.

graphNodes.name: Investiture
graphNodes.summary: The common substrate of Cosmere magic: spiritual power expressed differently by world, Shard, intent, and access method.

graphNodes.name: Three Realms
graphNodes.summary: Reality has Physical, Cognitive, and Spiritual aspects. Shadesmar is Roshar’s Cognitive Realm; bonds, Identity, Connection, and Shardic power involve Spiritual structure.

graphNodes.name: Stormlight
graphNodes.summary: Investiture carried by highstorms and stored in cut gemstones. Radiants inhale it for healing, physical enhancement, and Surgebinding; it leaks from imperfect containers.

graphNodes.name: Voidlight
graphNodes.summary: Odium-aligned Investiture used by the Fused, Regals, and some voidspren-linked systems. It has a different feel and visual signature from Stormlight.

graphNodes.name: Highstorm recharge
graphNodes.summary: East-to-west storms recharge exposed gemstones with Stormlight. The Stormfather is the storm’s great spren and the cycle underpins Roshar’s economy and ecology.

graphNodes.name: Everstorm
graphNodes.summary: Storm moving west-to-east, summoned at Narak. It restores singer minds, supplies transformations, and permits Fused returns without waiting for the old Desolation cycle.

graphNodes.name: Nahel bond
graphNodes.summary: A mutual bond between sapient spren and human or singer that grants Surges, Shardblade access, and increasing integration as truths or Ideals progress.

graphNodes.name: Radiant Ideals and truths
graphNodes.summary: Spiritual commitments that structure Radiant growth. Most orders speak ordered Ideals; Lightweavers advance through difficult personal truths.

graphNodes.name: Adhesion
graphNodes.summary: Surge of pressure and binding, used by Windrunners for Full Lashings and by Bondsmiths in deeper forms involving Connection.

graphNodes.name: Gravitation
graphNodes.summary: Changes the direction and strength of apparent gravity. Windrunners and Skybreakers use it for Basic and Reverse Lashings, flight, and projectile control.

graphNodes.name: Division
graphNodes.summary: Breaks, burns, or degrades matter. Associated with Skybreakers and Dustbringers; used sparingly or indirectly in the books through Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Abrasion
graphNodes.summary: Controls friction. Edgedancers use it to become nearly frictionless; Dustbringers share the Surge with different order emphasis.

graphNodes.name: Progression
graphNodes.summary: Manipulates biological growth and healing. Regrowth can restore recent injuries within spiritual constraints; Edgedancers and Truthwatchers use it.

graphNodes.name: Illumination
graphNodes.summary: Manipulates light, sound, and waveform-like information. Lightweavers create complex illusions; Truthwatcher expression is less clearly understood by Oathbringer.

graphNodes.name: Transformation
graphNodes.summary: Soulcasting: persuading or forcing matter’s Cognitive aspect to become another substance. Shared by Lightweavers and Elsecallers.

graphNodes.name: Transportation
graphNodes.summary: Movement between Physical and Cognitive Realms. Elsecallers use it directly; Willshapers share the Surge, though Venli is only beginning her bond.

graphNodes.name: Cohesion
graphNodes.summary: Manipulates the strong axial connections within solid matter, associated with Willshapers and Stonewards. Mostly historical or theoretical in this cutoff.

graphNodes.name: Tension
graphNodes.summary: Manipulates the stiffness of materials, associated with Stonewards and Bondsmiths. Dalinar’s bond hints at applications, but the system remains incompletely demonstrated.

graphNodes.name: Lashings
graphNodes.summary: Rosharan terminology for Gravitation and Adhesion techniques: Basic Lashings redirect gravity; Full Lashings bind surfaces; Reverse Lashings draw nearby objects.

graphNodes.name: Lightweaving
graphNodes.summary: Illusions woven from light and sound, often anchored to drawings, memories, or a chosen identity. Shallan can combine images and later coordinate many illusions at once.

graphNodes.name: Soulcasting
graphNodes.summary: Transformation of material into another Essence. Jasnah performs it directly; Shallan learns; ancient Soulcaster fabrials allow non-Radiants to specialize at severe long-term bodily cost.

graphNodes.name: Elsecalling
